title: Your first solve
heading: Your first solve
text: Your first solve Documentation index · CLI reference · Python API Build the CLI, solve a small instance, and choose the result your applicationneeds. Run every command below from the repository root. The example inputsare included in the checkout.

title: Your first solve
heading: Build the CLI
text:
Build the CLI Install Rust/Cargo, Git, and a C++14 compiler, then clone with submodules: git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/lseman/baldes.git
cd baldes
cargo build --release --features clp
./target/release/baldes --help
 The clp feature supplies the routing master and CLI. A defaultcargo build --release builds the core library. For optional backends andMake configuration, see Build and installation.

title: Your first solve
heading: Choose a solve mode
text: Choose a solve mode Goal Mode What to expect Get a feasible routing plan hgs A heuristic solution; no optimality proof Inspect the root LP relaxation solve Route columns, potentially fractional, and lower-bound information Search for an integer routing solution solve --tree An incumbent when found, a bound, and a remaining optimality gap Start with a small instance or customer subset. A time limit can stop a runbefore convergence; it does not promise an optimal solution.

title: Your first solve
heading: Find a feasible solution
text:
Find a feasible solution Run Hybrid Genetic Search on the bundled 32-node CVRP instance: ./target/release/baldes hgs instances/cvrplib/A-n32-k5.vrp --time 10
 Use this mode when you need routes quickly. HGS searches for a feasibleinteger routing plan; its objective does not prove a lower bound or optimality.

title: Your first solve
heading: Solve a root relaxation
text:
Solve a root relaxation Keep ten customers from a Solomon instance with time windows: ./target/release/baldes solve instances/Solomon/R101.txt \
  --customers 10 --time 60 --verbose --json root-result.json
 The progress table goes to stderr; root-result.json stores the result forinspection. Look at the solve status, LP objective, selected bound, and routevalues. Root route values may be fractional, so these columns are notnecessarily a dispatchable routing plan. A root status of Optimal means the LP relaxation converged. It does notestablish an optimal integer solution. The default bound mode is numerical;independent bound validation is available with --bound-mode certified.An unknown selected bound is null in JSON. See theCLI guide for the bound fields and validation behavior.

title: Your first solve
heading: Search for an integer solution
text:
Search for an integer solution Add --tree to explore the branch-and-price tree: ./target/release/baldes solve instances/Solomon/R101.txt \
  --customers 10 --tree --time 60 --verbose
 An incumbent is a feasible integer solution. The lower bound and incumbentdefine the remaining gap. Tree Optimal means that gap closed within theconfigured tolerances. If the run reaches a limit, inspect its status and gapbefore treating the incumbent as optimal. See the tree guidefor node limits, branching, and inherited state.

title: Your first solve
heading: Keep distance conventions consistent
text: Keep distance conventions consistent Routing commands default to --rounding tenth, truncating distances to tenths.Use --rounding nearest for TSPLIB nearest-integer distances, or--rounding none for unrounded Euclidean distances. Explicit distance matricesretain their supplied weights. When comparing an objective with a published result, match the distanceconvention and customer count first. BALDES root benchmarks use--rounding none; see the benchmark setup.

title: Your first solve
heading: Common setup fixes
text: Common setup fixes Symptom Next step Clp or CoinUtils sources are missing Run git submodule update --init vendor/Clp vendor/CoinUtils, then rebuild with --features clp. target/release/baldes is missing Run the CLI build above from the repository root. An instance cannot be opened Run from the repository root and use instances/Solomon/R101.txt or an absolute path. A root result contains fractional routes Use HGS for a heuristic integer plan or solve --tree for integer search.

title: Your first solve
heading: Continue with your model
text: Continue with your model Python API: construct customers in memory and inspect typed root results. CLI reference: cuts, logging, distance modes, and backend selection. Network models: coordinate one or more route families in the shared master. Options reference: supported pricing controls and their scope.

title: Unified solve interface
heading: Unified solve interface
text:
Unified solve interface Use baldes solve INPUT [OPTIONS] for routing instances and JSON pricing models.The CLI has one entry point and one parser for time, iteration and node limits,stabilization, bound mode, logging, pricing options and JSON output. Routing andnetwork adapters handle their model-specific controls. baldes solve instances/Solomon/R101.txt --customers 5 --time 10
baldes solve examples/networks/triangle.json --tree --json -
 A pricing JSON input can be a network object, an array of networks, or a modelcontaining rows and networks. Within a model, networks accepts either oneobject or an array. Compilation always creates a collection. A single networkhas the same solver path and defaults as an array containing that network.Shared rows and original-variable declarations belong to the enclosing model. Python exposes pybaldes.solve for instances, paths, complete network models,scalar pricing networks and arrays of pricing networks: from pybaldes import PricingArc, PricingNetwork, solve

pricing = PricingNetwork(
    id=7, vertices=3, multiplicity=(0, 1),
    arcs=(PricingArc(0, 1, -2), PricingArc(1, 2, 0)),
)
single = solve(pricing, stabilize=False)
collection = solve([pricing], stabilize=False)
assert single.lp == collection.lp == -2
assert single.oracle_calls == collection.oracle_calls
 For shared constraints, use solve(pricings, rows=rows) or construct aNetworkProblem. Its networks constructor argument also accepts a scalar.Instance.solve() and NetworkProblem.solve() call the same public operation.Routing data automatically selects capacity-only or time-window constraints;problem_type can explicitly override that inference.

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Direct Cargo builds
text:
Direct Cargo builds Install Rust/Cargo and clone the repository. The core library can be builtwithout an external LP backend: cargo build --release
 For the CLI and routing master, initialize the vendored dependencies and buildwith Clp. This requires a C++14 compiler: git submodule update --init vendor/Clp vendor/CoinUtils
cargo build --release --features clp
./target/release/baldes --help
 The clp feature builds Clp 1.17.10 and CoinUtils 2.11 from those submodules.To also enable the optional HiGHS backend and integer solver, install itsshared library and use cargo build --release --features clp,highs.The CLI and routing tree require clp; highs alone provides the library'sHiGHS backend and generic MIP API. See below for library discovery details. Default builds use the modern MetaSolver-compatible master-only enforcementfor Ryan–Foster and accumulated-resource branch rows. To use the olderpricing-enforced policies, disable default features and select the desiredbackend explicitly, for example cargo build --release --no-default-features --features clp. Certified mode still requires independent original-domainproofs and does not treat numerical master-only closure as certification. Disjoint service-start windows are optional: usecargo build --release --features multi-time-windows for the library, or--features clp,multi-time-windows for network JSON and the CLI. Seemultiple time windows for the Rust,Python and JSON APIs. Python installation is covered in the pyBaldes installation guide.

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Rank-one node memory
text: Rank-one node memory Use cargo build --release --features clp,rank-one-node-memory to generaterank-one cuts with node memory instead of arc memory. In make config, selectRank-one memory → Node, or set CONFIG_RANK_ONE_MEMORY=node in the savedconfiguration. CONFIG_RANK_ONE_MEMORY=arc preserves the existing runtime policy. The feature maps arc-memory requests (BALDESrankOneCutsMemoryType=1 or RustMemoryType::Arc) to vertex memory during cut generation. The default-copy andall-vertices modes already use vertex memory and retain their meaning. Explicitlyregistered cuts retain their declared representation. Node memory retains acut's remainder through remembered vertices, while arc memory can distinguishindividual arcs entering or leaving the same vertex; the resulting limited-memorycut coefficients and LP bounds can therefore differ. Master coefficients andpricing use the selected cut representation consistently. Python builds expose the same feature, for examplematurin develop --features rank-one-node-memory.

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: NG memory size
text: NG memory size Each vertex remembers at most 15 ng elements by default. Build with--features ng-memory-31 or --features ng-memory-63 to raise the limit to 31or 63; when both are enabled, 63 applies. In make config, cycleNG memory → 15 / 31 / 63, or set CONFIG_NG_MEMORY=31 (or 63) in thesaved configuration. The limit applies after arc memory is merged into each vertex. Graphs thatexceed it fail during preparation with native NG local memory exceeds N elements. Wider memory stores a 32- or 64-bit ng word in every label instead of16 bits, so labeling uses more memory and bandwidth; keep the default unless theneighborhoods need it. Rust code can read the compiled limit frombaldes::graph::ng::NG_MEMORY_CAPACITY, and Python frompybaldes.ng_memory_capacity (for example aftermaturin develop --features ng-memory-31).

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Gurobi master backend
text:
Gurobi master backend Download and extract the latest stable Linux release into the repository'signored external/ directory: ./scripts/setup/gurobi_downloader
 The script detects x86-64, ARM64, or PowerPC Linux, verifies Gurobi's publishedchecksum, and prints the installation path to use in make config. It reusesverified downloads and existing installations. Use --version 13.0.3 to pin arelease, --destination PATH for another directory, or --help for options.Extraction requires Python with tarfile.data_filter (Python 3.12+). Install Gurobi and configure a valid license. Set GUROBI_HOME to its platforminstallation directory, containing lib/, then build: export GUROBI_HOME=/opt/gurobi1300/linux64
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$GUROBI_HOME/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
cargo build --release --features clp,gurobi
./target/release/baldes solve instances/Solomon/R101.txt --master gurobi
 On macOS configure DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH as needed instead. The build detects theversioned C library (for example libgurobi130.so) in $GUROBI_HOME/lib.Set GUROBI_LIB_NAME=gurobi130 explicitly if that directory contains multipleversions. Gurobi is linked dynamically and is not bundled with BALDES.License errors are reported when the backend is initialized. GurobiMaster implements the generic Rust LpMaster interface with automaticalgorithm selection, warm-basis reoptimization, primal values, duals, reduced costs, basis-awarecut cleanup, solve limits, and independent model copies. Use --features gurobifor the library backend alone; the routing CLI/tree also require clp.All three native features may be enabled together. Enumerated-node integersolving continues to use the highs feature. Routing root/tree solves give HiGHS and Gurobi all CPUs available to the processby default. Use --master-threads N to limit their worker budget, or--master-threads 0 for all available CPUs. CPU affinity is respected.Clp and native IPM ignore this setting. HiGHS retains adaptive primal/dualsimplex; Gurobi uses automatic algorithm selection. Both receive the workerbudget and determine actual algorithm parallelism. Warm simplex reoptimizationmay remain serial, and more workers do not guarantee a faster solve.HiGHS models in one process must use a consistent worker budget because itsnative scheduler is shared; configure it before the first solve. Forks retaintheir parent's budget. In Rust, use RootOptions::master_threads; in Python,use solve(..., master_threads=N). For Python, build with maturin develop --release --features clp,gurobi frompython/, then pass master_solver="gurobi" to solve. Checkpybaldes.has_gurobi to see whether that wheel includes the backend.In make config, enable Gurobi backend and set Gurobi installation,or leave its path empty to inherit GUROBI_HOME from your shell. Save andrun make to build with those settings.

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Interactive configuration
text:
Interactive configuration From the repository root: make config       # Open the configuration window in your terminal
make              # Compile with the saved settings
 make menuconfig opens the same window. Use Up/Down or J/K to selectan option, Space/Enter to change it, S to save and exit, and Q/Escapeto discard changes. Text fields accept Enter to confirm, Escape to cancel,Backspace to delete and Ctrl-U to clear. Home/End jump to the first/lastsetting; Page Up/Page Down move five settings at a time. Settings are grouped into Build, Performance, Toolchain and Cargo. Wideterminals show contextual help and a live build summary beside the options;compact terminals keep help below the scrolling list. The header tracksunsaved changes. The menu adapts automatically when resized, down to 64 columnsby 20 rows, and respects NO_COLOR for a monochrome display. This is a kernel-style terminal menu, implemented in Rust rather than Linux'sKconfig tooling. It requires Make, Rust/Cargo, and POSIX stty in an interactiveANSI terminal (Linux/macOS). It opens in the current terminal; no desktopsession, Python packages, ncurses headers or UI library downloads are needed.The helper is compiled directly with rustc into target/baldes-build beforeconfiguration, so it does not need to build the solver first.

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Build options
text:
Build options Setting Default Effect Profile release Choose Cargo's release or dev profile Clp Off Enable the clp Cargo feature HiGHS Off Enable the highs Cargo feature Gurobi Off Enable the gurobi Cargo feature; requires an installation and license Command-line program Off Build the baldes executable along with the library; selects Clp Optional SIMD Off Cycle off / AVX2 / AVX-512; only CPU-supported modes are selectable Native CPU Off Add -C target-cpu=native, preserving existing Rust flags Release debug symbols Off Set CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=1 for profiling Offline Off Pass --offline to Cargo Locked dependencies On Pass --locked, preserving Cargo.lock Scalar resource dimensions 2 Set BALDES_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS; fixed capacity for Python and the default Rust types Parallel jobs 0 (automatic) Pass --jobs N when nonzero Target triple Empty (host) Pass --target TRIPLE for cross compilation HiGHS installation Empty (automatic) Set HIGHS_DIR to the root containing lib/libhighs Gurobi installation Empty (shell environment) Set GUROBI_HOME to the installation root containing lib/libgurobi The library, including native IPM, pricing, cuts, and HGS, is always included.These components currently have no Cargo feature switches. Algorithm settingssuch as cut priorities and IPM tolerances remain runtime options. The CLI requires Clp. Selecting the CLI enables Clp; deselecting Clp alsodeselects the CLI. Native CPU optimization cannot be combined with a targettriple. Cross compilation requires installing the Rust target and configuringits linker separately, including any enabled native solver libraries. Before building Clp, initialize its source submodules and provide a C++14compiler: git submodule update --init vendor/Clp vendor/CoinUtils
 HiGHS needs a shared library with 32-bit HighsInt. Discovery follows theexisting Cargo build: HIGHS_DIR/lib, vendor/highs/lib, pkg-config, then thesystem linker path. Leaving the menu's installation field empty preservesHIGHS_DIR from your shell. Configure your runtime library search path asneeded for a custom HiGHS installation.

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Saved settings and automation
text:
Saved settings and automation The menu saves a local .config, ignored by Git. Subsequent Make commandsread it. A missing configuration uses release/library-only defaults with nooptional solver dependencies. Cargo commands invoked directly continue touse their explicit Cargo flags; they do not read .config. make showconfig                # Display effective settings
make print-command             # Preview the Cargo build invocation
make defconfig                 # Replace .config with defaults
make defconfig CONFIG=ci.config # Write another configuration file
make CONFIG=ci.config          # Build with it
 For noninteractive use, run make defconfig and edit the file or supply asaved config via CONFIG=path. The format is CONFIG_NAME=value, using y/nfor booleans and double quotes for strings. Backslashes and quotes in stringsmust be escaped. Missing settings take their defaults; unknown/duplicate keys,invalid values and conflicting dependencies are rejected. The file is parsedas data and is never included as Make code or sourced by a shell. An example configuration for the CLI with both LP backends: CONFIG_PROFILE=release
CONFIG_CLP=y
CONFIG_HIGHS=y
CONFIG_GUROBI=n
CONFIG_CLI=y
CONFIG_SIMD=off
CONFIG_NATIVE_CPU=n
CONFIG_RELEASE_DEBUG=n
CONFIG_OFFLINE=n
CONFIG_LOCKED=y
CONFIG_JOBS=0
CONFIG_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS=2
CONFIG_TARGET=""
CONFIG_HIGHS_DIR=""
CONFIG_GUROBI_HOME=""

title: Configuring and building BALDES
heading: Other Make targets
text: Other Make targets Command Action make build / make all Same build as plain make make check Cargo check for the selected artifacts and features make test Run library/integration tests with the selected profile/features make clippy Lint library/integration tests and the selected CLI make fmt Check formatting in the baldes package make clean Run cargo clean -p baldes; retain .config make test-config Test config parsing, dependencies and Cargo argument translation make help List targets and tool overrides make test and make clippy select integration tests as well as the library;Cargo may build the CLI for integration tests when its Clp requirement isenabled, even if the CLI artifact is disabled for ordinary builds. Theworkspace's Python extension is built separately using its existing packagingcommands. CARGO=path and RUSTC=path override the tool executables. Existing compiler/linker environment variables remain available to Cargo.The frontend prints the command and any configuration-specific environmentoverrides before running it and propagates Cargo's failure status to Make. The scalar setting accepts any nonnegative usize. For example,CONFIG_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS=5 compiles capacity 5; models may activate fewercoordinates. The saved setting overrides BALDES_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS inheritedfrom the shell for Make builds. Direct Cargo or maturin builds use that environmentvariable instead and do not read .config. Explicit Rust Graph::<D> / Solver::<D>counts remain independent of the configured default. See scalar resources. Optional SIMD is disabled by default. In make config, cycle through off,avx2, and avx512; unsupported CPU modes are skipped. Saved modes are validatedagainst the host CPU and require an empty target triple. Legacy n / y settingsremain accepted as off / avx2.Direct Cargo builds use --features simd for AVX2 or --features simd-avx512for AVX-512F (requires Rust 1.89 or newer). On x86-64, sufficiently longdisposable-resource dominance scans use the selected kernel after runtime CPUdetection. AVX-512 builds fall back to AVX2 when available. Other CPUs and small scans retain theportable implementation. Scalar capacities remain arbitrary; the optimizedscan applies when the model activates one or two disposable resources andthe compiled capacity is at least two.The simd feature also enables runtime-dispatched AVX2 rank-one bitsetaccumulation for at least 16 words, independently of the resource dimension.This feature does not require target-cpu=native and does not change numericalcomparison tolerances or certification policy. For eight-label AVX-512F dominance scans, usecargo build --release --features clp,simd-avx512. The Python crate currentlyforwards simd, but does not declare simd-avx512. This feature includes simdand requires Rust 1.89 or newer;the default and AVX2-only builds retain the package's existing Rust requirement.Runtime dispatch prefers AVX-512F on supported x86-64 CPUs, then AVX2, thenthe portable implementation. No global CPU flags are required. The AVX-512kernel needs only AVX-512F, including for the packed NG masks, and preservesfirst-candidate ordering and the original floating-point comparison order.See SIMD dispatch for dispatch behavior and portability details.

title: Solver architecture and ownership
heading: Solver architecture and ownership
text: Solver architecture and ownership Documentation index · Solve interface · Source layout BALDES has one master framework. A single pricing network is a collection oflength one. Input shape does not select a separate column-generation or treealgorithm. A master containing only static variables can have no pricing networks.

title: Solver architecture and ownership
heading: From input to a solution
text: From input to a solution The CLI, Python wrapper or Rust caller supplies routing data or an explicitnetwork model. Routing registration produces the same model::Problemrepresentation: shared rows and a collection of networks. master/formulation builds the restricted LP, including network-quantityrows and shared rows. master/preprocessing owns propagation and flow rows. master/cg sequences LP solves, pricing, stabilization, cut installation,feasibility recovery and enumeration handoffs. master/pricing schedules enabled networks, collects their columns andcombines their bound contributions. Each network uses pricing::Solverfor its resource-constrained labeling search or retained route universe. For integer search, master/tree selects and evaluates nodes through onelifecycle driver. Model adapters supply branch candidates, original-modelwitnesses and certificates. The selected LP backend owns the native LP state. Concern One implementation owner Canonical rows and network collection master/model Restricted-master construction and row batches master/formulation LP/pricing/cut iteration and restart bookkeeping master/cg Network scheduling and aggregate pricing feedback master/pricing One network's labels, resource transitions and cost preparation pricing with labeling, graph and cuts Propagation and conservation rows master/preprocessing Frontier, node limits, dispatch and tree status master/tree LP backend and integer-copy controls master/solvers The two pricing directories describe two levels. master/pricing coordinatesnetwork oracles; pricing implements an oracle. A scheduling change belongs inthe coordinator, and a change to route extension or dominance belongs in theoracle/labeling layer. Both benefit one-network and many-network solves.

title: Solver architecture and ownership
heading: Why routing and model adapters remain
text: Why routing and model adapters remain master::model::Problem stores the model. master::routing::RoutingContextregisters customer-cover rows, fleet semantics and routing metadata around thatsame model. It does not define another graph/rows representation. Routing and explicit network inputs can supply different cuts, branch families,preprocessing rules and proof contracts. For example, routing hooks configurecapacity/rank-one separation; explicit models register their row coefficientsand original-variable decisions. These differences are properties of theregistration. They do not depend on whether a collection contains one networkor several. Encoding a routing problem manually as a network model does notimplicitly install all routing-specific hooks. The routing, model and imported-column tree adapters share selection, budgets,frontier storage and evaluation dispatch. Imported sources have their owncolumn transport and completeness contracts; model/imported/multiple groupsexternal sources and is not another tree or multi-pricing engine.

title: Solver architecture and ownership
heading: Public entry points
text: Public entry points Input / operation Entry point CLI routing file or pricing JSON baldes solve INPUT CLI integer search baldes solve INPUT --tree Python instance, path, pricing network, array or model pybaldes.solve(problem, **options) Python model constructors Instance, PricingNetwork, NetworkProblem Rust explicit network root master::model::solve Rust routing registration/root master::routing::RoutingContext, master::routing::solve Rust integer search for either registration master::tree::solve Low-level resource-constrained path pricing pricing::Solver / Python Solver Python routing input currently exposes root relaxation solves; explicit networkmodels additionally expose tree=True. These are interface capabilities, notseparate implementations selected by network count. The Python _solvetransport compiles model-specific input into the shared Rust framework. RootResult and NetworkResult preserve registration-specific reports.A shared engine does not promise identical LP bases or branching trajectoriesacross different registrations or policies. See results and guarantees.

title: Solver architecture and ownership
heading: Extending the framework
text: Extending the framework Keep a new generic scheduling, construction, restart or frontier rule in itsowner above. Put new model coefficients and witnesses in an adapter. Keep cutmathematics in cuts, with installation through the shared CG lifecycle. Tests belong in tests/, with private unit tests attached through #[path].Local investigations belong under ignored internal/; local experimental workbelongs under ignored working/. Neither is a public documentation source.

title: Source layout
heading: Source layout
text: Source layout Documentation index · Architecture · Test layout The source tree groups code by the work it owns. A pricing network and an arraycontaining that network use the same master framework. See thearchitecture guide for execution flow and adapter semantics.

title: Source layout
heading: Production ownership
text: Production ownership Directory Responsibility src/core/ Errors, options, logging and conservative floating-point arithmetic src/graph/ Graphs, resources, neighborhoods and bucket geometry src/labeling/ Label storage, resource extension, joining and dominance src/pricing/ Stateful network oracle, cost preparation, restrictions and retained route universes src/enumeration/ Route-domain proofs and bounded path collection src/cuts/ Cut definitions, registration, separation and coefficient replay src/master/model/ Canonical shared rows/networks, registrations, original variables and snapshots src/master/routing/ Customer/fleet registration, routing cut hooks, witnesses and certificates src/master/formulation/ Shared restricted-master construction and dynamic row insertion src/master/cg/ Column-generation lifecycle, artificial columns, pools, restarts and handoffs src/master/pricing/ Scheduling and feedback aggregation across enabled network oracles src/master/preprocessing/ Propagation, conservation rows and model/routing preprocessing adapters src/master/tree/ Shared lifecycle, frontier, policies, history, strong branching and adapters src/master/stabilization/ Smoothing, proximal stabilization and curvature rules src/master/solvers/ Clp, HiGHS, Gurobi and shared integer-copy controls src/extensions/ HGS, IPM, EVRP, p-step, robust routing and column elimination src/inputs/ Instance parsing and graph construction src/bin/baldes/ main.rs, unified cli.rs, and distinct CE/p-step commands src/api/ Public low-level interface helpers python/pybaldes/ Python data/results and unified solve.py entry point python/rust/src/frontend/ One _solve transport and private routing/network input compilers master::model::Problem owns shared rows and a network collection.RoutingContext holds that model with routing metadata. The physical sourceowners for tree and preprocessing algorithms are master/tree andmaster/preprocessing; their model-specific files live under those owners. Private adapters can be attached to their data-owning Rust module through#[path]. That preserves field privacy while keeping a single physical sourcefor the implementation. Public callers use the parent's exported interface,not private attachment names such as tree_adapter or flow_adapter.

title: Source layout
heading: Finding the right file
text: Finding the right file Change Start here New model rows / quantity layout master/formulation/mod.rs LP/pricing iteration or recovery handoff master/cg/driver.rs, master/cg/feasibility.rs Initial/cut/branch artificial columns master/cg/rows.rs Network visitation / admission master/pricing/mod.rs, master/pricing/scheduling.rs Raw objective pricing / cost cache pricing/variable_costs.rs Propagation or flow rows master/preprocessing/, including shared flow/mod.rs Node dispatch / budgets master/tree/driver.rs Open-node priority / overflow master/tree/frontier.rs Routing/model/imported tree interpretation master/tree/adapters/ CLI parsing and result output bin/baldes/cli.rs Python scalar/array normalization python/pybaldes/solve.py A module with implementation children normally uses name/mod.rs; a leaf usesname.rs. Keep shared state near its consumers, helpers private to their owner,and established solver verbs such as price, extend, join and separate.Split independently explainable responsibilities; avoid generic utils filesor moving long argument lists behind pass-through helpers.

title: Source layout
heading: Tests, examples and documentation
text: Tests, examples and documentation tests/unit/: private unit tests, attached with feature-gated #[path] modules. tests/api, tests/master, tests/pricing and other subsystem folders: public-interface integration suites, explicitly registered in Cargo.toml. python/tests/: Python wrapper and native-interface checks. examples/: runnable demonstrations; instances/: benchmark inputs. docs/: maintained Markdown, built into the documentation site. internal/ and working/: ignored local investigations and experiments. Test bodies and fixtures stay outside src/. Most unit paths mirror theirimplementation owner; the #[path] declaration is authoritative where a privateadapter belongs to another logical Rust module. The current separation gives one owner to master construction, network pricingcoordination, preprocessing and tree orchestration. Model-specific data andproof hooks remain explicit adapters. A future refactor of the CG loop shouldpreserve its restart, feasibility, cut-remapping and enumeration contracts;folder moves alone do not establish numerical or behavioral equivalence.

title: Command-line usage
heading: Command-line usage
text:
Command-line usage Documentation index · Build configuration · Python Commands below run from the repository root after building with --features clp. ./target/release/baldes solve instances/Solomon/R101.txt --customers 25 --rank1
./target/release/baldes solve instances/cvrplib/A-n32-k5.vrp --capacity-cuts
./target/release/baldes hgs instances/Solomon/R101.txt --population-size 50 --nb-iter 5000
 Use solve INPUT for both routing instances and pricing models. A .jsonpath contains a network model; Solomon and CVRPLIB pathsare parsed as routing inputs. JSON accepts a scalar network, an array, or anenclosing model with shared rows. The solve guide describes inputnormalization and common controls. Routing constraints are inferred from the instance. Use --ignore-time-windowsto solve Solomon data as capacity-only CVRP. hgs, ce and pstep are distinctalgorithm commands. Run baldes --help for the complete installed interface. Routing coordinate distances default to truncated tenths (--rounding tenth).Use none for unrounded Euclidean distances, nearest for TSPLIB nint, orceil for CEIL_2D. Explicit full/triangular distance matrices retain theirsupplied weights. The routing root's fleet bound is the customer count; itstree uses the instance fleet size. CVRPLIB DISTANCE limits are unsupported. baldes solve examples/networks/triangle.json --json -
baldes solve examples/networks/triangle.json --tree --nodes 100 --json -

title: Command-line usage
heading: Routing options
text: Routing options Option Meaning --ignore-time-windows ignore time windows and service times with solve --customers N keep the first N customers --ng N NG neighbourhood size (default 8) --steps S or --steps TIME,CAPACITY Initial bucket widths in graph resource units (time, capacity). A single value applies to both; 0 selects automatic sizing (default). Dynamic refinement can decrease these widths. --reference-ng the N nearest customers, ties by index (the comparison setup) --rounding MODE distances none (unrounded), nearest, tenth or ceil (default: tenth) --cuts enable rank-one, capacity, k-path, knapsack (rounding/1K), and Fenchel cuts; also 2-path for models with time windows. Requires the integer-demand Fenchel configuration to be valid. --rank1 separate limited-memory rank-one cuts --clp-scaling MODE equilibrium (default), auto, geometric, or off --capacity / --capacity-cuts separate rounded capacity cuts in the routing master --two-path-cuts enable capacity cuts with Kohl's time resource attached (VRPTW only) --tree run integer branch-and-price for the input registration --tree-threads N concurrent open-node evaluations; default 1, requires --tree for N > 1 --nodes N tree node limit (default 10,000) --branching MODE default (default), vehicles, ryan-foster, arc, cluster, resource, hybrid, or edge --no-strong-branching use fractionality instead of phased strong branching --no-diving disable strong diving --no-mip-heuristic disable restricted-master integer search --mip-nodes N node budget per restricted-master integer-search call --enumerated-mip solve complete enumerated node masters with HiGHS; requires --tree and the highs feature --deluxing filter complete enumerated columns before MIP; enables --enumerated-mip, requires --tree and highs, conflicts with --no-enumeration --no-enumeration no reduced-cost fixing or enumeration --upper-bound X initial incumbent for fixing --no-stabilization no dual-price smoothing --master MODE clp (default), ipm, highs, or gurobi; optional backends need their build features, and IPM disables stabilization --master-threads N HiGHS/Gurobi workers; default 0 uses available CPUs; Clp/IPM ignore this setting --bound-mode MODE numerical (default) uses pricing bounds with tolerances; certified requires independent original-domain bound validation --hgs-time S positive HGS search budget before routing solve; separate from --time --hgs-columns MODE best plan (default), all distinct feasible routes, or N cheapest new routes --dynamic-ng P strengthen NG memories from master cycles at separator priority P --option NAME=VALUE set a supported BALDES pricing option (repeatable) --verbose, -v, --log solver progress table on stderr, every 10 CG iterations --log-interval N enable progress every N CG iterations; N must be positive --iterations N master iteration limit --time S solve or standalone HGS time limit in seconds --json FILE write structured results; - emits JSON alone on stdout --population-size N HGS minimum population size (default: 25) --nb-iter N HGS iterations without improvement before stopping/restarting --seed N HGS random seed (default: 0) --help, -h show all CLI options, including tree controls Root Optimal means the LP relaxation converged; tree Optimal means theinteger routing gap closed within the configured tolerances. HGS suppliesfeasible solutions without an optimality proof. Root LP route values can befractional, and NG routes can revisit customers. Normal root and tree solves use numerical bounds and skip the full certificatesearch. Use --bound-mode certified for independently validated bounds. Thatmode attempts validation when an exact pass can close pricing or the incumbentgap; failure leaves its selected bound unknown. Route-feasibility checks andexact pricing remain enabled in both modes. JSON reports bound_mode, the selected bound, and separate numerical_boundand certified_bound fields. An unknown bound is null. A numerical estimatenever substitutes for an unknown certified bound. A tree result labels theguarantee of its global bound; it does not report a global numerical estimatein certified mode. Root results retain both estimates when available. Solomon instances are in instances/, and a few CVRPLIB ones ininstances/cvrplib/. Enable --verbose for an aligned progress table with the restricted-masterobjective, selected lower bound, incumbent, gap, reduced cost, column counts,current bucket step size (in resource order, separated by /), pricing phase,and elapsed time. Bucket step changes are also printed between progress rows,independently of the log interval. Use --log-interval 5 for more frequent output.When cut families are enabled, the table also shows their current cut counts;disabled families have no column. For advanced routing, see the branch-and-price tree guide andenumerated MIP guide. Build instructions are in the build guide; benchmark results are inRoot benchmarks. For named pricing controls, see the BALDES option reference.Public option names start with BALDES, for example--option BALDESlabelDominanceStrategy=1. Rust exposes supported metadata inOPTION_TABLE; Python exposes Solver.option_names() andSolver.option_support(name). The public list contains 41 supported controls,plus two enumerated-MIP controls when both clp and highs are enabled.Scope can depend on the operation or configured cut family.

title: pyBaldes documentation
heading: pyBaldes documentation
text: pyBaldes documentation All BALDES documentation pyBaldes is the Python distribution of BALDES. Import it as pybaldes.It provides typed routing inputs/results, a stateful resource-constrainedshortest-path pricing solver, and shared-master models with multiple pricingnetworks. Solves run in the Rust library; no CLI subprocess is required. pybaldes.solve is the common entry point for routing instances, paths, scalarpricing networks, arrays and complete models. Instance.solve andNetworkProblem.solve delegate to it. See the solve interfaceand architecture for normalization and shared ownership.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Network models and shared masters
text: Network models and shared masters Documentation index With clp, master::model::solve solves a shared root and returns an ownednode snapshot that can be resumed or forked. Its pricing graphs share masterrows. Each Network owns a graph, a unique nonnegative ID andnonnegative multiplicity bounds. Rust models may use a finite lower bound andpositive-infinite upper bound. Local arc IDs may overlap acrossnetworks: route identities include the network ID and resource schedule. A network is one pricing subproblem: a graph, route family and multiplicitybounds. One network and an array containing that network use the same coordinator.Several networks can represent different types, depots or resources, or severalcopies of the same family. Network count is independent of the number of CPUworkers used within an oracle. See the architecturefor the shared construction, pricing and tree lifecycle, and thesolve interface for scalar/array normalization. Problem.rows defines the shared constraints. Network.arc_entries containsone list of (shared_row, coefficient) pairs per physical arc, in graph order.route_entries adds coefficients charged once per route. The coordinator addsthe network multiplicity rows separately; callers do not include them in theshared-row indices. Arc costs define original route costs. Variable-costmapping used internally by pricing does not modify the supplied graphs.Physical multiplicity rows appear in input-network order: a finite upper rowcomes first, then a lower row when the lower bound is positive. An infiniteupper bound adds no row. Shared rows follow these multiplicity rows in theiroriginal order. In Rust, use Window { lower: 0., upper: f64::INFINITY } for an unlimited routecount; Window::new remains the finite scalar-resource window constructor.Original shared rows can prove a finite remaining count, which tightens futurecolumns and bound compensation and survives forks/fixing. If a negative reducedcost has no finite count bound, the estimate remains unknown while pricing cancontinue. A zero reduced cost does not multiply infinity. Truly unboundednegative-cost route directions report an unbounded backend solve. JSON uses"multiplicity": [0, null] for an unlimited upper count. The lower count mustremain finite and nonnegative. The coordinator maintains independent pricing state, combines columns into onerestricted master and aggregates each network's multiplicity contribution andstabilization subgradient. Output.oracle_calls counts individual oracle calls;Output.master.pricing_calls counts batches. Output.values gives the currentrestricted-master quantity for every route in Output.routes.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Network pricing schedules
text: Network pricing schedules Options.network_pricing_schedule selects NetworkPricingSchedule in Rust.The JSON/Python option is network_pricing_schedule; the CLI flag is--network-pricing-schedule. All three accept these choices: Schedule Network visitation full-sweep (default) Visit every enabled network in input order. cyclic Resume after the last visited network, wrap around, and return after a network generates a previously unregistered negative-reduced-cost route. sorted Visit unseen networks first, then ascending recent minimum reduced cost, breaking ties by input order. Return on the same new-route condition. promising-first Persistent primary/secondary queues following recovered strategy 2; normal solved networks enter the secondary queue. unvisited-first Persistent queues following recovered strategy 3; unvisited primary entries precede newly promising entries. For example, problem.solve(network_pricing_schedule="cyclic") in Python, orbaldes solve MODEL.json --network-pricing-schedule sorted. The optionalso applies to snapshot solves and the nodes of an assignment tree. A partial batch returns columns without an aggregate bound correction orsubgradient. It is never exact, even when each visited oracle used an exactphase. A traversal that finds no new negative route visits every enabled network;only a complete batch can supply a fresh global pricing estimate or establishpricing convergence. Cached scores affect visitation order only: minima andcoverage are recomputed at the current dual point. Disabled networks are skipped.The cursor and scores reset on a new solve, a formulation fork or a phase change.An installed complete enumerated universe continues to use its full scan.Early return requires reduced cost below minus the configured CG tolerance;insignificant negative routes do not interrupt the scan. The sorted score is an explicit BALDES heuristic. The two native queue policiesuse network_unpromising_limit (CLI --network-unpromising-limit, default 1),which limits normal solved visits after a new improving column appears. Emptysweeps still visit all networks. Queue order persists across phase changes;forks and new solves reset it. Normal modern native pricing returns zero evenwhen it generates columns; negative reduced cost does not imply the nativepositive-status promising classification. That positive branch is recoveredstatically but has no demonstrated normal-modern public reachability.Native strategy 1 is deliberately excluded: its pinned public control abortswith invalid-pointer corruption. These schedules change work distribution;speedups and identical native trajectories are not promised.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Proximal pricing
text:
Proximal pricing cg::Options.proximal selects explicit ProximalParameters in Rust. One hardband gives box-step stabilization, one finite-penalty band gives a three-piecepenalty, and two bands give five pieces. In JSON/Python: result = problem.solve(
    proximal={"bands": [{"half_width": 0.5, "penalty": 1.0}]},
    network_pricing_schedule="promising-first",
)
 penalty: null means a hard band. multi_point: true enables the privatesupport-plane epigraph and requires a finite outer penalty. Usemax_points (positive, default 1) to bound retained support planes; inactiveunprotected planes age out after more than two zero-activity solves. CLI callers can use--proximal-width 0.5 --proximal-penalty 1, omit the penalty for a hard box, orpass a complete bands object with --proximal FILE.json. Proximal pricingreplaces smoothing; --no-stabilization disables both. Auxiliary columns, support rows and beta variables belong to a private LP copy.Its objective cannot update the original bound or incumbent. An unsuccessfulproximal pricing pass retries the original master duals before completing aphase. Explicit modes reset their center on phase changes; automatic curvatureretains its accepted center and radii. Backends that cannotclone the master, or unfinished private solves, fall back to original duals.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Automatic curvature
text:
Automatic curvature Automatic three-piece stabilization needs no manually prepared state: result = problem.solve(proximal={"curvature": {}})
# Five-piece automatic bands:
result = problem.solve(proximal={"curvature": {"five_piece": True}})
 CLI flags are --automatic-curvature and --automatic-curvature-five-piece.--proximal FILE.json accepts the same object. Automatic curvature is a separatemode from explicit bands and multi_point; conflicting selections are rejected.--no-stabilization disables the selected mode. Existing defaults remain smoothing. Curvature option Default Meaning five_piece false Maintain inner and outer radii instead of one radius. kappa 1 Positive: initialize curvature from the first positive ordinary-row mean divided by Kappa. curvature 1 Configured starting curvature when Kappa is nonpositive. advance_rate 1 Radius adaptation rate, with native stored-float precision. artificial_activity_factor 10 Multiply curvature when stabilization auxiliaries remain active at a stopping pass. initial null Optional explicit prepared state; ordinary use needs no override. The controller measures original master duals against the previous acceptedcenter before pricing, and consumes that measurement once after the iteration.Retries and a later center move cannot replace the saved mean. Positive-meanbootstrap initializes the radii and curvature automatically. No eligible rowsmeans no fabricated feedback. Active dynamic rows use the same bands but donot enter the ordinary-row mean; generated network multiplicity rows are excludedfrom both measurement and automatic proximal variables. Root controllers useactual base/branch/cut row metadata. Custom CG controllers can implementcurvature_rows; row sense or append position does not define participation. node.with_row(...) adds an ordinary row. Rust with_dynamic_row(...) andPython node.with_row(..., dynamic=True) label an added dynamic row explicitly.An active private auxiliary above absolute activity 1e-6 can request a boundedno-new-column retry; these updates share the existing penalty/time/iterationbudgets. Equal-width bands retain separate activity variables. Automatic geometry survives pricing-phase and ordinary schedule restarts.Compatible warm starts retain the accepted center and exact global radii/curvaturewithout applying the explicit-mode child factor. New child rows start at centerzero; incompatible coordinate geometry is discarded while a restricted childcan retain global radius information. Resume is distinct from creating a child.Warm checkpoints validate configuration, physical row roles and original matrixprefixes; ordinary newly generated columns do not invalidate them. AuxiliaryLP columns, support planes and objective values never enter those checkpointsor authorize an original bound/incumbent. Phase estimates guide stabilization. Published lower bounds additionally usegraph-walk relaxations with downward arithmetic. Small acyclic scalar-resourcegraphs receive an additional work-limited path bound that keeps each path's costand resource lower states together. It supports signed secondary consumptionand waiting without using numerical labeling as a certificate. Equality waitingis relaxed, and an unfinished traversal retains the existing walk bound ratherthan publishing the minimum of a partial path set. If a negative cycle preventsa resource-free bound, nonnegative scalar consumption and bounded resourcewindows can justify a finite walk-length limit. The proof can combine dimensionswith different units: it sums their individual positive-arc occurrence limits.Arcs consuming zero on every selected dimension must form an acyclic graph.Thus different cycles may consume different resources. The fallback uses a bounded workbudget. Without a justified limit, or after arithmetic failure, budget exhaustionor an unavailable required path, the certificate remains unknown. A finiteresource-aware bound can still be too weak to close the gap. In certified mode, unavailable certificates cannot closethe gap; numerical mode retains its separate exact-pricing estimate. Finiteartificial penaltiesalso do not certify original-model infeasibility. A stalled restricted LP canstill contain artificial variables; its objective and route quantities arenot then an original feasible solution.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Assignment tree
text: Assignment tree master::tree::solve(problem, ModelTreeOptions { .. }) uses network-awaresnapshots. It tries proved shared resource-group splits,assignment rows, declared integer master variables, total network multiplicities,original physical-arc activities, then synchronized-service splits. WithModelTreeOptions::time_window_selection, arc activities are summed overwindow copies and time-window selection counts follow them; seebranching on time-window selection.It returns network-taggedinteger route quantities, an incumbent, selected bound mode, frontier bound andnode/work-limit status. Integer witnesses replay original graph resources,shared rows and original multiplicities with exact sums; objectives round upward.Fixed routes are included in this replay. A rounded labeling resource profilealone never authorizes an incumbent or fixed route. ModelTreeOptions::branching selects the family and child order.NetworkBranchingPolicy::MultiplicityFirst is the default: it tries fractionalnetwork route counts first and visits upper children first, following theobserved public native controls. ResourceFirst preserves the resource andassignment order above, with lower children first.It does not change disjunctions or proof bounds, and does not promise the sameLP basis, generated columns or total node count as another backend. Select itwith --network-branching multiplicity-first, JSON solve option"network_branching": "multiplicity-first", or Pythonsolve(..., tree=True, network_branching="multiplicity-first"). Tree selection is independent of branch-family selection.TreeSearchPolicy::Default (default) processes the deepest opennode first, then the lowest inherited numerical LP bound, then creation order. It uses thenative 1,000-node primary frontier and its overflow queue. Select thebound-first queue with TreeSearchPolicy::BestBound, CLI--network-tree-search best-bound, JSON "network_tree_search": "best-bound",or Python network_tree_search="best-bound". Queue comparisons use the numericalchannel even in certified mode; the selected certification bound still controlspruning and published proof bounds. Results retain nodes as thenumber of ordinary tree-node solves (excluding separate strong-branching trials).tree_processed_nodes also counts exact-pricing branching trials and freshnodes closed by an inherited bound. Restricted-LP and heuristic screens areincluded in strong_branching_trials and do not increment that processed count. Reusing a completed exact trial does not count it twice.All traversal policies budget outer tree selections. A phased branching passcan finish its trials past that limit, as in the native solver; its processedcount can therefore exceed the tree node limit.network_open_node_limit controls the primary frontier capacity (nativedefault 1000); overflow nodes use the native secondary priority queue. The CLIequivalent is --network-open-node-limit N.The native outer loop also requires a nonempty primary queue. If only overflownodes remain (including capacity zero after the root), the solve returnsIncomplete with the unresolved nodes and their bound retained.Native bound comparisons treatvalues as tied within 1e-6 + 1e-10 * max(abs(a), abs(b)); BALDES reproducesthat pairwise rule and the native vector-heap operations, including overflowpriority. Since tolerance-based pairwise ties are not transitive, this policyuses a custom heap rather than Rust's ordering-based BinaryHeap.network_tree_search="depth-bound-priority" selects deeper nodes first and prefersthe higher numerical LP bound at equal depth, followed by creation order.Its overflow queue retains the usual lower-bound preference, as in native.network_tree_search="bound-priority" selects native strategy 2. It ordersqueued children by the numerical LP dual bound, then the nativechild primal-bound sentinels, depth, parent treatment rank and creationorder. The child primal sentinels are equal before evaluation, so depth andparent rank decide ties. The default network_strategy2_rounding="unrounded"matches the native continuous-objective bound contract with nonpositiveintegerValuedBound. Integer-objective models can select "guarded-tolerance"for tolerant integer rounding, or "exact-ceil" for forced integer rounding.CLI uses --network-strategy2-rounding unrounded|guarded-tolerance|exact-ceil; JSON uses"network_strategy2_bound_rounding". These are ranking keys only and do notalter proof bounds. Rust callers can run snapshot.solve(options) after installingshared nonlinear rows, fixing routes or restricting master variables. It forksthe snapshot and retains cuts, bounds, fixed contributions and complete routeuniverses. A zero-node run preserves only the inherited bound of the requestedbound mode; a numerical bound is not promoted to a certificate. Every fallback split is an integer-valid floor/ceiling disjunction on anoriginal quantity. Continuous master variables are never branched as integers.These families still do not cover every fractional route decomposition; such anode remains Incomplete. An exact whole-original-flow contradiction can closea node. Positive artificials, a stalled LP or incomplete certification alone donot prove infeasibility. Complete-master integer deductions retain the explicitinteger-domain policy.Node/time limits retain the open-frontier bound. Bounds on fixed-route nodesare newly certified only when their RHS, offset and residual multiplicityreductions are exact; otherwise valid inherited certificates remain available,but a new original-domain bound stays unknown.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Finite column imports
text: Finite column imports Rust callers can combine routing networks with explicitly declared finiteoriginal-vector column domains using model::imported::solve. Seefinite column imports for coordinate links, column fixing,multiplicity bounds, identity mapping and complete-domain MIP.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Independent master variables
text: Independent master variables solve_with_master_variables(problem, variables, options) adds independentMasterVariable definitions to the shared master. Each definition has its ownID, objective cost, signed bounds (finite, one-sided or free), integrality flag and shared-rowcoefficients. IDs are independent of network and arc IDs. Root LPs relaxintegrality; complete-domain MIP retains it. Output.master_values returnsoriginal values by ID, separately from network-tagged routes. For a model with no pricing subproblems, Rust callers can usesolve_master(rows, variables, options). It solves the continuous relaxation andreturns the same snapshot API. Signed, one-sided, free and integer variablesretain their usual contracts. The empty pricing family is complete immediately:snapshot.solve_enumerated_mip(options) needs no preceding enumeration, andsnapshot.solve_tree(tree_options) branches integer master variables through the common tree entry point.No dummy network is required. A Problem::<D> with an empty networks list isalso accepted by solve_with_master_variables, for any compile-time D.An empty model has objective zero; original-row contradictions are available tothe tree as preprocessing proofs. This Rust API does not add master-variablefields to the CLI/Python JSON schema. Snapshots support with_master_variable_bounds(id, bounds) for restrictions orfixing. with_master_row(row, network_coefficients, master_coefficients) couplesthese variables to additive network activities;with_rank_one_master_row(row, floor_coefficients, master_coefficients) couplesthem to nonlinear floor rows. Existing parent restrictions remain in force.All operations preserve independent sibling snapshots. The corresponding treeentry point is master::tree::solve((problem, variables), tree_options). Signed variables retain their original coefficients and costs. Their boundsparticipate in joint propagation, and bounds tightened by original constraintsreach static master columns and publication certificates. Inferred positivelower bounds and negative upper bounds are also published as original-variablerows, so the LP, warm snapshots and MIP enforce those bounds. A bounded exactrow-reduction pass also combines shared constraints with linear equalities thatlink master variables. For example, a + b >= 1.5 and m = a + b implym >= 1.5; the optional integer policy strengthens this to m >= 2 when mis integer. The pass retains support-reducing sums/differences only, rejectsrounded coefficients/RHS values, and reserves most work for ordinary propagation.It does not treat nonlinear row envelopes as equalities. Continuous mastervalues remain continuous when route quantities are made integer in MIP andwitness validation. Infinite endpoints represent mathematical domains. An adverse dual point on anunbounded component can leave the published bound unknown. Original shared rowsmay supply a finite proof-only bound even with preprocessing disabled; this doesnot change the snapshot or replace infinity with a finite modeling cap.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Original activities, multiplicities and nonlinear rows
text: Original activities, multiplicities and nonlinear rows Rust snapshots expose with_activity_bounds(bounds, coefficients) to restrictan aggregate original variable across networks. Each RowCoefficients suppliesarc coefficients and a once-per-route coefficient for its network. Equal lowerand upper bounds fix the activity. with_multiplicity(network, bounds) boundsthe total route count, including fixed copies. Both operations fork the nodeand preserve restrictions in future pricing, descendants and enumeration. Activity bounds constrain the aggregate master activity. For example, an upperbound of 0.25 remains a fractional activity cap in the continuous relaxation.It is not an arc-availability flag. Opting into integer-domain preprocessing canstrengthen a proved integer activity cap below one to zero. Pricing supportsare defined separately by the graph and registered restrictions. with_rank_one_row(row, coefficients) installs a shared nonlinear row. EachRankOneCoefficients defines a network's coefficient asfloor(sum of visited vertex weights / denominator). Weights count each visit,lie between zero and denominator minus one, and must be zero at both terminals.Supported denominators are 1–7. The caller supplies a valid row. Fixed routes subtract their nonlinearcoefficient from its RHS, including when the row is installed after fixing.Pricing uses full memory; master coefficients retain the actual physical arcs.with_registered_cut_row(row, coefficients) accepts RegisteredCutCoefficientsfor existing packing, covering, limited-memory, arc-weighted and strong k-pathdescriptors. with_registered_cut_master_row also couples independent mastervariables. Use physical vertex/arc IDs for the selected network and consistentgraph-specific supports. Weights must be nonnegative and below the denominator(1–7); unsupported original-set mappings and incompatible descriptors arerejected. The caller supplies a valid inequality; these methods do not separatecuts automatically. Fixed-route shifts and future-column coefficients use theregistered memory contract. with_composite_cut_row(row, coefficients) sums several registered descriptorsinto one shared row, including multiple terms from the same network.with_composite_cut_master_row couples this sum to independent master variables.Repeated descriptors contribute repeatedly. Pricing applies the shared row dualto every term; replay and fixed-route shifts use their summed coefficient.This API expresses a sum, not an indicator that any term is present. The originalwith_registered_cut_row still rejects duplicate network descriptors. These Rust methods are not currently exposed in the JSON or Python model schema. with_presence_row(row, coefficients) installs a caller-supplied valid nonlinearrow over original-variable events. Each PresenceCoefficients supplies anetwork ID, a PresenceRow and event lists aligned with physical graph arcs.Mode::PairCount counts satisfied stored pairs, including duplicates;Mode::AnyPair contributes at most one. Repeated emission of an event does notmultiply its contribution. with_presence_master_row also couples independentmaster variables. All row senses are supported. Fixing replays the actualcoefficient, including rows appended after the fix; pricing, snapshots andcomplete enumeration/MIP use the same event definition. Original-domain certificates keep active presence rows together in a boundedwalk-state search. It charges actual event-pair increments using directedarithmetic, including duplicate pairs, repeated events and either dual sign.Event IDs are local to each row. Sparse event compression avoids allocating bythe largest event ID. Resource-derived walk-length bounds can cover adversecycles; otherwise an adverse cycle leaves this improvement unknown. Work ortime exhaustion falls back to the existing conservative relaxation. Thesecertificates do not require complete enumeration. Original-domain preprocessing drops nonnegative presence terms from <=relaxations and bounds them by the maximum coefficient times multiplicity for>= relaxations. When static terms exhaust the upper side of a <= or equalityrow, preprocessing searches source-to-sink walks with zero presence coefficient.It considers all pairs in that descriptor jointly, including events spread overseveral arcs, and forbids physical arcs absent from every such walk. The searchignores resources and elementarity, so its walk domain contains every feasibleroute. Cycles and repeated events are supported; equivalent incidence statesat the same vertex are merged. Sparse event IDs do not allocate the entiredeclared event domain. All searches share the preprocessing work budget. Anunfinished search publishes no additional walk-support exclusions; previouslyproved exclusions remain valid. These deductions participate in the jointflow/static-variable fixed point across pricing subproblems. Certified bounds can belooser than the numerical LP because their original-domain relaxation dropspositive presence penalties when joint presence-state certification exhausts itswork/time allowance; such a run can remain Stalled until a strongerproof or complete enumeration closes the gap. Registered cut rows also support original-domain zero-coefficient propagation.When directed bounds prove that static contributions exhaust a nonnegativerow's <= budget, every registered kernel in that row must be zero. A boundedwalk search keeps the kernels' packing remainders jointly, including vertex orphysical-arc memory resets. Covering and strong-entry kernels reject supporthits; repeated composite descriptors keep their sum semantics. Arcs absentfrom all zero-coefficient source-to-sink walks are forbidden before enumeration.The search ignores route resources and elementarity, so its walk domain is asafe superset. Interrupted searches publish no partial walk exclusions. These deductions share the flow/resource/presence work budget and repeat to ajoint fixed point. Signed static compensation or a positive fractional rowbudget prevents unjustified zero deductions. This is a necessary zero-budgetrule, not a general nonlinear optimizer or automatic cut separator. with_resource_knapsack_row(row, coefficients) installs a shared <= rowusing ResourceKnapsackCoefficients (network, resource coordinate, graph scaleand monotone nonnegative step cut). with_resource_knapsack_master_row alsocouples independent master variables. This API supports nonnegativeconsumption, initial usage and vertex/arc windows on a common power-of-two grid.The grid spacing must lie between 2^-18 and 1, and each value must use atmost 2^52 grid units. Integer schedules retain their existing range; fractionssuch as 0.5 and 0.125 are supported when the complete schedule fits thisrange. Finer binary fractions, negative values, and schedules requiring moregrid units are rejected before installation.Disposable resources may wait; equality resources must meet their windowswithout waiting. Coefficients use the earliest forward scalar schedule replayedfrom physical arcs; cached route profiles cannot change them. Pricing uses graphscaling and unrounded nonpositive duals. Fractional schedules, nonzero initial usage, waiting windows, intermediatecapacity changes and equality resources select forward-only pricing for theaffected network. Thispreserves the coefficient contract even if a caller requests bidirectionalsearch. Zero-initial integer disposable loads with uniform capacity retain theexisting bidirectional option. Fixed routes shift these rows, and descendants, enumeration and mixed MIPretain them. Complete-domain preprocessing can fix route quantities from thestep coefficients. Before enumeration, a row that permits only zero resourcepenalty can also forbid original arcs whose consumption guarantees a positivestep coefficient. Directed bounds on static variables must first prove that nonegative static contribution can compensate those penalties. Flow conservationthen propagates the arc fixings. The original-domain flow and resource-zerorules repeat while deductions enable each other, sharing one work budget.preprocessing_report().propagation.work_used reports the logical work spent.Incomplete budgeted passes retain valid partial deductions without claiming afixed point. Before complete enumeration, the original-domain certificatemay drop their nonnegative pricing penalty for a weaker valid lower bound;this need not close the LP gap. These methods require caller-supplied validinequalities and do not automatically separate resource-knapsack cuts. Node solves automatically propagate a joint arc-flow relaxation across networks.It includes shared activities, flow conservation and route multiplicities;nonlinear rows contribute safe activity envelopes. Proved-zero arc usage forbidsthat arc in future pricing and fixes affected retained columns to zero. Aftercomplete enumeration, a second pass can also deduce zero route quantities fromnonlinear coefficients. Missing future columns never justify these deductions. Use options.preprocessing.enabled = false to disable propagation, or adjustoptions.preprocessing.work_limit. snapshot.preprocess() runs the defaultpolicy on a fork; preprocess_with_options() supplies a separate budget.preprocessing_report() exposes aggregate arc and multiplicity bounds, workcompletion, route caps, zero fixings, and reasons for skipping unsafe arithmetic.Positive aggregate arc bounds are not per-route resource windows. After completetransfer, proved positive route-quantity caps are installed in the master andpreserved through cleanup, regeneration and descendants. Fixing copies of a routereduces its remaining cap. Upper-active columns may have negative reduced costs;the numerical and certified bounds account for these caps. Inexact coefficientaggregation or fixed-route reductions skip deductions. Exhausted work preservesvalid partial deductions. The default policy preserves the continuous LP and reports preprocessinginfeasibility without independently pruning a tree node. Setoptions.preprocessing.integer_domains = true to use original integer route,arc-usage and multiplicity domains, together with each master variable's declaredintegrality. Continuous master variables remain continuous. With this explicitpolicy, a proved contradiction can close an integer tree node even when its LPrelaxation is feasible. Reports distinguish inferred master-variable boundsfrom network activity bounds. Disabling propagation later does not widen asnapshot that already contains deductions; reuse an earlier ancestor for itsoriginal continuous relaxation.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Scope and model-specific behavior
text: Scope and model-specific behavior The canonical master accepts zero or more pricing networks. Static mastervariables, additive rows, registered nonlinear coefficients, original-variablebranches, snapshots and supported synchronization restrictions use that model.Registered cut kernels do not imply automatic separation of arbitrary nonlinearcuts. Routing registrations additionally provide their routing-specific cut,branch and witness hooks to the shared engines. Enumeration is complete only when its report establishes coverage of the stateddomain. Cutoff-bounded transfer covers improvements below its cutoff; a truncatedpool does not prove a global integer bound. A tree can return Incomplete whenits configured generators cannot split a remaining nonintegral decision or itsproof contract is unsupported. Read the relevant sections below and inspect thereturned reports rather than inferring guarantees from network count.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: CLI
text:
CLI The same solve command accepts a pricing model with a .json extension.It uses the shared master construction and pricing coordinator, with Clp forthis registration, and supports root solves and integer trees: cargo build --offline --features clp --bin baldes
target/debug/baldes solve examples/networks/triangle.json --json root.json
target/debug/baldes solve examples/networks/triangle.json --tree --json tree.json
# JSON alone on stdout, suitable for a pipe:
target/debug/baldes solve examples/networks/triangle.json --tree --json -
 The example has shared LP optimum 1.5 and integer optimum 2. --time,--iterations, --nodes, --bound-mode, --no-stabilization,--artificial-cost, --option NAME=VALUE, and --log-interval control solves.Run baldes solve --help for details. Routing-specific flags do not apply to explicit JSON network models.A successful command means the run completed and produced a result: inspectstatus and open_nodes for NodeLimit, TimeLimit or Incomplete outcomes. A model contains rows and networks. Rows use sense: "eq" | "le" | "ge"and a finite rhs. Each network has a unique nonnegative id, a verticescount, [lower, upper] fleet multiplicity, and an arcs list. Optionalfields are source (default zero), sink (default last vertex), resources,route_entries and ng. Vertex indices and shared-row indices are zero based.Arc IDs are assigned consecutively in each network's input order, starting atzero; overlapping IDs in different networks are supported. Each arc provides tail, head, cost and optional entries pairs[shared_row, coefficient]. Its optional consumption and bounds arraysmust match the resource count when nonempty. Arc bounds contain either[lower, upper] or null for each resource. Missing consumption is zero.Each resource has kind: "disposable" (default) or "equality", an optionalinitial value, and optional bounds with one [lower, upper] pair per vertex.Default resource bounds are [0, 100000]. Network route_entries are chargedonce per route. Optional ng contains one neighborhood list per vertex.Resources may be empty; the maximum count is the build's scalar capacity.Unknown fields, nonfinite values and inconsistent dimensions are rejected. Result routes retain network, local arcs, nodes, cost, resource states andvalue. A root's route_index identifies its registry entry for later fixing;zero-valued registered routes are retained too. fixed_routes lists fixedquantities separately. Unknown/nonfinite bounds and absent objectives are JSONnull, not Infinity. Root mode reports an LP relaxation; tree mode reportsan independently replayed integer witness when available. Their mode andbound_mode fields preserve that distinction.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Python
text:
Python The dedicated pyBaldes network guide covers Python model construction, solve options, snapshots, and synchronization. The sections here specify the shared Rust/CLI/Python model contract. Install the extension with Clp support (the Python build's default). The typedinputs use the same JSON schema as the CLI, allowing a single model to driveboth interfaces: from pybaldes import NetworkProblem, solve

problem = NetworkProblem.from_file("examples/networks/triangle.json")
root = solve(problem)
assert root.lp == 1.5
integer = problem.solve(tree=True)
assert integer.incumbent == 2.0

candidate = root.snapshot.fractional_assignments()[0]
left = root.snapshot.branch_assignment(
    candidate.shared_row, candidate.network, True,
)
right = root.snapshot.branch_assignment(
    candidate.shared_row, candidate.network, False,
)
assert left.solve().lp == 2.0
assert right.solve().lp == 2.0
assert root.snapshot.solve().lp == 1.5
 Models can also be constructed with NetworkProblem, SharedRow,PricingNetwork, PricingArc and PricingResource dataclasses. Useproblem.to_json() to export them for the CLI. NetworkResult.to_json()serializes owned result data and excludes its native snapshot. Root snapshots additionally expose with_row(SharedRow(...), coefficients)with NetworkRowCoefficients(network, arcs, per_route=0), andfix_route(route_index, quantity=1). Child operations return independentNetworkNode objects; node.solve(**options) returns a new result and snapshot.Quantities fixed in Python must be positive integers. Node handles belong toone Python thread and root/node calls keep the GIL. Fresh tree=True callsrelease the GIL and return owned results without a resumable snapshot. The root/tree solve accepts time_limit, max_iterations, node_limit,stabilize, bound_mode, artificial_cost, log_interval andpricing_options. Resuming a snapshot accepts node options; tree=Truerequires a fresh model. Tree iteration, pricing-batch and individual oraclecounts aggregate the evaluated nodes; nodes and open_nodes report tree work.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Complete enumeration and integer transfer
text:
Complete enumeration and integer transfer Enumeration is opt-in. Options.enumeration in Rust, enumerate=True inPython, or --enumerate in the CLI attempts a bounded full-domain transferat an accurate exact pricing checkpoint with no improving columns or positiveartificials. This can strengthen an NG master toits elementary-route master. Every enabled network must complete before anycolumns are committed. Existing valid columns and their bounds remain; cycliccolumns outside the integer domain are fixed to zero. All current physicalrows, including additive cuts/branches, remain in place. Descendants reuse thecomplete route universe and evaluate new row coefficients on it. Transfer supports nonempty physically elementary paths with disposable andscalar equality resources. Equality paths are collected through a disposablesuperset, then checked against the original equality transitions; paths feasibleonly by waiting are excluded. Equality resources with a non-fixed sinkwindow use forward pricing even if another direction was requested; backwardpricing requires a fixed terminal resource value. Direct source-to-sink arcs areincluded as one-arc routes in complete transfer and use the same original rowand objective accounting as other paths. Collection uses a downward resource relaxationthat cannot discard an exact-feasible path, then independently replays originalresources. Negative-consumption equality domains remain unavailable throughthis collector. Unsupported resources, ambiguous canonical replay, global work/path/storage limits or timeout leave the transfer unavailable. Normal pricing remainsusable. Limits apply across all enabled networks, not independently per network.The default candidate limit is 10,000, work limit 10,000,000, stored-arc limit1,000,000 and attempt budget one second. Disabled networks contribute no routes. enumeration_reports distinguishes no attempt, complete transfer and failure.Each report records attempts, per-network counts, route count, newly transferredcolumns and the failure reason. A repeated transfer on a complete snapshot doesnot duplicate columns. Failed transfers do not retain a partial universe.Each solve attempts at most one adaptive transfer, then resumes CG within theoriginal time and iteration limits. Backend transfer failures retain the originalmaster and warm start. A later solve can retry with different enumeration limits.The explicit Rust snapshot.enumerate(...) method attempts transfer immediately. No reduced-cost/objective cutoff removes paths during this collection; coverageis the full supported domain, including incumbent routes. Rust callers can separately request snapshot.enumerate_below(cutoff, &limits)to collect routes needed by integer solutions strictly below a finite objectivecutoff. This returns an immutable CutoffEnumeration, with coverage_cutoff(),report(), routes(), dual_point() and cost_bounds(). Limits cover allnetworks and proof preparation. Missing original-domain bounds, unsupportedresource replay and exhausted budgets return an error; the source snapshotremains usable. This API currently requires a snapshot that has not alreadyinstalled a full enumerated universe. Coupled objective costs are included in proof preparation. A bounded completescalar-path superset can provide a directed route-wide resource-cost lowerbound, which joins the cutoff's once-per-route constant. This preserves routeswhose large scalar cost is offset by a negative resource charge. Full-universecolumn bounds likewise use certified resource-cost lower endpoints. Path andcertificate work share the attempt's budget and deadline; unavailable replayor incomplete coverage leaves the proof unknown. The original integer-routedomain follows its declared physical-simple or finitely bounded-walk contract.Repeated-walk source programs still require independent replay and completecoverage under that cap. Unbounded cyclic domains remain unsupported. Thisscan can be too expensive for large networks. Activity rows and signed paired source objectives use a joint whole-columnbound. A complete bounded path scan encloses each reduced cost, then subtractsan upper enclosure of its additive arc weights to obtain a common routeremainder.
