Shared objective/activity terms therefore remain correlated in thecutoff proof. Collection accepts invariant paired activities or independentlycertified attained endpoints that weakly improve both cost and every row. Signedrow coefficients and inequality senses must agree with the endpoint direction.Equality/opposing rows, identity-specific column caps and uncertain endpointsremain guarded.A residual network cap below one needs no path scan because its integer routequantity must be zero. PWL paired resources and strict-domain slope pairs have independent directedfeasibility witnesses. A cost enclosure can remain non-singleton; finite-MIPproof outcomes still require exact objective encoding. Front-algebrapaired operations, standalone raw slope-interval fronts and plugins retaintheir explicit unsupported-proof behavior. With highs, call view.solve_mip(&MipOptions::default()) on that view. ItsObjectiveCutoff outcome means no integer solution improves the effectivecutoff; it does not mean the original model is infeasible. Time/node limits remain explicit. A cutoff supplied by the callerdoes not itself establish a feasible incumbent. The view cannot be resumed asan original-domain LP or attached to a different snapshot. Its rows, fixedcontributions and caps are frozen; derive a new view from each changed node.The adaptive CG handoff above continues to use full-domain enumeration.When tree enumerated_mip is enabled and full transfer is unavailable, the treetries cutoff enumeration using its validated incumbent or the smaller suppliedMIP cutoff. A failed attempt leaves normal branching available. Numerical modecan close a node from a sufficient MIP bound; certified mode uses returnedwitnesses without promoting a numerical MIP bound to a certificate. The CLI accepts --mip-cutoff X with --tree --enumerated-mip. The matchingJSON solve option is mip_objective_cutoff (finite number, or null for no suppliedcutoff). Reports include coverage_cutoff: null denotes full-domain coverage;a number denotes coverage only below that objective. A cutoff without anincumbent cannot close the original tree merely because its restricted poolhas no improving integer solution.Python's solve(..., tree=True, enumerated_mip=True, mip_objective_cutoff=...) uses the same policy. EachNetworkEnumerationReport.coverage_cutoff identifies the scope of its pool;None means full-domain coverage. With the optional highs feature, the tree can solve a complete transferredcopy as an integer model. Artificial columns are fixed to zero, and routebounds, fleet rows, shared rows, inherited cuts/branches, fixed-route RHScontributions and objective offsets are retained. If LP cleanup retired a route,the private MIP model restores it from the complete universe and reapplies itscap before solving. The original snapshot remains unchanged. Positive integer routes arereplayed against the original graph and original rows before an incumbent ispublished. Source masters and siblings remain unchanged after any MIP outcome. cargo build --offline --features clp,highs --bin baldes
target/debug/baldes solve examples/networks/triangle.json --tree --enumerated-mip --json -
# Force enumeration to decline and normal pricing/branching to continue:
target/debug/baldes solve examples/networks/triangle.json --tree --enumerated-mip --enumeration-route-limit 5 --json -
 --enumerated-mip requires --tree and HiGHS support; it also enables enumeration.--enumeration-time, --mip-time and --mip-nodes control per-attempt budgets.MIP timeout/node limits/backend failure do not authorize pricing termination.enumerated_mip_calls, enumerated_mip_nodes and enumerated_mip_failures reportwork and fallback. Full-MIP numerical proof outcomes may close numerical-modenodes; they never become certified-mode lower-bound certificates. A cutoffwithout a validated witness is not an incumbent or an infeasibility claim. Python uses the same options and reports: from pybaldes import NetworkProblem
problem = NetworkProblem.from_file("examples/networks/triangle.json")
root = problem.solve(enumerate=True)
assert root.enumeration_reports[0].complete
integer = root.snapshot.solve_enumerated_mip(time_limit=1.0)
assert integer.status == "Optimal" and integer.incumbent == 2.0
# Or combine node enumeration and MIP with the tree:
tree = problem.solve(tree=True, enumerated_mip=True)
assert tree.nodes == 1 and tree.incumbent == 2.0
 node.solve(enumerate=True, enumeration_route_limit=..., enumeration_work_limit=..., enumeration_stored_arc_limit=..., enumeration_time_limit=...) prepares a resumednode and returns a new snapshot. solve_enumerated_mip returns None when thenode has not completed transfer. Its optional objective_cutoff filters improvingwitnesses without restricting enumeration; ObjectiveCutoff remains distinctfrom Infeasible. MIP calls on existing Python snapshots keep the GIL and theirthread ownership. Fresh tree calls retain the existing GIL-release behavior. For Python, build with maturin develop --features highs (Clp is enabled bydefault). Clp-only builds still support complete enumeration; they reject MIPrequests explicitly.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Grouped accumulated-resource branches
text:
Grouped accumulated-resource branches A group can span several pricing networks. Name its original shared packing row,one resource coordinate, a stored threshold, and the physical arc IDs belongingto the group in each network. The packing row must prove at most one occurrence:its sense is eq or le, its RHS is at most one, all original contributions arenonnegative, and each member arc has a coefficient of at least one. Signedmaster-variable domains must also preserve nonnegative packing contributions. use baldes::master::model::ResourceGroupMember;
let members = vec![
    ResourceGroupMember { network: 7, arcs: vec![0, 2] },
    ResourceGroupMember { network: 42, arcs: vec![0, 2] },
];
let lower = parent.with_resource_group_branch(0, 0, 1.5, false, &members)?;
let upper = parent.with_resource_group_branch(0, 0, 1.5, true, &members)?;
 Both children include the boundary threshold - 1e-6. The lower child requiresresource usage at most that boundary; the upper child requires usage at leastit. Disposable resources can wait to satisfy an upper window. Equality resourcescannot wait. Restrictions cover every occurrence of each listed physical arc,including parallel alternatives. Other networks and arcs remain available. Shared trees also generate disposable-resource groups automatically from originalunit packing rows. They combine physical occurrences across networks, account forancestor windows and use feasible forward/backward schedule intervals to selecta threshold. Rust callers can inspect the current solved node withparent.resource_group_candidates(1e-6)? and attach either side withcandidate.apply(&parent, upper)?. The tree tries these candidates before itsassignment and aggregate-activity fallbacks. A failed attachment leaves theparent reusable and causes the tree to try another disjunction. Children own their restrictions through solves, further branches, route fixing,enumeration and MIP. Parent and sibling snapshots remain reusable. Retainedschedules refresh under their existing route tags and caps. Fixed schedulesremain fixed; a contradictory child is infeasible. If exact feasibility can beproved but a scalar schedule cannot be reconstructed, attachment returns anerror and preserves the parent. Resource-load rows on a disposable coordinate that an upper branch can re-timerequire complete enumeration before attachment. This keeps the rows' originalpath-load semantics. Call parent.enumerate(&limits) first; the same conditionapplies when adding such a row after a branch. Rows on other coordinates andpath-based additive or registered rows keep their usual workflow. Python exposes the same owned operation: from pybaldes import NetworkResourceGroupMember
members = (NetworkResourceGroupMember(7, (0, 2)),
           NetworkResourceGroupMember(42, (0, 2)))
child = parent.with_resource_group_branch(0, 0, 1.5, True, members)
result = child.solve(stabilize=False)
tree = child.solve(tree=True, stabilize=False)
 For the CLI, pass a JSON array of these restrictions with--resource-branches FILE. Each object has packing_row, resource,threshold, upper and members; each member has network and arcs.The model is restricted before the requested root or tree solve. cargo run --release --features clp --bin baldes -- solve \
  examples/networks/resource_groups.json \
  --resource-branches examples/networks/resource_group_upper.json \
  --tree --bound-mode certified --json -

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Synchronized service across vehicles
text:
Synchronized service across vehicles Pass synchronized_services to a native solve to require simultaneous serviceof a job by several distinct vehicle copies. A member identifies the servicevertex in one pricing network; each service has at most one member per network.A network with multiplicity two can supply two interchangeable vehicles usingtwo copies of the same elementary route. from pybaldes import SynchronizedService, SynchronizedServiceMember

service = SynchronizedService(
    id=17,
    resource=0,                 # scalar service-start time
    vehicles_required=2,
    reward=1.0,                 # counted once, not once per vehicle
    start=(0, 1440),            # inclusive integer domain
    members=(SynchronizedServiceMember(network=7, vertex=17),
             SynchronizedServiceMember(network=42, vertex=8)),
)
result = problem.solve(tree=True, synchronized_services=(service,))
 The native master appends a binary served variable and the coverage equalitysum(visits) = vehicles_required * served. Per-network linking rows additionallyenforce visits_in_network <= min(fleet_size, vehicles_required) * served.This is optional service: an unserved job has no visits. Keep its reward out ofincoming arc costs and remove ordinary unit-cover rows for that job; the solverretains all caller-supplied costs and constraints. Physical fleet limits remainin force. Rust callers set model::Options.synchronized_services; JSON solve optionsaccept the same array of definitions. The CLI accepts--synchronized-services services.json alongside --tree. Synchronization uses an independent disposable resource with nonnegative arcconsumption. Its value at the member vertex must represent service start; putservice duration in outgoing arc consumption. Disjoint service-start windowswork with multi-time-windows. Start domains contain integers between-2**52 and 2**52, inclusive; choose time units to obtain the desired grid.Ordinary pricing-grid limits also apply to resource values.The synchronized coordinate must be a graph scalar resource. Separate coupledresource domains may coexist on participating routes. Resource-load rows onthe synchronized axis are replayed when a start-domain branch changes routeprofiles; fixed-route contributions update the residual row RHS as well. Root solves are LP relaxations and may contain unsynchronized columns. Thenative tree propagates common earliest starts across all selected routes andchecks the complete joint schedule using exact resource replay. When thatcannot certify a witness, it splits a common integer start domain and clipsall participating networks. Restrictions survive snapshot forks, retained andinactive columns, enumeration and fixed routes. Published integer routeprofiles include the common starts. Time and node limits retain open nodes anda relaxation bound; they never turn a failed synchronization check into anincumbent or an infeasibility proof. An LP snapshot can be restricted explicitly withnode.with_synchronized_start(id=17, lower=300, upper=600). Its synchronizationdefinitions are immutable. Complete-domain MIP is deferred while any commonstart domain is non-singleton, since its route-only matrix is then a relaxation. The synchronization example uses optional service variables, multiple networkmembers and common-start restrictions. Local DSN experiments can live underignored working/; they are not distributed interfaces. Use the public Rust,JSON and Python registration contracts in this section for reproducible models. A runnable two-fleet example is included: cargo run --release --features clp -- solve \
  examples/networks/synchronization.json \
  --synchronized-services examples/networks/synchronization-services.json \
  --tree --json -
 Both vehicles start service at time 5; the minimization objective is -1.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Policy controls and registered original variables

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Shared pricing coordination
text: Shared pricing coordination Routing and explicit network input registrations use one pricing coordinator. Routing supplies a one-network collection; network models supplyall enabled networks. Scheduling, deadlines, admission, complete-batch checks,quantity corrections and subgradients use the same implementation. Modeladapters retain cut/NG updates, route-to-row coefficients and original-domaincertificate callbacks. Retained route domains also enter this coordinator;explicit finite masters keep their individual column caps. Live pricing uses the raw objective for both routing and explicit networkregistrations. Correcting only a returned rounded route cannot prove a globalminimum over routes that rounded dominance may have discarded.The routing result's oracle_calls counts actual oracle entries, includingphase-I entries and excluding bound-only skips. It is separate from CGpricing_calls. One live functor entry performs one raw-objective search;it does not first run and discard a cached-objective search. This metric isavailable in Rust, CLI JSON and Python results.

title: Network models and shared masters
heading: Original pricing-variable compilation (Rust)
text:
Original pricing-variable compilation (Rust) compile_pricing_variables(problem, definitions) compiles scopedOriginalPricingVariable registrations into a physical problem and aPricingVariableRegistry. Each registration supplies its network and model ID,original cost, shared-row entries, and (physical_arc_id, coefficient) setters.The final setter for an arc replaces earlier setters for that variable.Different variables, base arc costs, and base row entries remain additive.Expansion uses binary64 coefficients; certificates apply to that compiled model.The registry also retains original-space cost caching. Callregistry.configure_pricing(&mut options) for a Rust root solve; the registry'sbox/tree configuration and JSON/CLI/Python option builders install itautomatically. Each original reduced cost is rounded to1e-8 before applying itsassociation coefficients, matching the reference cache order. Base arc costsremain separate. The raw compiled physical objective is priced independentlyfor proof safety; a rounded-cache optimum alone cannot certify the raw model.Immutable metadata is shared across node forks and retained by default resumes;window compilation copies its physical arc associations. Appended shared rowscontribute their explicit physical-arc dual terms. Replacing the compiledcoefficient prefix falls back to ordinary physical caching and raw pricing. Signed associations retain their algebra in costs, shared rows and reportedactivities. A negative lower endpoint of an original-variable envelope remainsnegative for an optional network: choosing no route does not exclude itsnegative-activity routes. Graph feasibility still determines which activitiesare possible. The registry retains canonical expressions independently of route tags.registry.activity(network, id, &output) reports an outward Bounds enclosureat the current LP point, including fixed copies. integer: true requests anoriginal aggregate branch registration after the existing integer-path proof;call registry.configure_tree(&mut tree_options) to add those registrations.It rejects name conflicts before editing the options. Generated names areX_<network>_<id> and can be used with generator direction controls. Original-variable bounds must be encoded in the pricing graph. This compilerdoes not turn them into a global master restriction or add an implicit resource.Optional original-variable pricing envelopes can now be attached through theregistry with configure_boxes(&mut options, &[OriginalVariableBound { ... }]).The JSON/Python option is original_variable_boxes; the CLI accepts--original-variable-boxes FILE, containing an array such as: [{"network": 7, "id": 0, "lower": 0, "upper": 1}]
 These endpoints must already enclose the registered activity on every feasiblepricing walk. They do not impose a new graph restriction. The verifier usesweighted DAG walk ranges, bounded cyclic walks, or matching scalar-resourcebounds; it rejects unsupported or unaffordable proofs. Omitted upper bounds areunbounded. The declared endpoints remain unchanged after verification. Registered original variables also use independent default [0, +infinity]admission envelopes when graph analysis proves their activities nonnegative.This applies without an explicit original_variable_boxes option. Explicitenvelopes take precedence. A signed mapping whose nonnegativity cannot beproved keeps its graph domain and falls back to physical residual bounds oractual pricing; registration never clips a negative activity to zero. Admission evaluates the original variables independently, even when their costscancel on shared physical arcs. It adds an outward residual bound for base arccosts, row edits and rounding. Overlapping associations therefore do not doublecount physical costs. Existing witness, phase and complete-master-gap gatesstill apply; unsupported nonlinear/coupled pricing falls back to the oracle.Registry-backed node snapshots, tree forks and window copies retain theseexpressions. Rust SolveOptions callers with original-variable references usenode_options_with_registry or tree_options_with_registry; the builderswithout a registry reject unresolved references. Model JSON now accepts a top-level pricing_variables array with the sameregistration fields. The CLI and Python model frontend compile it once beforesolving. Python NetworkProblem.pricing_variables carries these declarations;its node handles retain the registry across row edits, fixing, resumes andsubsequent tree solves. Results report original_variables entries withnetwork, id, lower, and upper activity bounds. Tree/MIP results reportactivities only when an incumbent is available. Fresh-root and tree compilationuse the original physical arc IDs; restored tree paths are used for reporting.Rust callers needing both the physical problem and registry can useformat::Model::compile(); problem() returns only the compiled problem. For an accumulated custom/cumulative resource, supplyaccumulated_resource: <descriptor index> instead of arcs: {"network": 42, "id": 37, "cost": 2,
 "accumulated_resource": 1, "entries": [[0, 1]]}
 The variable denotes the descriptor's intrinsic accumulated charge on eachroute. Its cost replaces that descriptor's implicit unit objective coefficient;it does not scale numeric resource states or dependent resource constraints.Zero and signed costs retain the intrinsic activity for shared rows and resultreporting. Each descriptor can have one such original-variable registration.The original identity and intrinsic expression survive resumes and tree forks.Cost-bearing paired descriptors in either representation can also bind this field when theirnormalization is absolute_final_value. Negative original costs require a sourcedomain and use independently bounded maximum controls through the same masterpricing coordinator; model costs and shared-row coefficients remain distinct.Their primal activity is read from selected column values throughOriginalColumn / activity_from_columns; arc-only reporting is insufficient.Source-domain paired registrations support shared entries, including signedcoefficients and row duals that reverse the reduced objective. Pricing coversbounded physical paths, bounds terminal controls in each source region andretains distinct selected values through the common master coordinator.Unfinished path/control coverage is incomplete, never an infeasibility proof.Source paired bindings support the integer/envelope contracts below as well.Every base control must have integral terminal activity; integer extrema of acontinuous range are insufficient. Machine-front integer activities, negativeobjectives/rows and unproved boxes remain unsupported.Accumulated registrations accept integer: true when a program or complete-pathproof establishes exact integer activity. They register X_<network>_<id>through the same mapped-variable tree path, including activity branch rows andfresh/resumed trees. Unsupported or ambiguous domain proofs are rejected.Explicit original_variable_boxes areverified against a complete bounded scalar-path relaxation with independentcoupled feasibility and intrinsic activity certificates. Source paired envelopescover all terminal controls, with independent declared-bound tightening of LPenclosures. They retain signedendpoints and remain independent of master rows and objective coefficients.If a complete scan is unavailable, the integer-program proof can supply aconservative envelope on a DAG or explicitly bounded walk domain. Source pairedprograms with constant integer increments/clamps and zero waiting also admitan inductive terminal-window proof on cycles. A registration proof does notestablish complete pricing coverage of a cyclic domain. A requestedbox must enclose that entire proved range. Otherwise incomplete scans andambiguous certificates reject the requested envelope.Verified envelopes can also supply a coupled admission estimate on DAGs andexplicitly bounded walks. It combines the original transition-program objectivebound, conservative physical costs and outward shared-row arithmetic using theactual duals. It retains required network quantities and the existing master-gapand witness gates. Missing activity envelopes, unsupported nonlinear rows,unavailable objective proofs or exhausted budgets fall back to ordinary pricing. Networks can also supply activity_entries, an array of{"resource": 1, "row": 0, "coefficient": 1} objects, to add intrinsiccustom/cumulative activity directly to shared rows. These terms add to arc,per-route and other activity coefficients. Compilation retains them in thephysical Network, so Model::problem() preserves their solving semanticseven when the reporting registry is discarded. Numerical pricing and boundedcomplete-column certificates account for their dual terms separately from theoriginal objective. Certificates return an unresolved bound when their completepath scan exceeds its work or path budget. The same whole-column certificate also covers other coupled objectives whentheir resource interpreter supplies a proof. It keeps each path's physicalcost, resource charge and shared-row contributions together. Independentlyminimizing those parts can leave a weaker bound because the minima may belongto different paths. The joint scan uses half the caller's remaining logical work as its path,scan and stored-arc allowance, reserving the rest for source replay. It has noseparate fixed 4,096-path or 250,000-scan ceiling. An unavailable proof retainsthe existing conservative relaxation. Complete-domain route caps use the samecolumn evaluator. Prepared SlopePaired models with front_algebra operationscan explicitly select front_program_domain for machine-front certificates;that choice does not assert an exact-real source-domain proof. For explicit paired source choices, Route::with_paired_controls independentlychecks controls and reconstructs their original objective from the recipientresource program. NodeSnapshot::with_route_controls retains an alternativecolumn through the shared route pool. Scalar schedules and selected pairedvalues define route identity; equivalent source controls reuse one column. Recipient replay, fixed reductions,integer witnesses and original-variable reporting use those stored controls.Controlled charges replace ordinary paired charges at the same position in theobjective sum: numeric/front charges, slope pairs, then control-point pairs.Equivalent witnesses therefore preserve both column identity and binary64 cost.Correlated reduced-cost bounds follow that order, including independentlyenclosed uncontrolled paired charges and their declared normalization.Graph coefficients may also be negative with final-minus-initialnormalization in a source-domain Clp model. JSON/Python networks expose thesame setter as coupled_objective_coefficients, an array of[resource_index, coefficient] pairs. A resource bound to an original pricingvariable obtains its cost from that variable; declaring a graph cost for thesame resource is rejected. Graph costs on other resources survive variablecompilation. The source bound subtracts anindependently enclosed global initial-front minimum before applying the signedcoefficient. This graph-level objective does not redefine original pricingvariables or activity rows: their paired bindings still require absolutephysical terminal values.An already complete/cutoff universe cannot be widened; a missing controlledidentity cannot be fixed by aliasing its minimum-value physical path. Ordinaryminimum-front pricing is unchanged for models without paired rows. With sourcepaired rows, automatic pricing supplies minimum, maximum and row-boundarycontrol proposals and an independently bounded reduced cost. A bounded jointterminal LP also proposes controls satisfying several paired rows together.Global recovery can couple physical paths and networks, preserving fixed andbackground routes and signed master-variable contributions. Registered or newlyqueried points, including integer copy blocks at neighboring dyadic Gammavalues, can recover a witness when physical-path counts are integral; exact whole-modelreplay and column caps decide acceptance. These proposals do not prove coverageof varying controls. Enumeration ofpaired rows or negative objectives succeeds when each relevant terminal valuehas a singleton all-control proof on every retained path. This also coversfractional invariant values. Checked source controls survive transfer, fixingand finite-master replay. A varying resource may also retain an independentlycertified attained endpoint when its objective and all rows agree on a direction:negative costs favor maxima, positive costs minima, and zero costs either.Increasing Gamma helps positive lower-bound rows and negative upper-bound rows;decreasing Gamma reverses those signs. Equality rows, opposing requirements,identity-specific column caps and unattained endpoints remain guarded. Thisprojection preserves current-model feasibility and optimality, rather than everycontinuous control identity. Source LP row normalization removes a common factoronly when every quotient is exact; endpoint attainment never uses a tolerance.Adding a paired row to a full universe requires invariant matching values orproof that its existing endpoints still dominate for all old/new rows and theobjective. All terms in the pending row are checked together. Retained identitycaps may block projection, and fixed copies need independent point certificates.A cutoff universe cannot be widened. Finite MIP proof outcomes additionallyrequire singleton original activity coefficients, including coefficients thatrounded replay stored as zero. NodeSnapshot::optimize_route_control generates a paired source choice on aregistered physical path, using the common master::controls engine. The enginecompiles exact guarded PWL/clamp region matrices, verifies finite LP bounds andindependently checks candidate controls. It supports physical minimum/maximumand terminal-value restrictions. Complete region coverage and the returnedprimal/dual enclosure are distinct from an exact selector or a whole-modelpricing certificate. Budget/arithmetic limits remain unknown. Generated controlscan be retained with with_route_controls; paired shared-row pricing uses thissame optimizer under a shared query budget.

title: Shared-master network models
heading: Shared-master network models
text: Shared-master network models pyBaldes documentation · Results Use independent pricing networks when several route families contribute to thesame master constraints. Network IDs identify fleets or families; they need notbe consecutive. Arc IDs and vertex IDs are local to a network. Shared-row IDsare positions in NetworkProblem.rows, starting at zero.

title: Shared-master network models
heading: One network or a collection
text:
One network or a collection Use the same solve function for scalar and array inputs: from pybaldes import PricingArc, PricingNetwork, solve

network = PricingNetwork(
    id=7, vertices=3, multiplicity=(0, 1),
    arcs=(PricingArc(0, 1, -2), PricingArc(1, 2, 0)),
)
a = solve(network, stabilize=False)
b = solve([network], stabilize=False)
assert a.lp == b.lp == -2
assert a.oracle_calls == b.oracle_calls
 Pass rows=rows with a scalar/array, or use NetworkProblem(rows, networks).The latter accepts a scalar network or an array and always stores a tuple.pricing_variables optionally registers original pricing-variable mappings;see the model compilation contract.

title: Shared-master network models
heading: Build a complete model
text:
Build a complete model from pybaldes import (
    NetworkProblem, PricingArc, PricingNetwork, PricingResource, SharedRow,
)

problem = NetworkProblem(
    rows=[SharedRow("eq", 1.0)],
    networks=[PricingNetwork(
        id=19, vertices=3, multiplicity=(0.0, 1.0),
        arcs=[
            PricingArc(0, 1, 2.0, consumption=(1.0,), entries=((0, 1.0),)),
            PricingArc(1, 2, 1.0, consumption=(0.0,)),
        ],
        resources=[PricingResource(bounds=((0.0, 2.0),) * 3)],
    )],
)
root = problem.solve(stabilize=False)
assert root.status == "Optimal" and root.lp == 3.0
print(root.routes[0].network, root.routes[0].nodes)
 NetworkRoute.coupled_values is an immutable tuple of paired descriptor/valuepairs retained with the scalar resource_profile. Values describe the currentselected physical dependent state, independently of objective normalization;they are not full control trajectories or standalone feasibility certificates. The only covering route costs 3, contributes one unit to shared row 0, consumesone load unit, and uses one copy of network 19's allowed route multiplicity.problem.solve(**options) delegates to solve(problem, **options).Both require Clp.

title: Shared-master network models
heading: Model reference
text: Model reference Type Fields and defaults SharedRow sense, rhs; sense is "eq", "le", or "ge" PricingResource kind="disposable", initial=None, bounds=None, time_windows=None PricingArc tail, head, cost, consumption=(), bounds=(), entries=() PricingNetwork id, vertices, multiplicity, arcs, resources=(), source=0, sink=None, route_entries=(), activity_entries=(), ng=None, coupled_resources=(), coupled_objective_coefficients=(), paired_waiting_base_resources=(), paired_machine_inputs=(), paired_machine_roots=(), paired_machine_terminal_bounds=(), elementary=False, route_domain=None, front_program_domain=False NetworkProblem rows, scalar/array networks, optional pricing_variables Scalar kind accepts "disposable" or "equality". Resource bounds has one(lower, upper) pair per vertex when supplied; initial overrides the sourceinitial value. Optional windows are described in resources.PricingArc.consumption follows scalar coordinate order. Arc bounds entriesare optional (lower, upper) pairs constraining head states. entries contains(shared_row_index, coefficient) pairs for that arc. For a route p in network k, an additive shared-row coefficient is the sum of itsarc entries plus route_entries once per route. Multiplicity (lower, upper)bounds the sum of route variables in that network. Shared coverage rows andfleet multiplicity are different constraints. sink=None selects the lastvertex. ng supplies per-vertex neighborhoods; elementary=True selects anelementary network domain. coupled_resources accepts tagged descriptors. paired_waiting_base_resources=((coupled_index, scalar_index), ...) opts aslope_paired resource into waiting windows derived from the correspondingscalar resource. Each physical arc's window intersects its head vertex boundswith the arc bounds; absent arc bounds use -1e12 and 1e12. Indices refer tocoupled_resources and resources, respectively. Duplicate coupled indices,invalid indices, empty intersections, and scalar resources with multi-timewindows are rejected. The equivalent CLI JSON field uses arrays of pairs,for example "paired_waiting_base_resources": [[0, 1]]. An omitted or emptyfield leaves the paired resource's existing waiting behavior unchanged. paired_machine_inputs=((coupled_index, arc_inputs), ...) attaches exactprepared machine operands to a slope_paired resource using front_algebra.arc_inputs contains one mapping per physical arc in insertion order. Eachmapping supplies finite tail_limit, head_limit, waiting_lower,waiting_upper, integer waiting_rate, and forward_mapping, inverse,sum_vector, dependent_lower, and dependent_upper functions. Encode eachfunction as {"pairs": [[value, coordinate], [slope, end], ...]}. Themachine decoder also accepts a zero-width two-pair vector and a three-pairvector with a zero-width first segment. The waiting limits must be ordered. Resourceindices must be unique and each arc vector must match the graph's arc count.An arc may also include a backward mapping with tail_lower, tail_upper,forward_at_tail_lower, mapped_upper, and dependent (a prepared functionin the same pairs format). These are the separate operands needed by thebackward recurrence, which remains incomplete.These inputs invalidate prepared pricing state when changed. Whenfront_program_domain is enabled, the incomplete machine path uses them andalso requires paired_machine_roots=((coupled_index, {"pairs": [...]}), ...)with the separately prepared dependent root vector. The equivalent JSON field isan array of [coupled_index, arc_inputs] pairs. An omitted field defaults toempty. To initialize backward machine labels, supplypaired_machine_terminal_bounds=((coupled_index, (lower, upper)), ...) withthe prepared terminal base window. The associated arc operands must alreadybe supplied in paired_machine_inputs. coupled_objective_coefficients=((resource_index, coefficient), ...) setsgraph-level costs using each descriptor's declared normalization. With Clp,negative source paired costs support both absolute and final-minus-initialnormalization. A relative objective subtracts the global initial-front minimum,independently of the witness's initial coordinate. Each resource has one costowner: omit its graph coefficient when an original pricing_variables entrybinds that resource. Duplicate indices, unsupported descriptors and nonfinitecoefficients are rejected by the common graph setter. Omitted resources keepcoefficient one. The field works for one network and arrays of networks. The Rust interface additionally supports independent master variables andimported-column domains. Those registrations are not fields in the CLI/Pythonnetwork JSON schema. pricing_variables registers original pricing-variableidentities; it does not add arbitrary static master variables. See theshared model guide and column importsfor the Rust-only contracts. An original variable can use accumulated_resource instead of arcs to bindthe intrinsic charge of a custom/cumulative coupled descriptor. Its costreplaces the descriptor's unit objective coefficient; entries adds thatintrinsic activity to shared rows. Reported activity remains independent of theobjective coefficient. Accumulated registrations support continuous variables,integer registrations with complete exact-integer path proofs, and explicitoriginal-variable boxes whose envelopes can be certifiedover the complete bounded graph relaxation. Direct networkactivity_entries use objects with resource, row and coefficient fields.See original variable compilationfor the shared contract. accumulated_resource also accepts cost-bearing paired descriptors (raw slopes or control points) withabsolute_final_value normalization and a finite cost. Negative costs requirea source-domain model and use maximum-control pricing. The reportedvalue comes from the selected column, independently of the cost coefficient.For this paired binding, entries supports signed shared-row coefficients insource-domain models. integer=True is accepted when a program or completecontrol-domain proof establishes integral terminal activity for every control.Continuous ranges with integral endpoints are rejected. Verifiedoriginal_variable_boxes enclose all controls, including nonminimum choices;they are envelopes, not new model restrictions. Automatic pricing covers finitephysical paths and independently bounds alternative source controls. Incompletecoverage remains explicit. Machine-front integer activities/negative objectivesand rows remain unsupported.

title: Shared-master network models
heading: Model JSON
text:
Model JSON from pathlib import Path
from pybaldes import NetworkProblem

text = problem.to_json(indent=2)
restored = NetworkProblem.from_json(text)
assert restored == problem
Path("model.json").write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
restored = NetworkProblem.from_file("model.json")
 The same model format is accepted by baldes solve model.json. JSON rejectsnon-finite numeric literals; an unlimited multiplicity upper bound uses nullas described in the shared model contract. Synchronization definitions are solve options, not fields inNetworkProblem.to_json(); save them separately for reproducibility.

title: Shared-master network models
heading: Solve controls
text:
Solve controls All options to solve are keyword-only. Keyword Default Meaning tree False Solve a root LP or search a shared-master integer tree network_pricing_schedule "full-sweep" full-sweep, cyclic, sorted, promising-first, unvisited-first network_unpromising_limit 1 Positive queue batch budget network_branching "multiplicity-first" multiplicity-first, resource-first or phased branching policy stabilize True Dual smoothing when no explicit proximal configuration replaces it proximal None Explicit proximal bands and optional multi-point policy bound_mode "numerical" Numerical or certified lower bounds artificial_cost 2.76 Positive artificial-column configuration; not an incumbent bound time_limit 120.0 Solve time budget in seconds max_iterations 100000 Column-generation iteration limit node_limit 10000 Tree node limit log_interval None Optional positive progress interval pricing_options None Numeric BALDES option mapping synchronized_services () Common-start optional service definitions A schedule changes which networks are priced first; early improving columns donot establish that all networks have completed pricing. The solver coordinatesthe complete pricing checkpoint needed for bounds. Example proximal configuration: root = problem.solve(
    network_pricing_schedule="promising-first",
    proximal={"bands": [{"half_width": 0.5, "penalty": 1.0}], "multi_point": True},
)
 penalty=None selects a hard band. Use positive validated widths/penalties;see proximal pricing for the mathematicalcontract. Root and tree APIs have different option sets from routingsolve; there is no master_solver keyword here.

title: Shared-master network models
heading: Additional tree and stabilization controls
text: Additional tree and stabilization controls Keyword Default Behavior network_promising_limit 1000000 Promising-network queue budget stabilization_max_tree_depth 10000 Disable stabilization at this depth network_tree_search "default" default, best-bound, bound-priority, depth-bound-priority network_strategy2_rounding "unrounded" Queue-key rounding: unrounded, guarded-tolerance, exact-ceil network_open_node_limit 1000 Primary frontier capacity before overflow network_scoring_gap_tolerance 1e-6 Absolute branch-score gap tolerance network_search_inactive_columns False Reprice retained inactive columns before another oracle call network_share_inactive_columns False Reprice columns shared by tree nodes/trials network_branch_priorities None Named branch-family priority mapping network_branch_directions None Named generator directions for phased branching mapped_variables () Registered original aggregate branch variables packing None Packing-assignment registration variable_boxes / original_variable_boxes () Verified variable envelopes mapped_strong_branching True Evaluate admitted mapped branch proposals in trials These controls configure the shared lifecycle's model registration. Networkcount does not select another engine. Routing-specific Python keywords belongto routing input; a scalar PricingNetwork uses these model controls.

title: Shared-master network models
heading: Resume, branch, and add rows
text:
Resume, branch, and add rows A root result owns a NetworkNode snapshot. Child operations return new nodesand preserve their parent. Handles are bound to their creating Python thread. from pybaldes import NetworkRowCoefficients, SharedRow

root = problem.solve()
parent = root.snapshot
assert parent is not None
# Add an additive row requiring at least one route across the networks.
coefficients = tuple(
    NetworkRowCoefficients(n.id, (0.0,) * len(n.arcs), per_route=1.0)
    for n in problem.networks
)
child = parent.with_row(SharedRow("ge", 1.0), coefficients)
child_result = child.solve(stabilize=False)
assert parent.solve().lp == root.lp
 NetworkRowCoefficients(network, arcs, per_route=0.0, activities=()) suppliesone coefficient per physical arc and optional (coupled_descriptor, coefficient)activity terms. The constant is charged once per route. Deterministic activitiesand selected source paired values use the same with_row lifecycle, includingdynamic=True. These terms apply to existing and future columns. An existingcomplete universe accepts a paired term only after an all-control invarianceproof confirms that its retained coefficients remain valid. parent.fractional_assignments(tolerance=1e-6) returns NetworkAssignmentobjects with shared_row, network, and value. A candidate can be branched: for candidate in parent.fractional_assignments():
    assigned = parent.branch_assignment(candidate.shared_row, candidate.network, True)
    excluded = parent.branch_assignment(candidate.shared_row, candidate.network, False)
    print(assigned.solve().status, excluded.solve().status)
    break
 Use candidate IDs from the solved snapshot and supported original assignmentrows. Arbitrary shared rows need not define assignment disjunctions.fix_route(route_index, quantity=1) fixes a route using the snapshot's routehandle. quantity must be a positive Python integer at most 2**53; booleansand fractional values are rejected. Use a non-None route_index from thatsnapshot's routes, not an index into an unrelated result. with_resource_group_branch(packing_row, resource, threshold, upper, members)accepts NetworkResourceGroupMember(network, arcs) objects. The original packingrow must establish at most one occurrence. The operation has resource replayand row compatibility preconditions, including enumeration for some resource-loadrows. See grouped branchesfor the shared boundary convention and restrictions.

title: Shared-master network models
heading: Integer search
text:
Integer search from pybaldes import NetworkProblem

# Bundled example, run from the repository root.
triangle = NetworkProblem.from_file("examples/networks/triangle.json")
root = triangle.solve(stabilize=False)
integer = triangle.solve(tree=True, time_limit=30, node_limit=1000)
assert root.lp == 1.5
assert integer.incumbent == 2.0
print(integer.status, integer.bound, integer.open_nodes)
 root.snapshot.solve(tree=True, ...) starts a tree from that node's inheritedstate. Automatic search supports its documented branching families and mayreturn Incomplete when they do not resolve the model. A tree result has noresumable node snapshot. An incumbent remains distinct from a lower bound.

title: Shared-master network models
heading: Enumeration and integer transfer
text:
Enumeration and integer transfer Keyword Default Meaning enumerate False Attempt full route-universe transfer at a valid pricing checkpoint enumeration_route_limit 10000 Candidate route budget across networks enumeration_work_limit 10000000 Collection/proof work budget enumeration_stored_arc_limit 1000000 Stored route-arc budget enumeration_time_limit 1.0 Per-attempt time budget in seconds enumerated_mip False Use optional HiGHS integer transfer mip_time_limit 1.0 Per-MIP time budget mip_node_limit 100000 Per-MIP node budget mip_objective_cutoff None Optional finite improvement cutoff root = triangle.solve(enumerate=True)
for report in root.enumeration_reports:
    print(report.complete, report.routes, report.failure, report.coverage_cutoff)
 Full transfer commits only when every enabled network completes. Unsupportedresources, ambiguous replay, or exhausted limits leave normal pricing availableand do not install a partial universe. A failed attempt may be retried by a latersolve with different limits. NetworkNode.solve_enumerated_mip(time_limit=1.0, node_limit=100000, objective_cutoff=None) solves an available transferred copyand may return None when unprepared. HiGHS support is required for integer solving. With tree=True, enumerated_mip=True, the solver can use full transfer or acutoff-bounded improvement domain. Inspect each report's coverage_cutoff:None means full-domain coverage; a number restricts coverage to improvementsbelow it. Failure to improve an arbitrary cutoff is not original-modelinfeasibility and does not supply a feasible incumbent. Independent certificatesand numerical MIP bounds remain distinct. See theenumeration contract.

title: Shared-master network models
heading: Synchronized optional service
text:
Synchronized optional service SynchronizedService(id, resource, vehicles_required, reward, start, members)defines a job served by distinct vehicle copies at a common integer service start.Members are SynchronizedServiceMember(network, vertex) values. Service isoptional and its reward is counted once in the master, so exclude that rewardfrom route arc costs and remove ordinary unit-cover rows for this job. from pybaldes import SynchronizedService, SynchronizedServiceMember

fleets = NetworkProblem((), tuple(
    PricingNetwork(
        id=n, vertices=3, multiplicity=(0, 1),
        arcs=(PricingArc(0, 1, 0), PricingArc(1, 2, 0)),
        resources=(PricingResource(initial=0, bounds=((0, 0), window, (0, 100))),),
    ) for n, window in ((7, (0, 9)), (42, (5, 10)))
))
service = SynchronizedService(
    id=17, resource=0, vehicles_required=2, reward=1,
    start=(0, 10),
    members=(SynchronizedServiceMember(7, 1), SynchronizedServiceMember(42, 1)),
)
result = fleets.solve(tree=True, synchronized_services=(service,))
assert result.incumbent == -1
assert all(r.resource_profile[1][0] == 5 for r in result.routes)
 The synchronized resource must be disposable with nonnegative consumption.Put service duration on outgoing arcs. Start bounds are inclusive integers in[-2**52, 2**52]; the unit determines the time grid. The synchronized axis isa graph scalar resource; separate coupled resources may coexist. Resource-loadrows on the same axis are refreshed when synchronized start domains change.The routing registration accepts bounded walks without cuts; its automatic cutfamilies require a hard vertex elementarity group on every interior vertex.That restriction belongs to routing cut hooks and is independent of network count.Root LP columns need not form a synchronized schedule; the tree validates thejoint integer witness. A snapshot's service definitions are immutable. Narrow a start domain withwith_synchronized_start(id, lower, upper); parents remain reusable. CompleteMIP is deferred while common start domains are non-singleton. Thesynchronization contractexplains coverage equations and schedule validation. Original-variable pricing envelopes can be passed to solve or a node solve: result = problem.solve(
    original_variable_boxes=({"network": 7, "id": 0, "lower": 0, "upper": 1},),
)
 Each identity must occur in problem.pricing_variables. The bound must alreadyfollow from the pricing graph; an unproved envelope raises an error. Thesebounds guide pricing admission without adding a route restriction. Originalvariable costs remain separate during this calculation even if they cancel onshared physical arcs. See the compilation contract. Explicit source choices can be retained for an existing route withnode.with_route_controls(route_index, (PairedControl(resource, base), ...)).base contains the initial coordinate and one head coordinate per arc. Theresult is a new node; duplicate identities are reused. Controls need independentsingleton source certificates, and complete/cutoff universes and machine-frontmodel domains reject this operation. route.coupled_controls is an immutabletuple of PairedControl objects. Values and costs survive resume, fixing andtree solving; original-variable reporting reads the supplied selected value.Models without paired rows retain ordinary minimum-front pricing. Paired rowsuse the same master coordinator with bounded source-control generation, includingreversed reduced weights and row-boundary proposals. Complete enumeration retains invariant terminal values or a certified attainedendpoint that weakly improves both the objective and every row. Negative costsfavor maxima, positive costs minima, and zero costs either direction, subjectto all row signs and inequality senses. Equality rows, opposing requirements,identity-specific column caps, and uncertain/unattained bounds remain guarded.A new Gamma row may reuse invariant matching values or the same certifiedendpoints when they still favor the objective and every old/new row. Repeatedterms are checked together; restrictive retained-column caps and fixed-copycertificates remain part of the proof. Opposing/equality rows requiring othercontrols cannot widen the projected universe. Negative model costs use the same bounded source-control optimizer;machine-front negative models remain unsupported. node.optimize_route_control(route_index, resource, maximize=False, terminal=None, max_cells=4096, max_work=1_000_000, max_lp_iterations=10000, time_limit=1.0) generates a source control on oneregistered path. terminal=(lower, upper) restricts its physical dependentvalue. It returns an immutable ControlOptimization with control, dependent,work_used, lp_iterations,lower_bound, complete, maximize and cells. choice = node.optimize_route_control(route_index, 0, terminal=(4.0, 4.0))
if choice.control is not None:
    node = node.with_route_controls(route_index, (choice.control,))
 Every returned control has an independent source certificate. complete=Truemeans all regions were bounded/rejected and a feasible control was found, orall regions were proved empty. It does not assert a zero primal/dual gap.lower_bound applies to Gamma, or -Gamma when maximizing. An incomplete resultcan retain a useful feasible control; it cannot assert infeasibility. This is afixed-path descriptor search, not a whole-model pricing certificate. Its limitsare shared across LP regions. Machine-front models reject the source search.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Finite column imports
text: Finite column imports Documentation index With clp, Rust callers can import finite column domains throughmaster::model::imported. Routing networks are optional. Importedcolumns are original-vector patterns, so this interface also supports finitenon-routing models without constructing synthetic routes.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Model contract
text: Model contract Supply the ordinary shared Problem<D>, original MasterVariable definitionsand a list of imported::Subproblem definitions. Each subproblem declares: A nonnegative ID, distinct from other imported subproblems and routing IDs. The original variable IDs in its coordinate support. Nonnegative total multiplicity bounds, with an optional infinite upper bound. Its complete declared list of columns. Each imported::Column has a local ID, additional objective cost, nonnegativequantity bounds, an integrality flag and coalesced (original_variable_id, coefficient) entries. IDs need only be unique within their subproblem. Entriesmay be signed or fractional. An omitted entry has coefficient zero. For every original variable declared by any imported subproblem, the interfaceadds the equality x = sum(coefficient * column_quantity) over all participatingimports. Several subproblems may contribute to the same original variable.Declared supports with no columns still imply zero contribution. Originalvariables outside all imported supports remain independent master variables.Original shared rows and original-variable bounds constrain these aggregatevalues. Routing networks continue to contribute their own ordinary shared-rowcoefficients. The objective includes both original-variable costs and each column's additionalcost. To supply the whole pattern cost in Column::cost, set the correspondingoriginal-variable costs to zero. If an original variable represents a nonlinearper-pattern feature, callers supply that feature's actual coefficient in eachcolumn; this interface does not discover or separate nonlinear cuts. The declared columns define this finite domain. Importing a subset of anexternal pricing problem does not establish completeness for that largerproblem. Every declared column is loaded immediately; this is not a dynamicpricing callback.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Solving and restricting snapshots

title: Finite column imports
heading: Extending a declared domain
text: Extending a declared domain node.solve_with_columns(subproblem_id, additional_columns, options) solves anew declared model containing the old and additional columns. IDs must be newwithin that existing subproblem, and entries must use its declared originalcoordinate support. Repeated extensions are supported; duplicate IDs andinvalid definitions are errors that leave the parent usable. Explicit with_variable_bounds, with_column_bounds, with_multiplicity,with_routing_multiplicity, with_row, with_presence_row,with_registered_cut_row, with_composite_cut_row,with_resource_knapsack_row and fix_routerestrictions survive the rebuild. They are replayed by original IDs andqualified column IDs, so a changed internal allocation does not retarget a fix.with_multiplicity addresses imported groups; with_routing_multiplicityaddresses total route use in a routing subproblem. fix_route(route_index, quantity)fixes additional integer copies of a registered routing path. Rebuilds preserveits physical arc path and quantity, subtract its contribution from every sharedrow and remaining route multiplicity, and retain its objective contribution.Fixed copies still count against group multiplicity and contribute their costsand original vectors. Ordinary low-level child snapshots obtained throughnode.node() are separate objects; only the import wrapper's explicitrestrictions are replayed by this extension operation. Use node.with_row(row, routing_coefficients, original_coefficients) to add ashared restriction. Original coefficients are (original_variable_id, value)pairs; generated imported-column IDs are rejected. Routing coefficients usemodel::RowCoefficients, with physical arc order and an optionalonce-per-route term. Omitted coordinates and routing families contribute zero.Coefficients must be finite and coalesced. The caller supplies a valid cut orbranch restriction. Original-coordinate links apply the row to new importedvectors automatically. Rebuilds replay the row and subtract any fixed routingcontribution, whether the row was added before or after fixing. node.with_presence_row(row, presence_coefficients, original_coefficients)couples nonlinear routing-event presence to original coordinates. It usesmodel::PresenceCoefficients, with event lists aligned to physicalarcs, and supports both pair-count and any-pair semantics. The originalpresence descriptor survives extension. Fixed routes contribute their exactpresence coefficient before preprocessing the rebuilt model; imported vectorscontribute through the specified original-coordinate coefficients. The import snapshot and multi-group session also exposewith_registered_cut_row(row, routing, original),with_composite_cut_row(row, routing, original) andwith_resource_knapsack_row(row, routing, original). These accept the sameregistered cut or resource-load descriptors as ordinary routing snapshots,plus coefficients on original imported coordinates. Composite rows sum everysupplied kernel, including repeated descriptors on one routing group. Resourcerows retain the routing adapter's monotone binary-grid load and <= requirements.Their descriptors survive source batches, phase-I recovery, domain extensionand tree descendants. Original-domain certificates may remain weak for thesekernels. A correct restricted LP does not establish certified optimality; completerouting enumeration can supply the finite-domain proof after external sourcesare complete. Rebuilds install all routing kernels before replayingfixed-route contributions or running preprocessing. Callers remain responsiblefor the validity of the supplied row. Adding columns can invalidate bounds, zero fixings and infeasibility deductionsmade from the previous finite domain. The implementation therefore retains theoriginal input definition, rebuilds the model, replays explicit restrictions andreruns preprocessing and routing pricing. It starts with unknown lower boundsand discards old certificates, smoothing, cached columns and derived bounds.Even a zero-time solve of the expanded domain cannot inherit a narrower-domaincertificate. The supplied options configure this fresh solve. An empty additionresumes the unchanged snapshot and preserves its valid bounds. This operation rebuilds and reloads the declared model; it is not an incrementalpricing callback or a claim that an external pricing problem is exhausted. Theoriginal definition is retained once and shared between snapshots for thispurpose. Callers obtain values through the returned output's new identity map. node.node() exposes the ordinary immutable snapshot for preprocessing, trees,additional shared rows and MIP. Use node.values(&output.master_values) to decodevalues returned by those operations on this snapshot's descendants. Root solvesrelax declared integrality; tree or MIP enforces it. Pure imports have a completecolumn domain immediately, so solve_enumerated_mip needs no enumeration step.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Incremental domain sources

title: Finite column imports
heading: Numerical pricing requests
text: Numerical pricing requests session.pricing(options) optimizes the currently known restricted master andreturns ImportPricing. It disables finite-domain preprocessing, smoothing andenumeration so deductions from the known columns cannot become assumptionsabout future columns. A pricing point carries no bound or completion flag. point.costs() exports an ImportCosts objective: additional column cost plusper_column plus the sum of each original vector entry times its coordinateprice. The constant includes base and explicit multiplicity restrictions.point.reduced_cost(column) validates a proposed new, zero-lower-bound columnand evaluates its numerical reduced cost with the same reconstructed row maps.Original-coordinate objective costs enter through these duals; do not add thema second time. These are numerical search signals, not certified lower bounds. point.reduced_cost_bounds(column) returns an enclosure of that candidate'sexact-real reduced cost at the stored binary64 dual point. Exact expansionspreserve cancellation; directed intervals handle fractional underflow. Nonemeans arithmetic could not establish a finite enclosure; invalid candidatesremain errors. An upper endpoint below zero establishes a negative reduced costfor that candidate. A nonnegative lower endpoint establishes nonnegativity forthat candidate only. Neither result covers other columns or completes anexternal domain. Phase-I requests automatically omit original objective costs. Objective pricing fixes artificial quantities to zero before accepting duals.If the objective pass did not retain necessary routing paths, recovery obtainsfeasible paths from phase I and rebuilds their identities and original costs.A small finite artificial penalty therefore cannot by itself block an otherwisefeasible restricted-domain pricing request. A pricing request requires an optimal feasible restricted master. An empty orinfeasible restricted domain may need additional feasibility columns; the APIreturns an error rather than concluding that the external domain is infeasible.Numerical pricing requests publish no external-domain bound. Separate opt-incertificate requests are described below. Use the collection protocol to accept columns;only explicit enumeration completion permits the final declared-domain solve. For a restricted domain missing feasibility columns, usesession.feasibility_pricing(options). It minimizes artificial activity withall real objective costs zero, including imported columns, original coordinates,routing arcs and fixed route costs. The returned point haskind() == ImportPricingKind::Feasibility; restricted_violation() reportsnumerical artificial activity in the current restricted master. Positiveactivity does not prove the external domain infeasible, and zero activity doesnot complete that domain. ImportCosts.kind identifies the pricing objective. In feasibility mode,ignore additional column costs and minimize only per_column plus the vectorentries times coordinate prices. reduced_cost handles this distinctionautomatically. After generating feasibility columns, request ordinary objectiveprices to continue optimization. These phase-I signals are numerical; they donot constitute an exact Farkas certificate for an unknown domain. Time-limitedor unsolved augmented masters return an error instead of a stale pricing point.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Permitted column envelopes
text: Permitted column envelopes session.with_envelope(ColumnEnvelope { cost_lower, coordinates }) declaresrestrictions on every column in that imported group, including future columns.cost_lower bounds the additional Column.cost; each (original_id, Bounds)entry bounds one vector coordinate. Declare every coordinate in the group'ssupport exactly once. Omitted column entries mean zero. Known columns mustalready satisfy the declaration. Repeated envelopes intersect, preservingprevious restrictions. Collection and direct extension reject violations, and envelopes persist throughcompletion, snapshots and later extensions. A declaration is model input; itmust describe the intended domain. It is not inferred from the known columns. point.envelope_reduced_cost_bound() encloses the minimum reduced cost over thepermitted feature box and cost floor at the stored dual point. It relaxescorrelations, so it also covers unseen permitted columns. Objective pricinguses the additional-cost floor; phase-I pricing uses zero real cost. An adverseunbounded coordinate or missing cost floor can yield negative infinity. Nonemeans no envelope was declared or arithmetic could not establish a bound. Algebraic candidate queries may evaluate symbolic vectors outside the envelope;model acceptance still enforces it. This is useful for constructing the affineobjective intercept. An envelope reduced-cost bound alone does not establish afull-master bound, external feasibility or enumeration completion.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Certificates for open domains
text: Certificates for open domains session.objective_certificate(options) requests a conservative objective lowerbound over the retained finite imports, original routing domains, and everyfuture column permitted by this open group's envelope.session.feasibility_certificate(options) instead bounds the zero-real-costfeasibility model. Its strict positivity proves infeasibility for that declaredmodel. session.infeasibility_certificate(options) returns Some only whenthat strictly positive proof is available. Otherwise it returns None. ImportCertificate exposes kind(), lower_bound() and proves_infeasible().These requests are opt-in; ordinary pricing remains numerical. They do not marka collection complete or enable a final finite-domain solve while it is open. Publication requires coverage of future columns, valid dual signs and exactfixed-route reductions. Adverse residuals at unbounded original-variableendpoints, unsupported arithmetic or an adverse missing-column price withouta finite total multiplicity cap leave the bound unknown. Declared and explicitgroup multiplicity limits both apply. A zero total cap needs no envelope; anonnegative missing-column price needs no finite cap. Corrections use the fulltotal cap, which is conservative even when known copies already consume it. Bounds inferred by projecting only the known columns are excluded from thesecertificates: future vectors can invalidate those bounds. begin_import opens one group; begin_imports below opens several together.Unselected groups retain their declared finite domains.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Several open imported groups
text: Several open imported groups node.begin_imports(&[group_ids]) creates MultiImport over one shared model.Use with_envelope(group_id, envelope) for each selected group. Unknown orduplicate IDs are rejected. Empty selections are already complete. collect and collect_priced visit unfinished groups in the requested order,round-robin, under a shared deadline and batch budget. Every pricing requestsees all accepted columns from every group. ColumnBatch.complete completesonly the requested group. pending_groups() reports the remaining groups;solve is available only after all selected domains complete. Empty nonterminalbatches consume budget and cannot starve the other groups. Errors preserve theinput session, including batches accepted earlier in the failed call. The objective/feasibility/infeasibility certificate methods cover everyunfinished group at the shared dual point. Missing coverage for any such groupkeeps publication unknown. ImportCertificate::open_groups() identifies theunfinished domains covered by that certificate. Completed groups use theiractual finite columns, even if their envelopes were coarse. Once all selectedgroups complete, finite-domain projections may be used again. An empty selectionneeds no pricing callback; use its ordinary solved output for certificates.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Automatic pricing requests during collection
text: Automatic pricing requests during collection session.collect_priced(&limits, options, callback) runs a fresh restrictedphase-I request for each batch. Positive restricted artificial activity selectsfeasibility prices; zero selects ordinary objective prices. The callbackreceives &ImportPricing and the remaining time, with all previously acceptedcolumns visible through point.subproblem(). Both LP requests share the collection deadline and respect stricter LP timelimits. A batch/time limit returns a resumable session; the next call rebuildsprices for its accepted domain. Empty nonterminal batches consume the batchbudget. Invalid data or callback errors preserve the input session, with thesame external-side-effect caveat as ordinary collection. The callback returns ColumnBatch. Its completion flag still declares fullenumeration of the intended domain. Finding no negative reduced cost does notcomplete a session or authorize a bound. This driver automates feasibility andobjective pricing requests; it supplies no global pricing certificate. As withordinary collection, synchronous callbacks must cooperate with the remainingtime argument. For mixed routing/import models, all routing families must also complete theirenumeration before the MIP can claim full-domain coverage. MIP requires highs. This interface is currently Rust-only; CLI/Python input fields are unchanged.

title: Finite column imports
heading: Trees with open external groups
text: Trees with open external groups session.begin_tree() creates an immutable ImportTree. Calling it declaresthat every unseen column has quantity lower bound zero; register mandatorycolumns before starting. Tree callbacks reject new positive-lower-boundcolumns. This makes an exactly validated solution using known columns a validincumbent while external domains remain open. Call tree.run(&tree_options, &import_limits, callback) with ordinaryModelTreeOptions and ImportOptions. The callback receives fresh phase-Ior objective prices for the current node. Original-variable, qualified-column,routing-multiplicity and physical-arc branches remain in the restriction journalwhen new patterns arrive. Accepted patterns are shared with siblings. A sourcecompletion flag must enumerate the group's entire intended domain, includingpatterns excluded by a node's aggregate restrictions; completion is shared withsiblings too. Open nodes use directed envelope certificates for objective pruning andinfeasibility. Missing or loose certificates keep the node open. An integralrestricted solution alone never closes it. Once every group completes, freshpreprocessing and the existing finite-domain tree, enumeration and optional MIPbecome available. No finite-parent proof survives opening a domain. The result contains tree, status, bound_mode, bound, incumbent, open_nodes andper-invocation node/batch/column counts. Resume with result.tree.run(...) aftera node, batch or time limit. Preserve the bound mode across resumptions.tree.solution() returns the best validated objective, physical routes andoriginal/qualified column values from the incumbent's own lineage. Newlyregistered optional columns can be absent from those stored values. Empty nonterminal batches visit the other unfinished groups. A full roundwithout additions or completion returns Incomplete with a reusable frontier.Callback errors or invalid batches preserve the input tree; external callbackside effects remain caller-owned. Both budgets share one deadline, andsynchronous callbacks must cooperate with the remaining-time argument. Open sessions also provide with_variable_bounds, with_column_bounds,with_multiplicity, with_routing_multiplicity, with_row,with_presence_row, with_registered_cut_row, with_composite_cut_row andwith_resource_knapsack_row. These immutable restrictions apply during pricing andsurvive future source batches. Original-coordinate links automatically carryadditive and nonlinear-row coupling to newly accepted vectors.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
text: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle Documentation index · Branching ·Enumerated MIP The shared tree driver accepts routing registrations, explicit network modelsand imported-column adapters. Frontier selection, budgets and dispatch have oneimplementation; model hooks interpret nodes and supply branching decisions.This guide describes the routing registration. See network modelsand architecture for the other input contracts. The routing registration solves a set-partitioning master with one pricing graph.It requires nonnegative arc costs and unique public arc IDs. The base rows area fleet upper bound and one equality per customer; the tree validates thisstructure before searching.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Run a tree
text:
Run a tree cargo run --release --features clp --bin baldes -- \
  solve instances/Solomon/R101.txt --customers 10 --tree --time 60
 --nodes N sets the tree node budget (default 10,000). --json FILE writesvalidated incumbent routes, bounds, statuses, and work counters. Use--no-enumeration to disable both reduced-cost fixing and enumeration.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Optional parallel nodes

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Node processing
text: Node processing The search selects a node by its lower bound and evaluates it within theremaining global budget. Its main steps are: Construct the root master, or fork the solved parent and append the child'sconstraints. Run column generation, pricing, cut rounds, and enabled fixing/enumeration. Share valid elementary routes with the incumbent heuristic and other nodes. Search restricted columns for a feasible integer solution; optionally runHiGHS over a complete enumerated universe. Close the node when its selected bound meets the incumbent gap, or selecta branching candidate and create children. Strong trials and diving useisolated evaluations. With multiple time windows, options.branching.time_window_selection runs thetree on window copies of the arcs and branches on time-window selection countsafter arc flows; seebranching on time-window selection. Time limits are cooperative across solver operations. A backend call canfinish after its requested budget. Limits preserve bounds for unfinished nodes. options.root.bound_mode selects BoundMode::Numerical by default, orBoundMode::Certified for independent original-domain validation. The CLIequivalent is --bound-mode numerical|certified. Numerical bounds authorizeordinary pruning within the configured tolerances. Certified mode never usesa numerical estimate to close a node: an unsuccessful certificate attemptleaves the bound unknown. TreeOutput::bound_mode and JSON label the boundand the guarantee of gap-based termination. Warm starts retain the two boundsseparately, so changing modes cannot promote a parent's numerical estimate.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: What a child inherits
text: What a child inherits State Child handling Clp master Deep-copy model, basis, solution, scaling, and simplex state Branch and cut rows Preserve physical rows and coefficient mappings; append new branch rows Existing route columns Retain coefficients and upper bounds; retire routes outside the new domain Pricing graph Carry bucket preparation, fixed bucket arcs, NG state, options, and adaptive state Labels Rebuild for the child's duals and active branch resources Enumeration Retain/filter routes where compatible and preserve branch-distinct arc paths Sibling state Own independent mutable models and pricing state When enumeration changes the master to full-memory cut coefficients, existingcolumns are updated as well as new ones. Reusing limited-memory coefficientsfor only part of the enumerated master would change the model.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Root snapshots and manual inheritance
text: Root snapshots and manual inheritance Set RootOptions::capture_state = true to retain a solved NodeSnapshot inRootOutput::snapshot. The tree arranges snapshot capture for its own nodes.Manual callers use routing::inherit_branches(parent, additional_branches, options)for typed constraints, or routing::inherit for arc-flow tuples. Supply only theadditional branches; the parent already contains its ancestor rows.To retain the child's snapshot for another generation, enable capture on thatsolve too. Snapshots retain both restricted-master columns and the generated column pool,including cached columns that have not entered the master. Child branch rowsand cut cleanup update cached coefficients as well as loaded coefficients.Regeneration checks the child's current path restrictions; a cached route isnot automatically admissible. Manually constructed column-generationWarmStart values provide generated_pool in creation order; an empty pool isinitialized from the loaded columns. The snapshot exposes bound_mode(), branch_depth(), active_cuts(), andenumerated_routes(). A route count alone does not establish completeness;the enumerated-MIP adapter separately checks the completion flag.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Incumbents, proofs, and status
text: Incumbents, proofs, and status Source Supplies an incumbent? Certifies the routing lower bound? Validated elementary route solution Yes No, by its objective alone Restricted-column integer heuristic Yes, after validation No Exact node pricing When the resulting routes form an integer witness Numerical estimate in normal mode; independent certificate required in certified mode Heuristic strong trial or dive Can find a witness No proof for the original node Complete enumerated HiGHS MIP Yes, after validation Only within saved enumeration coverage and for proved outcomes A cost-only --upper-bound can assist root fixing, but the tree needs actualfeasible routes before accepting an incumbent. It does not invent a solutionfrom the supplied number. Optimal means the configured gap is closed under the selected bound mode. TimeLimit,NodeLimit, and Incomplete retain unfinished-node bounds. Check whether afinite incumbent and routes are present before treating a limited run as asolution. JSON encodes nonfinite numbers as null. The restricted-column heuristic uses TreeOptions::mip_node_limit andmip_time_limit; CLI --mip-nodes budgets that heuristic. Optional HiGHS nodeMIP has separate controls and counters; see Enumerated MIP.

title: Branch-and-price tree and node lifecycle
heading: Limits and supported models
text: Limits and supported models Every root, child, and priced trial runs node preprocessing before columngeneration. A worklist propagates continuous bounds through the originalarc-flow master rows and flow conservation, including equivalent outgoingcover rows. Child nodes also propagate active inherited capacity, complement,and two-path cut rows using their exact additive arc coefficients and currentphysical row bounds. Retired cut rows are excluded. Contradictions certify node infeasibility without LP solving orpricing. Zero upper bounds retire inherited columns and restrict both pricingdirections and complete enumeration. Positive aggregate lower bounds remainenforced by their original master rows; they do not require every route tocontain the arc. Parent and sibling state remains independent. RootOutput::preprocessing reports bound updates, processed rows,infeasibility, and whether the bounded worklist reached completion. Reachingthe work limit keeps valid deductions and continues ordinary node evaluation.The reusable master::preprocessing engine accepts signed sparse rows andinfinite variable bounds, but callers must supply a complete formulation.Applying it to an unfinished restricted-column master would be unsound. Ryan–Foster preprocessing closes transitive together groups, excludes arcsbetween apart groups, and fixes all incident arcs of an internally contradictorygroup to zero. Covering and assignment rows then determine whether that groupis mandatory and the node is infeasible. Pricing resources still enforce thecomplete route-level rules; preprocessing does not replace them. Preprocessing currently covers the single-network routing model. The boundedactivity worklist may leave contradictions that require solving the LP.Decomposition-wide local/global multiplicity links remain outside this adapter.
