title: Solver concepts and interface choices
heading: Solver concepts and interface choices
text: Solver concepts and interface choices Documentation index · First solve

title: Solver concepts and interface choices
heading: From paths to a routing solution
text: From paths to a routing solution Pricing finds resource-feasible source-to-sink paths with low reduced cost.A master chooses quantities of route columns to satisfy customer or other sharedrows. Column generation alternates master LP solves with pricing. Cuts add validinequalities; branch-and-price searches integer decisions across a tree. These layers return different objects. A cheap feasible path is not a full fleetplan. A converged root LP can be fractional. A feasible integer incumbent is anupper bound in minimization; pricing supplies lower-bound information under itsconfigured guarantee. Compare the two only when both concern the same model,distance convention, and inherited node restrictions.

title: Solver concepts and interface choices
heading: Select the workflow
text: Select the workflow Need CLI Python Reading Feasible heuristic routing plan hgs HGS seeding within root solve CLI Routing root LP solve solve pyBaldes routing Single-network integer routing tree solve --tree Not exposed by solve Routing tree Custom RCSP pricing Through a model Solver Pricing Shared-master root / integer search solve MODEL.json / solve MODEL.json --tree NetworkProblem.solve(tree=...) Network models One canonical model contains shared rows and zero or more pricing networks.A network can represent one route family; routing input registers customer/fleetsemantics around that same model. Construction, pricing coordination and treeorchestration are shared. Registrations supply their own cut, branching and proofhooks. See architecture and source layout.

title: Solver concepts and interface choices
heading: Three meanings to keep separate
text: Three meanings to keep separate Route feasibility checks a path against resource and node restrictions.Pricing exactness establishes a minimum over the configured pricing domain,which may be an NG relaxation. Independent certification validates boundsor witnesses using its supported arithmetic/model contract. A pricing exactnessflag alone does not establish an independent master certificate. The selected bound_mode is numerical by default. Certified mode keeps missingcertificates unknown rather than substituting numerical estimates. JSON usesnull for unknown bounds. See Python results and theCLI bound fields.

title: Solver concepts and interface choices
heading: Resources and route domains
text: Resources and route domains Scalar resources combine arc consumption, initial states, and vertex windows.Disposable coordinates may wait; equality coordinates do not. Coupled resourcesexpress additional domains and state-dependent costs on the same physical graph.Their definitions are distinct from scalar coordinate IDs. Seescalar resources, coupled resources,and multiple windows. NG memory is a relaxation of elementary routing: a priced path can revisit acustomer when the memory permits it. Complete supported enumeration can transferan elementary route universe into a master. A bounded collection attempt is notcomplete just because it returned routes. Inspect enumeration coverage beforeusing a finite-pool MIP as a proof. See enumerated MIPand network transfer.

title: Solver concepts and interface choices
heading: Reproduce an objective
text: Reproduce an objective Match instance data, customer subset, rounding, explicit matrix, NG construction,cuts, backend, bound mode, and limits. CLI coordinate distances default totruncated tenths; Python follows the instance's convention. Root benchmarkreproduction requires --rounding none. Compare objective values only afterthose choices match, and report limits and proof scope with every result.

title: Maintaining the documentation
heading: Maintaining the documentation
text: Maintaining the documentation Documentation index · Source layout

title: Maintaining the documentation
heading: Documentation organization
text: Documentation organization Directory Reader and purpose guides/ Installation, first workflows, CLI, concepts, and contributor guidance pybaldes/ Python-only handbook: installation through public API reference solver/ Solver lifecycle, algorithms, guarantees, and integer search reference/ Cross-interface options, resources, algorithms, and build behavior extensions/ Specialized formulations and shared-master model contracts benchmarks/ Measured results with reproduction conditions Keep introductory workflows runnable and short. Put field/default tables in therelevant reference, mathematical contracts in solver/model guides, and Pythonusage in pybaldes/. Cross-link shared guarantees rather than changing themindependently. guides/python.md remains an entry page for existing links.

title: Maintaining the documentation
heading: Build and validate
text:
Build and validate Documentation builds require Python 3.10+ and the pinned documentation packages,not a solver compilation: python -m pip install -r .github/scripts/docs-requirements.txt
python -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p 'test_compile_docs.py'
python .github/scripts/compile_docs.py --output /tmp/baldes-docs-preview
 The compiler reads all Markdown under docs/, maps README.md to index.html,checks local targets and heading fragments, rewrites source links to repositoryURLs, copies referenced images, and produces a search index. It renders beforereplacing an existing generated output. It refuses to replace non-generatednonempty directories. Generated HTML is not the documentation source. When source comments or Rust interfaces change, validate the generated Rust APIlinks too (the backend dependencies for these features must be installed): RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links" \
  cargo doc -p baldes --no-deps --features clp,highs,multi-time-windows
 To preview locally, serve the parent directory of the generated docs output andopen the relevant index.html. The normal website build uses landing/docs/;its deployment workflow is .github/workflows/landing.yaml.A website build includes the dedicated pyBaldes section at docs/pybaldes/index.html.

title: Maintaining the documentation
heading: Check claims against the interface
text: Check claims against the interface For Python, inspect exports,unified solve,routing data,network data/snapshots, and native bindings underpython/rust/src. Public Python features come frompython/rust/Cargo.toml, not every root-crate feature.For CLI claims, inspect the command's parser/help and execute --help from thematching build. Use implementation and regression tests to verify behavior;a docstring or type stub alone may omit a feature gate or describe old behavior. The architecture owns the engine/adapter explanation;source layout owns filesystem responsibilities;solve owns common input normalization. The CLI and Python referencesadd their registration-specific controls without introducing separate algorithms. When an API changes, update examples, defaults, return fields, and build gatestogether. In particular, refresh pyBaldes API signaturesafter changing public wrappers or bindings. Validate all runnable examples usingthe same source/native-extension build. State any unavailable optional backendinstead of claiming those examples ran.

title: Maintaining the documentation
heading: Review checklist
text: Review checklist Specify the interface and solve mode for each claim of optimality. Separate numerical bounds, independent certificates, incumbents, and phase-I objectives. State distance conventions, units, ID spaces, and per-arc vector ordering. Show feature requirements next to optional APIs. Avoid claiming complete enumeration from a truncated pool. Keep one canonical page for each contract and update all links when moving a page; do not retain obsolete split-interface guides. Link every guide from a discoverable index and verify heading fragments. Record machine, limits, features, repetitions, and rounding for performance claims. Do not rewrite benchmark measurements without rerunning their documented setup.The root chart requires explicit --rounding none. Historical measurements andinternal audit artifacts do not establish current performance or full solvercorrectness.

title: Install pyBaldes
heading: Install pyBaldes

title: Install pyBaldes
heading: Install from a checkout
text:
Install from a checkout The source package requires Python 3.9+, Rust/Cargo 1.85+, Git, and a C++14compiler for the default Clp build. Package construction uses maturin.Use a virtual environment so the interpreter used to install is also the onethat imports the extension: git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/lseman/baldes.git
cd baldes
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install .
 For an existing checkout, initialize the two native dependencies before installing: git submodule update --init vendor/Clp vendor/CoinUtils
python -m pip install .
 The mixed package contains Python wrappers and pybaldes._core, a PyO3 extensionusing Python's stable ABI starting with Python 3.9. ABI compatibility does notremove platform, CPU, or shared-library requirements. The commands above buildfrom local source; they do not assume an available binary wheel on a package index.

title: Install pyBaldes
heading: Verify the installed build
text:
Verify the installed build import pybaldes

print(pybaldes.__version__)
print(pybaldes.__file__)
print("Clp:", pybaldes.has_clp)
print("HiGHS:", pybaldes.has_highs)
print("Gurobi:", pybaldes.has_gurobi)
print("Scalar capacity:", pybaldes.resource_dimensions)
print("NG capacity:", pybaldes.ng_memory_capacity)
print("Multiple windows:", hasattr(pybaldes.Solver, "set_vertex_time_windows"))
 Clp is enabled by default. Both routing roots and shared-master network solvesrequire it, even if a routing root selects another LP solve backend.Low-level Solver pricing and ResourceModel do not require Clp.

title: Install pyBaldes
heading: Build features
text:
Build features Pass features through pip's maturin build arguments: python -m pip install . --config-settings=build-args="--features multi-time-windows,ng-memory-31"
 Python crate feature Effect clp (default) Build the Clp master and expose routing/network solving highs Link HiGHS; enable its routing LP backend and network enumerated MIP gurobi Link Gurobi; enable its routing LP backend; runtime license required simd Enable optional runtime-dispatched SIMD kernels multi-time-windows Expose disjoint service-start windows rank-one-node-memory Select node memory for generated rank-one cuts ng-memory-31 / ng-memory-63 Increase compiled NG memory from the default 15; 63 takes precedence ryan-foster-master (default) Enforce Ryan–Foster branches through master rows, matching modern MetaSolver accumulated-resource-master (default) Enforce accumulated-resource branches through master rows, matching modern MetaSolver The Python feature list is defined by python/rust/Cargo.toml.Do not assume every root-crate Cargo feature is forwarded by the Python crate.The Python crate currently forwards simd, but does not declare simd-avx512.See the BALDES build guide for native library discovery,Gurobi environment variables, and backend requirements. For a pricing-only extension: python -m pip install . --config-settings=build-args=--no-default-features
 This also selects pricing-enforced Ryan–Foster and accumulated-resourcebranches. Add --features clp if the extension should retain LP/network solvingwhile using those pricing-enforced policies. For HiGHS or Gurobi, first configure the native installation as described in thebuild guide, then build with the corresponding feature: python -m pip install . --config-settings=build-args="--features highs"
# Or, with a configured Gurobi installation and license:
python -m pip install . --config-settings=build-args="--features gurobi"
 These features retain default Clp unless --no-default-features is also passed.A backend flag reports compiled support, not runtime library/license health.

title: Install pyBaldes
heading: Scalar capacity
text:
Scalar capacity Solver(n_vertices, n_resources) chooses the number of active scalar resourceswithin a compiled capacity. The default capacity is two. Rebuild to change it: BALDES_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS=5 python -m pip install .
 Inspect pybaldes.resource_dimensions afterward. Coupled resources declared withResourceModel are a separate interface; their IDs are not scalar coordinates.Direct pip/maturin builds read BALDES_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS, not Make's .config.

title: Install pyBaldes
heading: Develop and test
text:
Develop and test Inside an activated virtual environment: python -m pip install maturin pytest
maturin develop --release
python -m pytest python/tests -q
 The root pyproject.toml points maturin at python/rust/Cargo.toml and installswrappers from python/pybaldes/. Rebuild after changing Rust code or features.Restart long-lived interpreters and notebook kernels after replacing the nativeextension. Optional-feature tests skip when their required build is unavailable.

heading: pyBaldes quickstart

title: pyBaldes quickstart
heading: Solve a small routing relaxation
text:
Solve a small routing relaxation This example uses only in-memory data. No instance download is required: from pybaldes import Customer, Instance

instance = Instance(
    name="triangle",
    capacity=2,
    customers=[
        Customer(0, 0, due=100),  # depot at index 0
        Customer(1, 0, demand=1, due=100),
        Customer(0, 1, demand=1, due=100),
        Customer(1, 1, demand=1, due=100),
    ],
    vehicles=3,
)
result = instance.solve(
    problem_type="vrptw",
    capacity_cuts=True,
    time_limit=30,
    reduced_cost_fixing=False,
)
print(result.status, result.lp, result.bound)
for route in result.routes:
    print(route.value, route.cost, route.nodes)
 With a converged solve, the cut-strengthened objective is approximately5.4142135624. Route values are LP column weights. A value such as 0.5 meansthe relaxation uses half a column; it is not half a vehicle to dispatch.Optimal describes convergence of this LP, not proof of an integer VRP optimum. The returned graph uses source 0 and a separate terminal depot. For this example,customer IDs are 1, 2, 3 and the terminal ID is 4. Do not indexinstance.customers[4]; map the terminal back to depot 0 for visualization.

title: pyBaldes quickstart
heading: Read a bundled instance
text:
Read a bundled instance Run from the repository root: import pybaldes

result = pybaldes.solve(
    "instances/Solomon/R101.txt",
    customers=10,
    rounding="none",
    time_limit=30,
)
print(result.status, result.numerical_bound, result.certified_bound)
 CVRPLIB input automatically selects capacity-only routing; an explicit override is optional: from pybaldes import Instance

instance = Instance.from_file("instances/cvrplib/A-n32-k5.vrp")
result = instance.solve(time_limit=30)
 Python defaults to the instance's distance convention. CLI routing defaults totruncation to tenths. Match rounding explicitly when comparing the interfaces.

title: pyBaldes quickstart
heading: Export a result
text:
Export a result from pathlib import Path

Path("root-result.json").write_text(result.to_json(), encoding="utf-8")
for step in result.history:
    print(step.iteration, step.lp, step.minimum_reduced_cost, step.exact)
 Unknown numerical quantities can be infinite in Python. RootResult.to_json()converts non-finite floats to JSON null; to_dict() preserves them.

title: pyBaldes quickstart
heading: Price a path directly
text:
Price a path directly Use the low-level interface when you own the master or need a constrained path: from pybaldes import Solver

solver = Solver(3, 1)
solver.set_source(0)
solver.set_sink(2)
load = solver.new_resource("load", 0)
a = solver.new_arc(0, 1, -2.0)
b = solver.new_arc(1, 2, 1.0)
solver.set_arc_consumption(a, load, 1.0)
solver.set_arc_consumption(b, load, 1.0)
for vertex in range(3):
    solver.set_vertex_bounds(vertex, load, 0.0, 2.0)
    solver.set_ng_neighborhood(vertex, [vertex])
minimum, routes, exact = solver.price_with_status(10, exact=True)
assert exact
assert minimum == -1.0
assert routes[0].nodes() == [0, 1, 2]
print(routes[0].original_cost, routes[0].resource_consumption(load))
 This solves the configured pricing domain. It does not create customer-coveringrows, solve a routing master, or independently certify a master lower bound.See pricing for repeated dual updates and networksfor a master managed by pyBaldes.

title: Routing inputs and options
heading: Routing inputs and options
text: Routing inputs and options pyBaldes documentation · Results

title: Routing inputs and options
heading: Customer and Instance
text:
Customer and Instance Customer(x, y, demand=0.0, ready=0.0, due=math.inf, service=0.0) is a frozenvalue object. Coordinates define Euclidean distances unless an explicit matrixis supplied. Time windows constrain service start; service duration contributesto the next transition. The depot must be the first customer and have zero demand. Instance(name, capacity, customers, vehicles=1, rounding="none", distances=None)normalizes customers and matrix rows into tuples. Every customer must be aCustomer. Native solving performs additional numeric/model validation. Field Contract name Model label capacity Positive vehicle capacity customers Depot followed by customers in internal index order vehicles Input metadata; the routing root uses customer count as its fleet upper bound rounding Distance convention used when no solve override is supplied distances Optional full depot/customer matrix; supplied weights determine distances For VRPTW, supply finite ready and due values, including for the depot.The default infinite due is convenient for CVRP but is not a valid VRPTWwindow. CVRP ignores time windows and service durations. from pybaldes import Customer, Instance

instance = Instance("matrix", 2, [
    Customer(0, 0), Customer(1, 0, demand=1), Customer(0, 1, demand=1),
], distances=[
    [0, 2, 3],
    [2, 0, 4],
    [3, 4, 0],
])
result = instance.solve(problem_type="cvrp")
 Instance.from_file(path) accepts a string or path-like object and reads Solomonor CVRPLIB .vrp data. Constraint type is inferred when solving;use problem_type only to override it. Instance.truncated(N) returns a new instancecontaining the first N customers plus the depot, truncating both matrix axes.It requires 0 < N < len(instance.customers) and preserves the original object.

title: Routing inputs and options
heading: Distance conventions
text: Distance conventions Value Coordinate-derived distance "none" Unrounded Euclidean distance "nearest" TSPLIB nearest integer (nint) "tenth" Truncate to tenths "ceil" Round upward to an integer Solomon files default to none; CVRPLIB EUC_2D defaults to nearest andCEIL_2D to ceil. Explicit CVRPLIB full/triangular edge-weight matrices retainthe supplied weights. A solve's rounding=None uses instance.rounding.Match these conventions before comparing objective values. CVRPLIB route-lengthconstraints (DISTANCE) are not part of this routing interface.

title: Routing inputs and options
heading: solve
text: solve solve(instance, *, ...) accepts an Instance, file path string, or path-likeobject. instance.solve(**options) delegates to the same function. Alloptions below are keyword-only. The call requires a Clp-enabled build.

title: Routing inputs and options
heading: Model and pricing
text: Model and pricing Keyword Default Behavior problem_type None Infer from finite due times; "vrptw" or "cvrp" explicitly overrides it customers None Keep the first N customers before solving ng 8 NG neighborhood size; constrained by compiled memory reference_ng False Use reference nearest-customer neighborhood construction rounding None Override coordinate distance convention pricing_options None Mapping of supported BALDES names to numeric values capacity_cuts False Enable rounded capacity cuts two_path_cuts False Enable capacity-family Kohl separation with time resource; VRPTW only rank_one_cuts False Enable limited-memory rank-one cuts stabilize True Dual-price smoothing; disabled by IPM stabilization_max_tree_depth 10000 Shared stabilization depth gate; routing Python calls solve the root reduced_cost_fixing True Reduced-cost fixing and route enumeration; disabling disables both upper_bound math.inf Supplied incumbent objective used for fixing; use a valid feasible bound NG pricing can include repeated customers. Exact pricing of this configuredrelaxation does not make every route elementary. Rank-one cut memory alsodepends on build features. Inspect supported controls withSolver.option_names() and Solver.option_support(name); see thepricing option reference for scope and values.

title: Routing inputs and options
heading: Master and bound policy
text: Master and bound policy Keyword Default Behavior master_solver "clp" "clp", "ipm", "highs", or "gurobi"; last two need features master_threads 0 HiGHS/Gurobi worker budget; 0 uses available CPUs; Clp/IPM ignore it bound_mode "numerical" Numerical bounds or independent "certified" validation clp_scaling "equilibrium" "equilibrium", "auto", "geometric", or "off" clp_keep_work_areas True Retain native work buffers across LP solves HiGHS uses a process-shared native scheduler: keep its worker budget consistentwithin one process and configure it before the first solve. CPU affinity limitsthe available worker count. A higher budget does not guarantee faster solving.Selecting IPM disables stabilization. Gurobi additionally needs its runtimelibrary and a valid license. All backend choices still require the Clp model store.

title: Routing inputs and options
heading: Heuristic seeding, limits, and logging
text:
Heuristic seeding, limits, and logging Keyword Default Behavior hgs_time None Positive HGS time budget in seconds before column generation hgs_columns "best" Best plan, "all" validated encountered routes, or positive integer count of cheapest new routes hgs_seed 0 HGS random seed time_limit 120.0 Root solve budget in seconds; separate from HGS max_iterations 100000 Column-generation iteration limit max_cut_rounds None Optional cut-round limit verbose False Emit progress to stderr log_interval 10 Positive interval between progress rows from pybaldes import solve

result = solve(
    "instances/Solomon/R101.txt", customers=10, rounding="none",
    master_solver="ipm", hgs_time=0.5, hgs_columns="all", hgs_seed=7,
    capacity_cuts=True, bound_mode="certified", time_limit=30,
    verbose=True, log_interval=5,
)
print(result.status, result.bound, result.incumbent)
 The HGS budget is additional work, so time_limit alone is not an end-to-endwall-time cap. Failure to obtain a certificate leaves the certified bound unknown;it never substitutes the numerical estimate. See results.

title: Stateful pricing with Solver
heading: Stateful pricing with Solver
text: Stateful pricing with Solver pyBaldes documentation · Quickstart · Resources Solver owns a directed graph and retained pricing state. Use it to obtainresource-feasible paths, or as an oracle inside a master that you implement.It does not create or optimize a shared master automatically.

title: Stateful pricing with Solver
heading: Construction order and IDs
text: Construction order and IDs Construct Solver(n_vertices, n_resources). The active scalar count cannotexceed pybaldes.resource_dimensions. Set source/sink and add directed arcs, retaining the IDs from new_arc. Configure scalar kinds, initial values, vertex bounds, and arc consumption. Configure NG neighborhoods or elementarity sets. Install any coupled-resource model after the physical graph is complete. Set pricing options, optionally prepare buckets, and price. Vertex IDs are zero-based. Arc IDs follow insertion order. Per-arc vectors mustuse that order, including arcs not used by a returned route. new_resource(name, kind) configures the next pre-created scalar coordinate; it does not grow theconstructor's resource count. The name is an interface label, not a lookup key.

title: Stateful pricing with Solver
heading: Scalar resource semantics
text: Scalar resource semantics kind Meaning 0 Disposable resource: nonnegative consumption; may wait to reach lower bounds 1 Equality resource: signed accumulation without waiting Initial values default to source lower bounds unless explicitly set. Lower andupper bounds are inclusive. Equality here describes propagation, not a masterrow's equality constraint. Backward equality pricing needs fixed sink windows;otherwise the engine selects forward search. See scalar resources. The quickstart builds a complete load example.For a time resource, arc consumption typically includes travel plus tail service;vertex bounds constrain service start. The low-level API does not infer thesequantities from coordinates.

title: Stateful pricing with Solver
heading: NG and elementarity
text: NG and elementarity set_ng_neighborhood(vertex, nodes) requires distinct valid IDs and inclusionof the vertex itself. Actual preparation is limited by the compiledpybaldes.ng_memory_capacity (15 by default), including merged arc memory.The binding's preliminary size check is not a promise that 64 entries fit.NG relaxation permits some revisits; it is not full elementarity. add_elementarity_set(nodes) returns a set ID;attach_elementarity_to_node(vertex, set_id) associates an existing set witha vertex. These are low-level elementarity controls. In declarative networks,PricingNetwork(elementary=True) requests the network's elementary domain.

title: Stateful pricing with Solver
heading: Repeated pricing in column generation
text:
Repeated pricing in column generation Build the graph once and update reduced costs as master duals change: from pybaldes import Solver

solver = Solver(3, 0)
solver.set_source(0)
solver.set_sink(2)
solver.new_arc(0, 1, 2.0)
solver.new_arc(1, 2, 1.0)
solver.build_default_resource_buckets()

# Example reduced arc costs computed by your master integration.
solver.set_reduced_costs([-3.0, 1.0])
minimum, routes, exact = solver.price_with_status(30)
if not routes and not exact:
    minimum, routes, exact = solver.price_with_status(30, exact=True)
for route in routes:
    print(route.cost, route.original_cost, route.arcs())
 set_reduced_costs(costs) requires one finite value per physical arc. It preservesoriginal costs and prepared graph state. Derive reduced costs using your ownrow coefficients; this API cannot infer the rows in an external master. update_reduced_costs(costs, duals) instead replaces original arc costs andapplies vertex dual prices. Supply one cost per arc and one dual per vertex.Use it when original costs change or when the vertex-dual representation matchesyour master. Do not feed already reduced costs into it and subtract duals twice.

title: Stateful pricing with Solver
heading: Pricing returns and exactness
text: Pricing returns and exactness Call Return Contract solve() (cost, Route) or None Single-route pricing; None is not a master infeasibility proof price(maximum) (minimum, routes) Staged pricing without an aggregate exactness flag price_with_status(maximum, exact=False) (minimum, routes, exact) Staged pricing; can return heuristic improving columns price_with_status(maximum, exact=True) Same triple Run unlimited-label pricing phase once; can include nonnegative columns enumerate(maximum) (1e12, 0, routes) Current compatibility wrapper around phase-0 pricing; first two values are placeholders maximum must be a positive integer. Only use a minimum as a pricing bound whenthe returned exactness flag establishes it for the configured domain. Unlimitedlabels do not remove time, arithmetic, memory, or model-domain restrictions.An NG-domain minimum is not the same as an elementary-path minimum. The low-level enumerate() method does not itself transfer a complete universeinto a master or populate the retained enumeration store. Do not interpret itsplaceholder values as a bound or route count. enumerated_count andget_enumerated(index) inspect an existing retained universe; callingenumerate() alone does not establish one. For reported route coverage and MIPtransfer use the network workflow.

title: Stateful pricing with Solver
heading: Route and Phase
text: Route and Phase A low-level Route owns its data and remains valid after the solver is released. Member Meaning cost Priced route objective, including configured coupled charges original_cost Original objective before reduced-cost adjustments nb_nodes Number of entries in the node sequence nodes() / arcs() Copies of ordered vertex/physical-arc IDs resource_consumption(resource_id) Final scalar resource value is_certified Whether the producing pricing result was exact; not a directed arithmetic certificate get_phase(index) returns Phase with check_ng, allow_jump_arcs, andlabels_per_bucket. phase_count reports the configured schedule size.

title: Stateful pricing with Solver
heading: Configuration method reference
text: Configuration method reference Method Purpose set_source(v), set_sink(v) Select terminal vertices set_graph_id(id) Set diagnostic graph identity new_arc(tail, head, cost) Add physical arc; return its ID new_resource(name, kind), set_resource_type(resource_id, kind) Configure pre-created scalar coordinates set_arc_consumption(arc_id, resource_id, value) Set one finite consumption set_vertex_bounds(vertex_id, resource_id, lower, upper) Set inclusive scalar bounds set_initial_resource(resource_id, value) Set finite source state set_vertex_time_windows(vertex_id, resource_id, windows) Optional disjoint windows; feature-gated set_ng_neighborhood(vertex_id, nodes) Replace a vertex's NG memory add_elementarity_set(nodes), attach_elementarity_to_node(vertex_id, set_id) Configure elementarity membership set_pricing_controls(cutoff, max_labels, max_columns) Set cutoff and positive work/output limits set_option(name, value), get_option(name) Set/read a numeric BALDES option option_names(), option_support(name) Static supported-name list and availability/scope explanation build_default_resource_buckets() Prepare bucket labeling using current graph/options set_bidirectional_mode(mode) 0 off, 1 normal, 2 halfway Choose options before preparing buckets. If topology, elementarity, or arc orderchanges after coupled resources are installed, reinstall their definitions soprepared domains match the graph. Prefer rebuilding the solver for topologychanges between iterations. Cost-only updates have a dedicated reuse interface.

title: Coupled resources and function encodings
heading: Coupled resources and function encodings
text: Coupled resources and function encodings pyBaldes documentation · Pricing Scalar coordinates cover additive consumption and vertex bounds. ResourceModeladds physical-graph resource families with selection domains, simultaneouspickup/delivery, numeric dependencies, and state-dependent objective terms.It attaches definitions to the same solver; it does not expand your vertex IDs.

title: Coupled resources and function encodings
heading: Declare and install
text:
Declare and install from pybaldes import ResourceModel, Solver

solver = Solver(3, 0)
solver.new_arc(0, 1, -20.0)
solver.new_arc(1, 2, -20.0)
model = ResourceModel()
parent = model.add_custom_resource(
    increments=[2.0, 1.0], weights=[3.0, 4.0],
    forward_bound=7.0, backward_bound=3.0,
)
model.add_piecewise_linear_cost(
    parent, functions=[[(0.0, 0.0), (10.0, 10.0)]] * 2,
)
model.install(solver)
minimum, routes, exact = solver.price_with_status(10, exact=True)
assert exact and minimum == -17.0
assert routes[0].original_cost == -17.0
 Each increment/weight/function vector has one entry per physical arc in insertionorder. A returned resource ID refers to this declaration list. Dependentresources reference an earlier compatible numeric parent, not a scalar ID fromSolver.new_resource. Keep IDs returned by methods instead of hard-coding them.Install after graph construction. Reinstall after topology/arc-order changes.Installation invalidates prepared labels, fixing, and enumeration state. In this example the custom state moves from 0 to 2 to 3. Its own objective chargeis 2*3 + 3*4 = 18; the dependent piecewise charges add 2 + 3 = 5.Adding those to base arc cost -40 gives -17. Coupled charges appear inRoute.original_cost as well as its priced objective.

title: Coupled resources and function encodings
heading: ResourceModel methods
text: ResourceModel methods The API reference lists exact signatures. Method Inputs and meaning add_selection initial, per-arc allowed bitmasks, optional vertices, relaxed=False; intersect selected-value domains add_simultaneous_pickup_delivery capacity, per-arc deliveries, pickups, tolerance=1e-6; enforce physical route load add_cumulative_cost initial, per-arc increments, weights, optional sink_upper and source_upper; accumulate state-dependent cost add_custom_resource Per-arc increments, weights, optional forward_bound, backward_bound; zero-initial numeric state with directional cost bounds add_dependent Earlier parent, initial, lower, upper, per-arc offsets and factors; affine dependency add_piecewise_linear_resource initial, lower, upper, per-arc knot functions; direct state transitions add_piecewise_linear_cost Earlier parent and per-arc knot functions; objective charges evaluated on parent state add_piecewise_linear_dependent Earlier parent, own initial/bounds, per-arc knot functions; dependent numeric transitions add_encoded_piecewise_linear_resource Direct transitions using EncodedFunction objects add_encoded_piecewise_linear_cost Parent-state charges using encoded functions add_encoded_piecewise_linear_dependent Numeric dependency using encoded functions add_interval_cost Initial interval, global bounds, per-arc increments and knot functions; preserve a shared continuous initial choice add_slope_interval_cost Interval cost with explicit slope encodings and front policy add_paired_piecewise_linear Initial interval/front, per-arc arrival/increment/lower/upper functions, integer waiting rates, and mode add_slope_paired Paired relation with encoded slope functions, front policy, and cost normalization install Validate and attach the declaration list to a Solver Selection masks encode allowed values as bits, rather than a list of scalarvalues. Simultaneous pickup/delivery checks the combined physical load along theroute; independent total delivery and pickup bounds do not capture that contract.Numeric transition equations, directional bounds, and feasibility tolerances arespecified in the coupled-resource model guide.

title: Coupled resources and function encodings
heading: Knot and slope encodings
text:
Knot and slope encodings from pybaldes import EncodedFunction

knots = EncodedFunction.knots([(0.0, 2.0), (4.0, 10.0)])
slope = EncodedFunction.slope_segments([(2.0, 0.0), (2.0, 4.0)])
affine = EncodedFunction.affine(2.0, 2.0, 0.0, 4.0)
assert knots.value(3.0) == slope.value(3.0) == affine.value(3.0) == 8.0
assert knots.value(5.0) is None
restored = EncodedFunction.from_dict(slope.to_dict())
assert restored.value(3.0) == 8.0
 Knot pairs are (argument, value). Slope encoding instead begins with(initial_value, initial_coordinate); each later pair is(segment_slope, ending_coordinate). They are different representations withdifferent evaluation order. Do not pass knot pairs to slope_segments.affine(intercept, slope, lower, upper) prepares an anchored slope representation. .encoding and .policy identify the stored encoding and evaluation policy..value(argument) returns None outside the accepted domain; invalid arithmeticraises ValueError. to_dict()/from_dict() retain explicit wire encoding.Use them when inserting encoded functions into network JSON descriptors. Knot functions use strict closed domains. Slope functions accept evaluationpolicy "strict_domain" (default) or "endpoint_tolerance". Slope interval/pairedresources separately choose front policy "strict_domain" or"front_algebra". Strict fronts require strict slope functions;front-algebra fronts require endpoint-tolerance slope functions. Knotfunctions cannot be substituted where lossless slope encodings are required. Paired modes are "feasibility", "cost_bounded", and "cost_unbounded".Slope-paired normalization defaults to "absolute_final_value"; the alternativeis "final_minus_initial_minimum". These choices affect objective meaning andarithmetic; do not change them to bypass a domain error. A successful numericalfront operation does not automatically provide an independent bound certificate.

title: Coupled resources and function encodings
heading: Disjoint time windows
text:
Disjoint time windows Requires a build with multi-time-windows: from pybaldes import Solver

if hasattr(Solver, "set_vertex_time_windows"):
    solver = Solver(3, 1)
    for vertex in range(3):
        solver.set_vertex_bounds(vertex, 0, 0.0, 20.0)
    a = solver.new_arc(0, 1, -2.0)
    b = solver.new_arc(1, 2, -1.0)
    solver.set_arc_consumption(a, 0, 4.0)
    solver.set_arc_consumption(b, 0, 2.0)
    solver.set_vertex_time_windows(1, 0, [(0.0, 2.0), (8.0, 12.0)])
    minimum, routes, exact = solver.price_with_status(10, exact=True)
    assert routes[0].resource_consumption(0) == 10.0
 Arrival at 4 waits until 8; the final state is 10. Ordinary vertex boundsintersect the window union. Bounds [3, 7] at the middle vertex would make thatvisit infeasible; the gap is not filled by the windows' convex hull. Supplynonempty finite closed intervals on disposable resources. For declarative networks use PricingResource(time_windows=...), with oneentry per vertex; None uses ordinary bounds for that vertex. Seemultiple time windows for validation rules.

title: Coupled resources and function encodings
heading: Declarative network resources
text: Declarative network resources PricingNetwork(coupled_resources=(descriptor, ...)) accepts JSON-style mappingswith a kind tag. It is separate from ResourceModel.install(solver), whichoperates on a low-level solver. Per-arc vectors and parent declaration indicesretain the same ordering requirements. Use the descriptor schema in thecoupled-resource guide, includingexplicit bounds objects and function encodings. Routing text readers do notinfer coupled resource definitions. Unsupported certificate operators or exhausted work can leave bounds unknown.Resource replay, pricing exactness, integer witness validation, and independentbound certificates are separate operations; inspect the corresponding result.

title: Results, bounds, and exactness
heading: Results, bounds, and exactness
text: Results, bounds, and exactness pyBaldes documentation · Routing · Networks

title: Results, bounds, and exactness
heading: Identify the quantity before using it
text: Identify the quantity before using it For a minimization model, an independently justified lower bound L and a validinteger incumbent U imply L <= optimum <= U. An LP column vector may befractional. Its objective is not automatically an integer incumbent, and arestricted-master LP objective is not automatically a bound on all possiblecolumns before pricing has justified it. Quantity Interpretation lp Current reported master LP objective; check status and pricing completion bound Selected lower bound under bound_mode numerical_bound Floating-point pricing estimate under solver tolerances certified_bound Independently validated bound, when available incumbent Best reported integer objective, when one is known Low-level pricing minimum Reduced-cost minimum; use as a pricing bound only with returned exact=True Low-level Route.is_certified Pricing-phase exactness marker; not an independent master certificate bound_mode="numerical" selects the numerical bound and normally skips theindependent certificate search. bound_mode="certified" requests independentoriginal-domain validation when pricing or the incumbent gap can close. Anunsupported operator, exhausted work budget, or unknown arithmetic can leavethe certificate unknown even when the numerical estimate is finite. For root results an unknown certificate is -math.inf in Python and null inJSON. Network result unknown quantities are None, serialized as null.Do not replace an unknown bound with lp, zero, or the incumbent.

title: Results, bounds, and exactness
heading: Status and solve mode
text: Status and solve mode For routing input, solve returns a root relaxation and Optimal means theconfigured root LP converged. For network input, tree=True requests integersearch through the same public function. NetworkResult.mode distinguishes root, tree, and enumerated-MIPworkflows. In a tree, Optimal describes integer gap closure under the selectedbound policy and tolerances. Read bound_mode alongside status. A time, iteration, or node limit can leave a useful incumbent without provingoptimality. A network tree can report Incomplete when its available branchingfamilies cannot resolve the remaining fractionality. Infeasibility conclusionsmust come from the solver's relevant feasibility/proof status, not an emptyroute list. The feasibility guide explains phase I.

title: Results, bounds, and exactness
heading: RootResult reference
text: RootResult reference The frozen result objects contain tuple-valued collections. Fields Meaning status, bound_mode Termination and selected bound guarantee lp, bound, numerical_bound, certified_bound Objective and lower-bound quantities above lp_before_cuts LP objective before cut strengthening incumbent, pruned_by_bound Integer upper bound and bound-pruning outcome cuts, cut_rounds Generated rows and separation rounds; counts include retired rows iterations, pricing_calls Column-generation work counters columns Route columns added over the run master_columns Final master size, including artificial columns fixing_calls, enumerated_routes Fixing/enumeration counters duals Exported master dual vector seconds, pricing_seconds, solver_seconds Reported elapsed/component timers simplex_iterations, ipm_iterations LP backend iteration totals routes Positive LP RootRoute columns history Iteration records feasibility Auxiliary FeasibilityReport records RootRoute(value, cost, nodes, arcs) contains the column weight, original routecost, node sequence, and arc sequence. For N routing customers, the source is0 and the separate terminal depot is N+1; internal customer IDs are 1 through N.The node sequence may repeat under NG relaxation. RootRoute uses .nodes and.arcs attributes; low-level Route uses .nodes() and .arcs() methods. Iteration fields are iteration, lp, minimum_reduced_cost, new_columns,columns, exact, phase, pricing_calls, alpha, and misprices.They expose the per-iteration objective, pricing output, phase exactness, andstabilization diagnostics. Do not infer a global certificate from exact. FeasibilityReport fields are status, iterations, pricing_calls,simplex_iterations, ipm_iterations, seconds, artificial_activity,lower_bound, and certified_infeasible. Its bounds belong to the auxiliaryphase-I objective, not the original routing objective.

title: Results, bounds, and exactness
heading: NetworkResult reference
text: NetworkResult reference Fields Meaning mode, status, bound_mode Solve workflow, termination, and bound policy lp, bound, numerical_bound, certified_bound, incumbent Optional objective/bound quantities routes, fixed_routes Active route solution and separately retained fixed contributions duals Shared-master dual values iterations, pricing_calls, oracle_calls Total work and (network ID, calls) pairs nodes, open_nodes Tree evaluation and remaining-node counts seconds Reported elapsed time enumeration_reports Per-attempt route coverage reports enumerated_mip_calls, enumerated_mip_nodes, enumerated_mip_failures Integer transfer work snapshot Thread-bound resumable node for root results; otherwise may be None NetworkRoute fields are network, route_index, value, cost, nodes,arcs, resources, and resource_profile. Network and arc IDs are local to themodel's declared network; route_index is a snapshot route handle, not an arcor a position in the returned positive-route list. It can be absent.resources gives final scalar values; resource_profile records states alongthe route. Include fixed_routes when interpreting child-node contributions.Synchronization rewards can be master contributions outside the route costs. NetworkEnumerationReport fields are attempts, complete, networks,routes, transferred, failure, and coverage_cutoff. A route limit is abudget, not evidence of complete enumeration. A finite coverage_cutoffrestricts the covered improvement domain; consult it before interpreting a MIPresult as a proof. See network enumeration.

title: Results, bounds, and exactness
heading: Serialization
text:
Serialization import json
import math

# With a RootResult named result:
data = result.to_dict()  # ordinary dataclass data; may retain infinities
text = result.to_json(indent=2)  # strict JSON; non-finite floats become null
assert isinstance(json.loads(text), dict)
if math.isfinite(result.bound):
    print("Selected finite bound:", result.bound)

title: Results, bounds, and exactness
heading: Pricing work and retained original witnesses
text: Pricing work and retained original witnesses RootResult.pricing_calls counts coordinator requests and RootResult.oracle_callscounts entries into its network oracle. NetworkResult.oracle_calls reportsper-network counts; pricing_calls counts coordinator batches. A partial networkbatch is not globally exact. Exact pricing describes the configured pricingdomain, which can remain an NG relaxation. NetworkResult.tree_processed_nodes, strong_branching_trials,mapped_history_ranked and mapped_branch_evaluations describe selection/trialwork. These are distinct from the number of fully priced nodes. Original-variablereports appear in original_variables. A valid original-model witness found during pricing can survive even when thecurrent relaxed solution is fractional or unsynchronized. For example, optionalservice models may retain a feasible empty solution of objective 0 while theirrelaxed bound is negative. That does not earn reward for an unserved job or closethe remaining tree. Inspect routes, original variables, status, bound and opennodes together.

title: pyBaldes troubleshooting and reproducibility
heading: Installation and import
text: Installation and import Symptom Check and action ModuleNotFoundError: pybaldes Use the same interpreter for python -m pip install . and execution; inspect python -m pip --version. pybaldes._core cannot be imported Build/install the native extension; merely adding python/ to PYTHONPATH is insufficient. Clp/CoinUtils source missing during build Initialize vendor/Clp and vendor/CoinUtils submodules, then rebuild. Native library cannot be loaded Check platform-compatible extension and dynamic HiGHS/Gurobi library discovery. Root/network solve says Clp is required Rebuild with default features or clp; selecting IPM does not remove this requirement. HiGHS/Gurobi selection rejected Check has_highs / has_gurobi, rebuild with the feature, and verify native installation/license. Old behavior after a Rust edit Rebuild with maturin and restart the interpreter or notebook kernel. Disjoint-window method absent Rebuild with multi-time-windows; check with hasattr. Inspect pybaldes.__file__ to locate the imported package. A stale extensioncan coexist with newer Python wrappers, especially with manually managedPYTHONPATH. Install the package as a unit rather than copying _core alone.

title: pyBaldes troubleshooting and reproducibility
heading: Model validation
text: Model validation Symptom Likely cause VRPTW rejects customer data Infinite default due, invalid bounds, or non-finite data; set explicit finite windows including depot. Resource count rejected Active count exceeds resource_dimensions; change the build capacity or model. NG local memory exceeds capacity Neighborhood plus merged arc memory exceeds ng_memory_capacity; reduce it or rebuild with wider memory. Per-arc vector rejected Vector length/order does not match all inserted physical arcs. Network identity or row error Duplicate network IDs or invalid zero-based shared-row indices. Piecewise function rejected Invalid ordering, domain, representation, or policy mismatch. Snapshot route fixing fails Wrong snapshot handle, unavailable route index, unsupported domain, or non-integer quantity. JSON refuses infinity/NaN Network model/option serialization is strict; use finite model bounds and valid options. Validation can occur in a Python wrapper, during native preparation, or duringpricing. Low-level errors can be RuntimeError; routing/network input errorsoften use ValueError or TypeError. Preserve the full error message and asmall reproducer instead of treating every error as an infeasible model.

title: pyBaldes troubleshooting and reproducibility
heading: Interpret solve outcomes
text: Interpret solve outcomes Fractional routes are expected in a root LP. Use the appropriate integerworkflow for a dispatchable plan. Root Optimal does not prove an integer optimum. Unknown certified bounds remain unknown even if the numerical bound is finite. Empty heuristic pricing output does not establish an exact pricing minimum. enumerate() on low-level Solver does not prove complete universe coverage. A network enumeration failure leaves ordinary pricing/search available; inspectfailure, complete, and coverage_cutoff before using an integer-transfer result. A user-supplied upper bound or cutoff is not itself a validated feasible plan. If objectives disagree across Python and CLI, match customer count, explicitmatrix weights, rounding, NG construction, cuts, bound mode, and backend first.Python uses the instance's rounding by default; CLI routing uses tenth.Published root benchmark reproduction requires --rounding none.

title: pyBaldes troubleshooting and reproducibility
heading: Concurrency and lifetime
text: Concurrency and lifetime Routing solve releases the GIL during native solving. Freshsolve(..., tree=True) also releases it. Shared root solves and callsthrough NetworkNode retain it; node handles are thread-bound and must remainon their creating thread. Low-level Solver calls currently retain the GIL, soPython threads do not imply concurrent low-level native pricing. Low-level Route owns its returned data and survives solver destruction. ANetworkNode owns its snapshot and can survive deletion of the root result.JSON export omits the native node and cannot be used to resume it. For independentworker processes, construct/install model state in each process rather thanpassing native handles as if they were serializable Python records.
