title: Scalar resources
heading: Python and default Rust builds
text:
Python and default Rust builds With make config, edit Scalar resource dimensions; the saved key isCONFIG_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS (default 2). These APIs use one capacity fixed when the library is compiled. SetBALDES_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS to change it; leaving it unset selects 2: BALDES_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS=5 cargo build --release --features clp
BALDES_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS=5 maturin develop --features clp
 Use baldes::DEFAULT_RESOURCE_DIMENSIONS in Rust orpybaldes.resource_dimensions in Python to inspect that capacity. Creating or registering more resources returnsan error. Rebuilding is required to change the capacity; there is no finite menuof runtime specializations. Explicit Rust types such as Graph::<9> workindependently of this setting.

title: Scalar resources
heading: Resource semantics
text: Resource semantics Every active coordinate participates in extension, dominance, forward/backwardjoins, route reconstruction, enumeration, branching, resource knapsack charges,conservative path domains, and exact incumbent checks. A main disposable resource has nonnegative arc consumption and may wait to reacha lower bound. Pricing also supports signed consumption on non-main disposableaxes; a negative increment can make waiting necessary to enter the next vertexwindow. Equality resources accumulate signed consumption without waiting. Arcwindows constrain the head state after extension. Initial values default tosource lower bounds. Backward equality search requires fixed sink windows;price selects forward search when those are not fixed. Bucket indexing uses at most two selected axes, independently of scalar capacity.A resource above index one can be the main axis through Graph::main_resource.Positive EngineControls::steps or Solver::bucket_steps select additionalnonnegative disposable axes; at most one joins the main axis. Signed secondarydisposable axes stay in exact extension, dominance, joins and route replay butare not discretized. Resource-group branching and resource-load zero-arcpropagation also decline signed axes when their proof requires nonnegativecumulative loads. Unselected resources still participate in feasibility anddominance. More active resources can retain more nondominated labels and increasetime and memory. Existing resource-kind, NG, budget, and certificate-eligibilityrestrictions still apply.

title: SIMD dispatch
heading: SIMD dispatch
text: SIMD dispatch Documentation index The optional simd feature enables four-label AVX2 dominance scans.simd-avx512 includes it and enables eight-label AVX-512F scans on Rust 1.89+.Both features are off by default. Runtime detection keeps binaries portable:AVX-512F (when compiled in), AVX2, then the portable implementation. Scansshorter than 16 remaining labels use the portable implementation. With simd, rank-one local-search bitset accumulation also uses AVX2 onsupported x86-64 CPUs for differences spanning at least 16 u64 words.The kernel widens integer AND/OR operations through compiler vectorization;slice bounds checks remain in place, and floating-point gain calculationsretain their order. Short bitsets and other CPUs use the portable loop.simd-avx512 includes this AVX2 bitset path; only dominance uses AVX-512F. The AVX-512F kernel uses ordered comparisons, retains the exact EPSILONaddition/subtraction order, and returns the first matching label or prefixkey stop in storage order. It widens eight packed u16 NG masks into eightu64 lanes without requiring AVX-512BW, VL, DQ or VPOPCNTDQ. All loadedcolumns are checked before pointer loads; tails use the scalar kernel.The comparison tests exercise direct AVX2/AVX-512 paths and runtime dispatchagainst an independent scalar reference, including NaNs, infinities,subnormals, signed zero, epsilon boundaries, offsets and incomplete blocks.

title: SIMD dispatch
heading: Build configuration
text: Build configuration See the build guide for Cargo features and saved Make settings.SIMD is optional and disabled by default; kernel timings alone do not establishan improvement in complete solver performance.

title: Coupled resources
heading: Coupled resources
text: Coupled resources Coupled resources run in the existing physical-graph labeling framework. Installselected/binary value domains, simultaneous pickup/delivery, cumulative costs,bounded affine or piecewise-linear dependencies, base-state maps, andstate-dependent costs, and free-entry interval-cost fronts with Graph::set_coupled_resources,Solver::set_coupled_resources, or Python ResourceModel.install.No graph expansion or separate pricing front is used by this path.Paired pickup-before-delivery constraints are outside the requested scope.

title: Coupled resources
heading: Resource definitions
text:
Resource definitions Absolute nonnegative objective coefficients are supported for cost-bearingpaired descriptors through set_coupled_objective_coefficients. Extension,canonical joins and independent cost certificates use the same coefficient;physical selected values and feasibility remain unchanged, including at zeroweight. With Clp, the graph setter also accepts negative coefficientsunder either normalization in source-domain models. JSON/Python networks usecoupled_objective_coefficients pairs to invoke the same setter; a resourcebound to an original pricing variable takes its cost from that variable instead. Relative costs subtractthe global initial-front minimum before scaling; they do not subtract theinitial value chosen by a route witness. The shared master independentlyencloses this baseline and prices alternative controls, including maxima.Ordinary minimum-front pricing and physical-path cutoff inspection rejectnegative models. Negative machine-front coefficients remain unsupported.Tiny coefficients are applied directly, without a q - 1 adjustment that could erase them. Control-point PairedPiecewiseLinear descriptors accept an explicitnormalization, using the same conventions as raw slopes. The default isfinal_minus_initial_minimum; select absolute_final_value for a physicalterminal-value objective. The Python add_paired_piecewise_linear builderaccepts the same keyword. Empty paths have zero charge under either convention. An original variable can bind an absolute-final-value paired descriptor (raw slopes or control points)with a finite cost (negative costs require a source model). Reporting reads the column's selected value throughOriginalColumn; arc-only reporting rejects such bindings. Source-domain pairedshared rows accept signed coefficients. Pricing bounds minimum/maximum terminalcontrols and retains row-boundary proposals through the common coordinator.Bounded terminal LPs also propose joint row targets across resources, physicalpaths and networks, retaining fixed routes and signed master contributions.Each target requires its own replayed source control. Integer witness recoverycan replace fractional control mixtures with registered or newly queried pointsand integer copy blocks. It validates the entiresolution, including other networks, fixed routes, master variables and columncaps. With simultaneous service, recovery returns the jointly certified scalarschedule and checks the resulting column identities against caps and retainedcoverage. Proposal failure supplies no infeasibility proof or enumeration coverage.Source paired bindings also support verified variable envelopes and integeractivity registration. Integer proofs must cover every control: a boundedinteger recurrence or singleton integral terminal enclosures on every coveredpath suffice. Integral minimum/maximum endpoints alone do not. These bindingsuse the existing mapped branch rows and tree replay; ambiguous proofs rejectregistration. Custom/cumulative registrations keep their signed row/branch contracts. Reconstructed routes retain coupled_values, ordered pairs of coupleddescriptor index and selected physical dependent value for cost-bearing pairedresources. These values participate in route identity and survive snapshots,canonical schedule copies and model/Python output. They stay physical underobjective normalization or phase-I cost suppression. Without explicit sourcecontrols they describe the minimum-front choice; selected values alone are notan independent control certificate. Paired shared-row pricing generates explicitsource controls for alternative terminal values.With the Clp feature, PairedControl { resource, base } retains one explicitsource trajectory: the initial base coordinate and one head coordinate perphysical arc. CoupledKernel::certify_paired_control checks that descriptor'sstrict source domains, arrivals, waiting, clamping and dependent bounds usinga shared work budget and deadline. Its physical terminal enclosure is independentof objective coefficients, normalization and phase-I suppression. It can certifya nonminimal control on a path whose optimized front selects another value.Knot functions use their real linear interpolants; a verified exact affineidentity may tighten a point enclosure. This does not claim reproduction ofthe numerical evaluator's rounded interpolation sequence.PairedControlCertificate::certifies_value accepts only singleton enclosures;being inside a wider enclosure does not prove attainability. A rejected control does not prove the path infeasible. Arithmetic ambiguity orbudget exhaustion returns unknown. This certificate covers one source descriptor,not other resources, graph continuity/scalar windows, master rows, a globalminimum or the alternate machine-front domain. Route.coupled_controls retains explicit source choices alongsidecoupled_values. Selected values determine identity alongside scalar schedules;controls retain the witness and survive pool transfer,snapshots, fixed routes, tree import and Rust/JSON/Python reporting. Ordinarypricing still emits minimum-front choices. Route::with_paired_controls provesand reprices a supplied control; NodeSnapshot::with_route_controls retainsan alternative for an existing physical route through the shared pool. Acomplete/cutoff universe cannot be widened this way. Explicit route controlsrequire singleton source certificates and are rejected for machine-front modeldomains; the standalone source verifier remains a separate contract.certify_with_controls checks supplied choices on controlled descriptors andordinary independent certificates on the remaining resources. With Clp, master::controls::optimize_paired_control generates source choicesfor a fixed path by covering all declared PWL regions and growth/clamp branches.NodeSnapshot::optimize_route_control applies the same search to a registeredroute. It supports minimizing/maximizing physical dependent value and an optionalterminal window. LP primal points are proposals; independent source replay checksevery returned control. Finite-matrix dual bounds cover regions, and a separatephase-I bound is required to reject a numerically infeasible region. Exact guardedcoefficient construction avoids silently rounding a different source model. ControlOptimization.complete reports full region coverage with a feasiblecontrol or proved emptiness. A complete feasible result can retain a nonzeroprimal/dual gap: lower_bound bounds Gamma for minimization and -Gamma formaximization. Limits and unsupported arithmetic leave the result incomplete;a partial result may still contain a valid control. work_used andlp_iterations let callers share budgets across queries. This bounds one descriptoron one path. Paired shared-row pricing combines these bounds with the physicalpath relaxation, other resource certificates and correlated objective/rowexpressions to bound the whole original column. It shares a work/iterationbudget and deadline across paths and returns incomplete when coverage fails.Paired envelopes cover every source control, independently of the currentobjective or shared rows. Declared terminal bounds can tighten outward LPbounds without a tolerance. Bounded integer recurrences can also supplyconservative envelopes when path enumeration is unavailable. General continuouspaired integrality, machine-front controls and larger unproved domains remain open.Enumeration can retain invariant terminal values or an independently certifiedattained endpoint that weakly improves both cost and every row. Negative costsfavor maxima, positive costs favor minima, and zero costs allow either direction.Row signs and inequality senses must agree with that direction: increasingGamma helps a positive lower-bound row or a negative upper-bound row. Equalityrows and opposing requirements still need invariant values. Identity-specificcolumn caps disable endpoint projection. Base controls may vary continuously;pricing, envelopes and enumeration share their min/max and recurrence proofs.Uncertain or unattained endpoints leave transfer incomplete without a partialuniverse. Exact common factors in source LP rows are removed only when everycoefficient and the right-hand side divide exactly, allowing tight endpointcertificates without a numerical tolerance.A new paired row can reuse a full universe after proving either invariantmatching values or that every retained value remains a certified dominatingendpoint for the objective and all old/new rows. The entire new row is checkedtogether, including repeated terms. Restrictive caps on retained identitiesblock endpoint replacement; fixed copies require point certificates. Cutoffuniverses and rows requiring discarded controls remain rejected. Pool and incumbent validation require stored paired values to match canonicalnumerical replay or supplied independently verified source controls. Scalar/path-onlyhelpers ignore that metadata for auxiliary proof columns; budgeted full-resourcereplay honors supplied controls. Canonical metadata alone does not certify the selected control independently. For graphs containing only custom/cumulative coupled descriptors, forwarddominance also uses a finite-horizon signed proof when the physical graph isacyclic, or an explicit walk cap or complete elementarity proves a finitecontinuation horizon. Bounds and dominance share that prepared horizon.Consistently signed weights determine the state order, even with signedincrements or negative prefix costs. Directed magnitude bounds must prove everyfuture state, charge and cost sum finite. Mixed-sign weights require equalstates unless an integer-lattice envelope proves every intermediate operationexact; then a bounded continuation charge may consume the numeric prefix gap.Cycles without a proved horizon, weighted activity objectives and uncertain overflow retain theconservative comparison. This proof does not spend a physical-cost gap. For signed custom/cumulative programs on DAGs, pricing supplies the currentvertex to the same comparison. Prepared descendant summaries exclude arcs thatcan only occur before that vertex, preserving both signs of genuinely reachablefuture weights. Rust callers can use dominance_penalty_at_vertex for thiscontract; the context-free dominance_penalty keeps its global envelope.Unsupported cyclic or heterogeneous programs retain the global proof. Backward comparisons with vertex context use the existing propagatedsource-to-vertex numeric entry envelopes in their outward suffix correction.This can prove fractional comparisons when the global entry box is too broad;it does not assume that signed prefixes are nonnegative or suppress roundingallowances. Route-cap updates refresh these propagated domains together withthe horizon for both original and auxiliary pricing kernels. Backward custom/cumulative comparisons also tighten suffix corrections onproved integral programs. Reachable entry-state envelopes are intersected withthe integer lattice, and both correction dot products and their difference mustfit the exact binary64 integer range. Those comparisons need no floating-pointrounding allowance. Fractional coefficients, unknown domains and largerintermediate sums retain the outward correction bound. All per-arc vectors use the original graph's arc vector order, includingarcs into the sink. They do not use physical arc IDs as array indices.Multiple resources compose in declaration order. Resource Transition Charging Retain continuous earliest-departure time over remaining energy, consume travel energy, enforce service windows, and optimize partial charging with station-specific PWL curves. PairedPiecewiseLinear Retain a dependent front over a base coordinate, compose strictly FIFO total-arrival functions, optimize waiting, enforce function-valued dependent bounds. Feasibility and two restricted cost modes are explicit. IntervalCost Choose one shared initial value in the initial interval; on every arc add its increment, enforce state/charge domains, and charge the PWL function. Minimize the full route sum over that choice. SlopeIntervalCost Retain prepared slope segments through translation, restriction and addition, with an explicit front-operation policy. SlopePaired Retain prepared slope relations with general arrival composition, waiting and function-valued bounds, explicit operation policy and absolute-final or final-minus-initial cost normalization. Runtime validation is deferred. Selection Intersect the remaining value domain with arc and vertex masks; reject an empty domain. Up to 64 values are supported. Optional vertices gives one mask per vertex. Forward extension checks the head; backward extension checks the tail. With relaxed, an unremembered vertex resets the domain to initial after checking feasibility, forgetting earlier arc and vertex eliminations. By default (BALDESselectionTighteningSchedule 1) the routing master follows the reference schedule: per resource it takes the minimal violating interval ending at an improper path's first violation, remembers those no longer than BALDESmaxNGaverNeighbourhoodSize (or else the path's shortest one), and skips tightening while BALDESmaxNGneighbourhoodSize is negative. Schedule 0 remembers all minimal violating intervals. Remembered intervals include both endpoints. This also applies with omitted vertex masks. Incumbents always use the exact rule. SimultaneousPickupDelivery Deliver before picking up at each stop, with all route deliveries loaded at departure. Enforce capacity at departure and between all stops, admitting loads up to capacity + tolerance (default 1e-6, also used by load dominance; 0 is exact). CumulativeCost Update x += increment[arc], then add x * weight[arc] to the objective. Optional sink_upper and source_upper are the resource's upper bounds at the sink and source. With nonnegative data, dominance reads sink_upper as a bound on the weight of any completion (a forward label with a larger x pays (x_a - x_b) * sink_upper) and source_upper as a bound on the increments of any prefix (backward labels). CustomResource Zero-initialized cumulative state and cost: x += increment[arc], then charge x * weight[arc]. Optional forward_bound and backward_bound provide independent dominance constants. No vertex transition or hard state bounds. Dependent Update y += offset[arc] + factor[arc] * parent_after; reject values outside the declared closed bounds. The parent must be an earlier numeric resource. PiecewiseLinearDependent Update y += function[arc](parent_after) within the function's finite argument domain, then enforce the dependent state bounds. PiecewiseLinearResource Replace x with function[arc](x_before), enforcing the input domain and output window. PiecewiseLinearCost Add function[arc](parent_after) to the objective without changing the parent. The function domain remains a constraint in phase I. For simultaneous pickup/delivery the state is total deliveries D, net pickupsminus deliveries N, and the greatest prefix value M of N, including zero.After a service (d,p), update D += d, N += p-d, M = max(M,N) and requireD+M <= capacity. This is sufficient for the completed route: its departureload is D, and its maximum load is D+M. Increasing D at a later stop alsochecks the load required at earlier stops. Two independent delivery/pickuptotals would miss that constraint. Deliveries and pickups must be nonnegative. Cumulative weights, increments and affine dependency coefficients may be signedbut must be finite. Arithmetic overflow is reported as an error. Dependencies usethe parent's value after its transition on the same arc, and do not wait orclamp to bounds. These are explicit modeling contracts; arbitraryexternal dependency-type conventions are not asserted to have identical semantics. CustomResource exposes the fixed cumulative-style custom family separately fromCumulativeCost. It shares the numeric kernel, joins, dependency handling anddirected path certification, but always starts its state and objective at zero.Signed finite increments and weights are allowed. forward_bound promises anupper bound on the total weight of any completion; backward_bound promises anupper bound on the increments of any prefix. These optional constants only helpdominance with nonnegative increments and weights. They do not impose hardfeasibility limits, and omitting them keeps conservative dominance. Both must befinite and nonnegative when supplied. Rust uses CoupledResource::CustomResource { increments, weights, forward_bound, backward_bound }. Python usesmodel.add_custom_resource(increments, weights, forward_bound=None, backward_bound=None).For example, increments [2, 1] and weights [3, 4] charge 2*3 + 3*4 = 18.The JSON descriptor retains its own kind: {"kind":"custom_resource","increments":[2,1],"weights":[3,4],"forward_bound":7,"backward_bound":3}
 There is no initial parameter. This descriptor is a built-in numeric costresource; use CoupledPlugin for extension-defined feasibility callbacks. Piecewise-linear functions have at least two knots [argument,value], strictlyincreasing finite arguments, and finite adjacent argument/value differences.They are continuous and may increase, decrease or have flat segments. Exactknots return the supplied value. Interpolation uses (x-x0)/(x1-x0), theny0 + t*(y1-y0), clamped to the segment's endpoint value range to preservemonotonicity despite rounding. Outside-domain arguments are infeasible; noextrapolation, resource waiting or state clamping is introduced.

title: Coupled resources
heading: Explicit slope encodings for numeric resources
text:
Explicit slope encodings for numeric resources The encoded numeric variants preserve the supplied function representation:EncodedPiecewiseLinearResource, EncodedPiecewiseLinearDependent, andEncodedPiecewiseLinearCost. Existing knot-based variants and their constructorskeep their current behavior. A slope function is evaluated with ordered segmentmultiply/add operations, rather than converting it into argument/value knots.Those two evaluation methods can differ for fractional arguments. Prepared slope pairs have a distinct layout: the first pair is(value_at_lower, lower_argument); each remaining pair is(slope, segment_end). A single prepared pair is a point function. An affineinput pair instead means (intercept, slope) and must be prepared over a domain;it is not a point or a knot pair. from pybaldes import EncodedFunction, ResourceModel

function = EncodedFunction.slope_segments(
    [(2.0, 0.0), (3.0, 5.0), (-1.0, 10.0)],
    policy="strict_domain",
)
assert function.value(2.0) == 8.0
assert function.value(7.0) == 15.0
assert function.value(11.0) is None
copy = EncodedFunction.from_dict(function.to_dict())

model = ResourceModel()
resource = model.add_encoded_piecewise_linear_resource(
    initial=0.0, lower=0.0, upper=100.0,
    functions=[function],  # One function per physical arc, in insertion order.
)
 strict_domain rejects arguments outside the exact stored domain.endpoint_tolerance explicitly selects the recovered endpoint comparison policy,which may snap arguments just inside or outside the endpoints. It does not applythat tolerance to other resources or interior knots. Both policies reportnonfinite/intermediate overflow as an error. An outside-domain result is None;a genuine function value of 1e12 remains a value. Dictionary/JSON round tripsretain the encoding and policy and validate their contents. Raw-domain image, preimage and directed-certificate proofs remain conservative.Unknown bounds retain candidates; endpoint-tolerance preprocessing must not discardaccepted near-boundary states using the nominal endpoints. Phase I still enforcesfunction domains while suppressing objective contributions. Raw interval andpaired-front support is separate work and is not provided by the numeric variants.The implementation and tests are written, with compile checks completed; runtimevalidation of this new API is deferred at the user's request during concurrent work. SlopeIntervalCost provides a separate free-entry interval resource using preparedslope functions. The Python builder isadd_slope_interval_cost(initial_lower, initial_upper, lower, upper, increments, functions, policy="strict_domain"). Functions must be slope-encoded; knotconversion is rejected. The alternate operation policy front_algebrarequires functions with leaf policy endpoint_tolerance; strict_domain requiresmatching strict leaves. This keeps function evaluation and front operationchoices explicit. Each forward extension translates the coordinate, restricts the allowed domain,adds the charge front and scans its segment endpoints for a minimum. Backwardlabels retain ordered suffix replay for the final joined objective. Unprovedoperations produce an explicit incomplete result. Forward dominance acceptsbitwise-equal fronts, ordered by the independent scalar prefix costs. Understrict_domain it otherwise accepts only identically zero fronts when everycharge is zero or costs are suppressed in phase I; such a front dominates wheneach of the other's components lies in one of its components. Unequal costlystrict fronts never compare, because translation and addition re-round segmentspans and can reverse a current pointwise order. Under front_algebra acovering front may exceed the other by delta, with values within the referencetolerance counted as equal, and pays delta plus the difference of currentminima; this follows the reference's tolerant front comparison and is a parityrule rather than a binary64 proof. Backward labels compare only with identicalsuffix programs. Completion bounds, fixing and certificatesremain conservative. The result is aminimum of the computed front algebra, not a promise of a global minimum overevery sequential binary64 evaluation of the source program. Compile checks pass;new runtime regressions remain deferred.

title: Coupled resources
heading: Free-entry interval costs
text:
Free-entry interval costs IntervalCost { initial, bounds, increments, functions } retains a continuouspiecewise-linear cost function in each physical label. Unlike a deterministicbase state, its initial value is chosen over the whole route. Minimizing each arcor each half independently is invalid: charges x and -x on [0,4] jointlycost zero, although their independent minima sum to -4. Forward extension shifts the cost frontier by the arc increment and adds thecharge at the arrival state. Backward extension pulls the suffix frontier andcharge back through that increment. Joins intersect domains and minimize the sumat the common state, correcting the independently minimized prefix/suffix costs.Signed increments, signed/nonmonotone continuous charges, singleton feasibleintersections, and multiple independent interval resources are supported. Initialand global windows must be finite, nested closed intervals. Every arc has oneincrement and one charge function. Charge domains remain constraints in phase I. These fronts participate in pricing, original-cost replay, cuts, fixing,enumeration, retained repricing and node forks. CoupledLabelState::interval_cost_frontsexposes the current knots in declaration order. A frontier cannot be a numericdependency parent because it has no single arrival value. Reversal reuse remainsdisabled for this family. Production dominance normally requires equal costfronts. Domain inclusion is sufficient for the restricted all-zero front withzero future charges; frozen-front comparisons additionally require independentscalar and resource accounting. A current normalized front difference alone isnot a certificate for future rounded additions. Completion caches do notapproximate missing frontier correlations. Floating-point operations can report arithmetic failure. A translation that mergesdistinct frontier knots is rejected rather than silently dropping a cheaperinitial choice. Directed witness replay supports conservative objective intervalsfor exact integral state translations, argument knots and window endpoints withinits bounded exact domain; other cases return unknown. These intervals may beloose and do not establish an original-domain pricing certificate. This is an explicit additive-transition interval-front contract. Use the pairedrelation below for function-valued transitions with waiting. Raw externaldescriptor import and tolerance parity are separate work. from pybaldes import ResourceModel

model = ResourceModel()
model.add_interval_cost(
    initial_lower=0.0, initial_upper=4.0, lower=0.0, upper=4.0,
    increments=[0.0, 0.0],
    functions=[[(0.0, 0.0), (4.0, 4.0)],
               [(0.0, 0.0), (4.0, -4.0)]],
)
# Install on a two-arc physical graph: the joint resource charge is zero.

title: Coupled resources
heading: Paired function relations and waiting
text:
Paired function relations and waiting PairedPiecewiseLinear { initial, initial_base, arcs, mode } retains the leastattainable dependent value at every feasible base coordinate. The initialfunction describes the dependent value over the initial base window. EveryPairedResourceArc supplies total base arrival(t), departure-dependentincrement(t), head-dependent lower(x) and upper(x), and an integerwaiting slope. Arrival must be strictly increasing and satisfyarrival(t) >= t. It is the total arrival coordinate, not the consumption alone. For departure base t and a chosen head base x >= arrival(t), the least nextdependent value is max(previous(t) + increment(t) + waiting * (x - arrival(t)), lower(x))
 It must not exceed upper(x). Function domains also constrain the departureand head coordinates. Waiting choices, lower-bound clamping and disconnectedfeasible intervals are retained in the front; choosing one locally cheapestarrival would lose valid routes. Waiting provenance is retained per piece. PairedResourceMode::Feasibility adds no objective and permits function-valuedbounds. CostUnbounded permits signed increments and waiting slopes but requiresconstant dependent bounds shared across arcs; its name does not remove thosebounds or the finite base domains. CostBounded additionally requires positiveincrements, nonnegative waiting slopes, and an initial function no lower thanthe shared lower bound. Both cost modes use normalization: the defaultfinal_minus_initial_minimum subtracts the initial minimum;absolute_final_value charges the physical terminal minimum. An empty path costs zero. These restrictionsdo not apply to the existing signed IntervalCost contract. Forward extension builds the full relation. Backward labels retain an orderedphysical suffix program; joins apply that suffix to the actual forward relation.This preserves lower-bound clamping and waiting without assuming that they havean additive inverse. A feasibility adjoint is available internally, but backwardcost joins currently use replay and can cost more than a specialized suffixenvelope. Completion bounds remain conservative. Forward feasibility dominancerequires a front that covers the other front and stays below it; backwardfeasibility dominance compares known upper fronts by coverage and the oppositevalue order. Numerical comparisons use absolute tolerance 1e-4 or relative2.22e-10. Cost-unbounded fronts with an upper bound of at least 1e12 cancompensate a higher front through a cost penalty, provided the independentscalar and resource cost orders also hold. Reversal reuse is disabled. This is a numerical resource contract. Arithmetic ambiguity or excessivefront work produces an error; it is never converted to infeasibility or acomplete-pricing claim. Directed path certification uses an independent outwardreachability relaxation and checked control witnesses. A proved witness givesfeasibility and an enclosure of the optimum charge; an empty outer relaxationproves infeasibility. A failed witness search, uncertain boundary or exhaustedshared budget remains unknown. Numerical optimized fronts are not proof inputs.A non-singleton objective enclosure can bound a column but does not establishexact finite-MIP objective encoding. Raw external descriptor compatibility isnot claimed. Phase I suppresses objective charges while retaining dependenttransitions and feasibility. Python exposes the same contract throughResourceModel.add_paired_piecewise_linear(initial_lower, initial_upper, initial, arrivals, increments, lowers, uppers, waiting, mode="feasibility", normalization="final_minus_initial_minimum"). Functionarguments are lists of (base, dependent) knots; each per-arc vector uses theoriginal arc order. waiting contains signed 32-bit integers. Mode strings are"feasibility", "cost_unbounded", and "cost_bounded".The complete network example isexamples/networks/paired_piecewise_linear.json.Its two required physical routes contribute paired costs 7 and 5. Waiting coefficients represent signed 32-bit runtime values. In the retainedmodern MetaSolver artifact, registration stores a binary64 coefficient, thenboth directional extension wrappers truncate it toward zero to that integertype. BALDES exposes the integer runtime parameter directly. Retained comparisonfixtures include nonlinear functions and cases where this conversion changesthe optimum. For FrontAlgebra, aligned affine fronts can retain a single rounded crossingwith a nonconstant lower bound using the observed encoded-continuity ordering.Strict-domain crossing checks remain separate. A feasibility-only raw pairedresource can also prove a preserved first-endpoint witness across unit FIFOtranslations when its full-front certificate is unavailable. This provesexistence with zero objective charge; it does not certify an objective minimumor widen the default source-domain proof. The separate raw SlopePaired variant uses prepared slope functions for everyfunction role. Python exposesadd_slope_paired(initial_lower, initial_upper, initial, arrivals, increments, lowers, uppers, waiting, mode="feasibility", policy="strict_domain", normalization="absolute_final_value"). All functions must be EncodedFunctionslope encodings with leaf policies matching the operation policy, as forSlopeIntervalCost. The existing knot builder retains its stated delta cost. Rust callers using front_algebra can supply per-arc accumulated-base waitingwindows with Graph::set_paired_waiting_windows. Supply one finite orderedwindow per physical arc, already intersected with its destination vertex'sbase-resource window. The bounds are distinct from the domains of thedependent lower and upper functions. Reinstall them after replacing theresource definitions or changing graph topology. The recovered zero-lengthwaiting path remains limited to the supported bound and provenance cases.When a physical scalar resource represents that base coordinate,Graph::set_paired_waiting_windows_from_resource constructs the intersectionfrom the destination and arc bounds. It rejects empty or disconnectedmulti-time windows and uses finite -1e12/1e12 defaults for absent arc bounds.For the modern CLI/Python network model, supplypaired_waiting_base_resources as (coupled_resource_index, scalar_resource_index) pairs instead. For example, JSON accepts"paired_waiting_base_resources": [[0, 1]] and Python acceptspaired_waiting_base_resources=((0, 1),). The field defaults to empty;duplicate paired indices are rejected. Backward raw paired labels also retain a numerical upper front when theprepared adjoint can compute one. Rust callers can inspect these fronts withCoupledLabelState::slope_relation_backward_fronts; an absent front means theadjoint was unavailable or empty. The adjoint applies the dependent bounds,reverse waiting envelope, base map and dependent increment using the raw sloperepresentation. Its result is advisory: it does not certify source-controlfeasibility or replace ordered suffix replay when joining labels.slope_relation_backward_outcomes_with_budget can recompute the outcomes witha caller-supplied work and time budget instead of reusing a cached unknown. For a nonempty raw cost route, absolute_final_value charges the final dependentminimum, including the initial value. The alternatefinal_minus_initial_minimum subtracts the initial minimum. A fresh root chargeszero under both conventions. Phase I suppresses this objective while keepingdependent transitions and bounds. Raw paired forward dominance compares covering fronts under the selected policy.In cost_unbounded mode with front_algebra and no reachable upper bound(every upper at or above the 1e12 marker), a front may instead exceed the otherby delta and pay scale * delta plus the objective difference, following thereference's shifted-front comparison. This is a parity rule under the recoveredtolerance, not a binary64 proof; strict_domain keeps exact coverage.In feasibility mode with strict_domain, backward labels also retain an upperfront when the slope functions can be converted into knot functions withoutchanging their stored segment slopes. Unsupported conversions, singletonfunction domains, terminal upper bounds above the 1e12 numerical infinitymarker, and failed adjoints leave that upper front unknown; joinscontinue to replay the physical suffix. Different suffix programs can dominateonly when every active feasibility relation has a known upper front and noother resource requires replay-dependent comparison. front_algebracontinues to use suffix replay without this backward dominance optimization. The raw implementation retains front-operation provenance and uses a correctrunning-minimum waiting envelope. The name front_algebra selectsrecovered arithmetic/comparison choices where supported; it does not promisereproduction of the reference's underpricing on accepted nonconvex waitingfixtures. A computed front minimum, a source replay and a directed global pricingcertificate remain distinct. Strict-domain paired slopes can use the independentdirected control certificate described above, preserving their ordered slopeencoding. Exact dyadic standalone slope fronts also have independent operatorcertificates under the strict policy. Native raw interval certificates independently interpret the declared machinefront program from the original descriptors. Software binary64 arithmeticchecks translation, reanchoring, native coordinate alignment and summed-slopemerges, topology and the full endpoint scan. Native addition retains the firstnear-equal summed slope and extends its endpoint; the strict policy retainsseparate pieces. Production optimized minima are never proof inputs. Default raw interval feasibility additionally requires an independent sharedsource-control witness, replayed with outward arithmetic inside the hard andsource domains. Failure to find that witness is unknown. A computed emptyfront alone cannot prove default source infeasibility; only an independentempty source-domain relaxation can do so. Native paired defaults retain theirindependent source-domain certificates where supported. Rust callers can explicitly select a different original model withgraph.set_front_program_domain(true)?. For native raw interval andpaired resources, this defines feasibility by the checked ordered IEEE frontprogram. It is a model-domain change, not a proof hint or an assertion ofsource-control/exact-real equivalence. Strict and other resource families keeptheir stated semantics. The default is false. Graph clones, node forks andcost suppression preserve the choice; replacing resource descriptors resetsit. The graph and kernel getters expose it. kernel.certify_front_program(arcs, &mut work, deadline) checks that alternatemodel and returns a FrontProgramCertificate without changing a defaultgraph's domain. Its result cannot replace the default source-feasibilityguard. has_machine_front_contracts() identifies native raw resources;has_machine_cost_contracts() identifies objectives for which a source-controlabstract bound is insufficient. Per-route certificates and complete finitecollectors remain available independently. A checked component machine value is not a minimum of sequential source-controlreplay or of an exact-real control problem. Other resource and arc contributionsstill require outward aggregate bounds, and exact finite-MIP cost encodingretains its separate guard. Unproved operations, arithmetic overflow,unsupported topology and exhausted proof budgets remain unknown. The native-front composition policy handles in-domain start snapping,tolerance-sized constant intervals, near-knot segment advancement, and theseparate near-equal-slope merge rules for outer knots and inner endpoints.These choices do not change strict_domain arithmetic. A point front alreadysatisfying constant bounds can retain nearby bound-domain endpoints when itlies inside their exact intersection. Tolerance does not extend a disjoint domain. Runtime checks include direct coupled/paired route tests and selected originalbinary helpers. The October 24 comparison matched 1,600 finite composition casesand 36,872 extended-label insertions with nonempty cut descriptors. These arebounded operator/consumer checks, not complete resource or solver equivalence.Near-disjoint domains, unproved bound crossings and other unsupported numericalcases still return explicit incomplete outcomes. Evidence and reproductionartifacts are retained locally underresults/metasolver-parity-fixes-20261024/.

title: Coupled resources
heading: Python
text:
Python For Python installation, declaration order, method signatures, and complete examples, see pyBaldes resource modeling. from pybaldes import ResourceModel, Solver

solver = Solver(4, 0)
for tail, head in [(0,1), (1,2), (2,3), (0,2), (2,1), (1,3)]:
    solver.new_arc(tail, head, -1.0)
model = ResourceModel()
model.add_simultaneous_pickup_delivery(
    capacity=4.0,
    deliveries=[0,4,0,4,0,0],
    pickups=[4,0,0,0,4,0],
)
model.install(solver)
minimum, routes = solver.price(50)
assert routes[0].nodes() == [0,2,1,3]
 add_selection, add_cumulative_cost, add_custom_resource, add_dependent, andadd_piecewise_linear_dependent install the otherresource families through the same model. Route.original_cost reports theoriginal coupled objective; Route.cost reports its priced cost. The shared network JSON interface, used by baldes solve and PythonPricingNetwork, accepts an optional coupled_resources list and optionalelementary flag. Each descriptor uses a kind tag: {
  "coupled_resources": [
    {"kind": "selection", "initial": 3, "allowed": [3,3,3,3,3,3]},
    {"kind": "simultaneous_pickup_delivery", "capacity": 4,
     "deliveries": [0,4,0,4,0,0], "pickups": [4,0,0,0,4,0]},
    {"kind": "cumulative_cost", "initial": 0,
     "increments": [1,1,1,1,1,1], "weights": [1,1,1,1,1,1]},
    {"kind": "dependent", "parent": 2, "initial": 0,
     "bounds": {"lower": 0, "upper": 100},
     "offsets": [0,0,0,0,0,0], "factors": [1,1,1,1,1,1]}
  ],
  "elementary": true
}
 This is a fragment of a pricing network, not a complete model. Python acceptsthese same descriptors in PricingNetwork(coupled_resources=(...), ...).The specialized CVRP/VRPTW text instance readers do not infer these quantities. For example, the additional JSON descriptor below defines one physical arc'spiecewise function. Supply one function for every physical arc: {"kind": "piecewise_linear_dependent", "parent": 0, "initial": 0,
 "bounds": {"lower": 0, "upper": 100},
 "functions": [{"points": [[0,0], [2,1], [4,3]]}]}
 The corresponding Python method accepts functions=[[(0,0), (2,1), (4,3)]].Parent indices always refer to the same resource declaration list. Base maps usekind: "piecewise_linear_resource" with initial, bounds, and functions;state costs use kind: "piecewise_linear_cost" with parent and functions.Python provides add_piecewise_linear_resource and add_piecewise_linear_cost.Base maps can express state-dependent consumption, waiting, saturation and resetsexplicitly by their knots; the engine adds no implicit waiting or reset rule.

title: Coupled resources
heading: Label operations and current limits
text: Label operations and current limits Charging uses ChargingResourceArc entries in physical arc-vector order.Each entry supplies travel time/energy, a service-start window, service duration,and an optional cumulative energy-to-time curve. Curves strictly increase from[0,0] through the battery capacity. The initial energy and departure time areexplicit. Stations also constrain charging completion by closing time. The fullcontinuous front survives; backward joins replay their retained suffix on theactual forward state. Front work is bounded per extension and exhaustion returnsan error. Charging adds no cost, is not a numeric dependency parent, usesconservative equality dominance, and disables reversal reuse. Directed pathcertification declines this family, including in phase I. See theEVRP adapter for end-to-end pricing andschedule reconstruction. Selection labels carry the remaining domains. Simultaneous load labels carrycomposable delivery/net-load/peak summaries. Forward numeric labels carry actualvalues. Backward numeric labels carry affine entry conditions and a cumulativecost function; a join evaluates them at the forward label's actual values.Kernels containing piecewise dependencies instead retain shared continuationprograms for numeric constraints. A join replays that suffix from its actualforward entry values. Composition therefore adds a shared link rather thanmultiplying piecewise regions, and flat/nonmonotone functions need no inverse.Cumulative cost remains affine in its independent numeric coordinates; thesekernels cache diagonal cumulative-cost maps in linear per-arc space.State-dependent nonlinear charges are kept out of the backward baseline andreplayed at the actual forward entry state during joins. Each suffix carries anexact-sum interval, an absolute charge bound and a count; these provide an outwardroundoff allowance for the ordered charge sum without rescanning the wholesuffix to build a bound. Unknown/overflowing envelopes disable cost pruning.Affine-only kernelsretain the dense precomputed-map fast path. Shared programs have iterativerelease to avoid recursive destruction of long paths.Dependency constraints are therefore not tested at an invented backward arrivalvalue. All original scalar coordinates and cut/branch states still participate. Numeric transitions are prepared once per physical arc when resources areinstalled. Forward programs retain declaration order with resolved parent slots;backward programs cache the triangular affine map, offsets, entry conditions andcost coefficients. Label extension composes the cached map with its suffix.This trades per-arc storage (quadratic in numeric resource count) for avoidingrepeated matrix construction. Phase I rebuilds the cached cost terms with zeroweights while preserving the resource transitions and constraints. A symbolicmap overflow is recorded and reported if backward extension uses that arc;it does not prevent finite forward replay. Dependency preprocessing first checks each arc's declared entry/exit windows.It then propagates source-reachable numeric intervals forward and sink-compatibleintervals backward through the full graph. Rounded-addition preimages areexpanded before subtraction. Direct base-map preimages use bounded searches overordered binary64 arguments on each segment. They preserve flat portions,nonmonotone branches and rounding plateaus without requiring an algebraic inverse;segments already entirely inside the target range bypass the searches. Piecewise argument domains participate in bothpasses. Arcs with empty necessary domains are disabled without renumbering thephysical graph. The work limit is at most 64 paired passes; each descendingiterate is conservative, so stopping early only weakens pruning. Unknownarithmetic retains candidates. kernel.preprocessing() reports pass count,convergence and usable-arc counts; route_arc_possible reports the necessarycomplete-route filter for an arc. replay/replay_state still evaluate standalonepartial resource paths without the complete-route filter. Resource dominance now uses directional orders. A forward simultaneous state(D,N,M) can dominate another when all three coordinates are no larger; backwardfeasibility only needs D and M, so backward net load may differ. Selectedvalue domains use superset dominance. Forward dependency dominance propagatespossible comparison directions through the earlier-parent chain. A smallerstate is allowed when the lower window is protected by nonnegative increments;a larger state is allowed when nonpositive increments protect the upper window.Negative factors reverse the parent comparison. Competing effects retain bothpossible directions and must satisfy both protections, otherwise dominance isrejected. Preparation encloses every intermediate operation over declared andprepared numeric domains, and unequal comparisons require finite arithmetic.Both entry states must lie in those domains. Equality remains available whenthese sufficient conditions cannot establish an order; backward conditions keepthe existing identical-expression/window-implication rule. Piecewise slopesigns participate in forward order propagation when the prepared parent domainis contained in every arc function's domain. Backward nonlinear comparisonsrequire identical continuation programs before applying cost compensation. Aflat function still constrains its parent through the argument domain; outputequality does not erase that constraint. Unbounded cumulative parent comparisonsalso retain directional guards against overflow unique to the dominator.Direct base maps retain equality dominance until a whole-map feasibility orderis established. Parents of arbitrary nonlinear cost functions retain equality(including differences induced by ancestors), so cost-free numeric comparisonscannot discard a better future objective. Charged-resource dominance separately orders physical scalar reduced costs andaccumulated numeric costs before considering the mixed label key. Equal numericinputs retain the repaired baseline rule. Unequal inputs can use a preparedzero-compensation proof for cumulative-cost models, optionally combined withselection and simultaneous loads: nonnegative increments and weights permit0 <= a <= b; nonpositive increments and weights permit b <= a <= 0.Both cones produce ordered nonnegative future charges, and the dominator'saccumulated numeric charge must also be nonnegative. Zero-weight coordinatesretain directional overflow guards. Signed cases outside those cones retainconservative equality conditions. Dependency/domain checks remain mandatory.Composite numeric/dependency models keep the baseline identity rule because thebroader checks did not improve the measured workload. No positive current-keymargin or cost compensation is spent by charged forward dominance. Backward dominance requires identical continuation programs, compatible entrywindows and numeric state, with its outward coefficient-difference bound whereapplicable. Unknown arithmetic retains both labels; an overflow during actualextension is reported rather than silently proving route infeasibility. Completion pruning now includes an outward lower bound on the cumulative joincorrection. The engine builds direction-wide hulls of actual retained numericstates and suffix cost coefficients after labeling. Individual bucket scansuse narrower per-bucket hulls, while inherited completion minima keep thebroader hull that includes predecessor candidates. Per-bucket compatibilitychecks also use selected-domain unions, simultaneous-load envelopes andsupported backward affine entry conditions. Skipping one bucket's scan neverskips its predecessor traversal. Each completion query fixesits own state and bounds the opposite states. This works with signed coefficientswithout assuming a finite walk length. The two dot products in the implementedjoin are enclosed separately, preserving their floating-point evaluation scope.Missing hulls or arithmetic overflow leave the bound unknown and retain thecandidate. These bounds are used by pricing, completion, fixing and directionalenumeration; they are not scalar-only original-domain certificates. Hulls are rebuilt after fresh/continued labeling and discarded on new pricing,continuation or node forks. If elementarity or physical topology changes afterresource installation, reinstall the definitions so prepared dominance domainscannot become stale. Replacing the resource preparation also invalidates labelsat unchanged scalar arc costs. Forward-prefix reversal reuse is available for symmetric selection masks andsimultaneous loads with symmetric physical-arc quantities, integral deliveriesand pickups, and capacity at most 2^52. Uniform-sign net increments retain theoriginal compact reuse rule. Mixed signs additionally track an internal suffixpeak R = max suffix net load, updated by R = max(0, R + pickup - delivery).Reversing the arc sequence swaps prefix and suffix peaks; publicload_summaries() remains (D,N,M). Mixed-sign reuse builds a union of the two feasible prefix orientations. Eachload resource retains a prefix while D+M <= capacity or D+R <= capacity.With several resources this may retain extra prefixes whose feasible orientationsdiffer; every complete join still checks all resources in the actual physicalroute orientation. Dominance preserves both roles through ordered D,N,M,R.Standalone extension/replay and ordinary backward labels remain strictly feasible.Single-orientation completion hulls, completion-existence fixing and arbitraryordinary completion callbacks cannot certify this union, so those pruningoperations conservatively decline in the mixed reuse path. The scalar resource/depot symmetry checks and conservative reduced-cost potentialchecks must also pass. Numeric and PWL resources, fractional loads, asymmetricresource events and presence rows retain ordinary directional labeling.Phase-I cost suppression does not make a numeric resource reversible. Pricing,fixing and enumeration use the same eligibility rules. Arithmetic failuresinvalidate completion instead of proving that no route exists. The physical graph retains its ordinary 1024-vertex limit. There is no extra1024-state expansion limit on this production path. Labels remain subject tonormal label, time and path limits. A cyclic graph without a justified routelength/resource bound can still exhaust those limits. Integer witnesses use outward interval replay for coupled feasibility andobjective contributions. A straddling boundary or unsupported arithmetic remainsunknown. Encoded knot/slope numeric programs include independently enclosedendpoint-snap branches. Plugins can opt into CoupledPlugin::certify, whichmust independently prove original-domain feasibility under the caller's workand deadline; its default returns unknown. Ordinary numerical plugin transitionsdo not supply proof. Charging supplies independently checked explicit targetsand relaxed necessary-condition propagation; failure to find a target remainsunknown rather than infeasible. For numeric and interval costs, a polynomial directed walk relaxation propagatesstate/objective enclosures over the original physical graph up to the integerroute contract's vertex-simple hop limit. It can retain a cost certificate whenliteral path enumeration exceeds its limit. Unsupported objective operators,overflow or exhausted proof work still return unknown. Original-domain scalarrelaxation collectors and additive-costcertificates do not silently claim support for coupled resources. Generalexternal dependency-type semantics and exact native dominance/bound policiesare not claimed to match the reference binary.

heading: Multiple time windows

title: Multiple time windows
heading: Python and network JSON
text:
Python and network JSON Build Python with maturin develop --features multi-time-windows (or add thatfeature to the existing wheel build). The stateful solver exposes: solver.set_vertex_time_windows(1, 0, [(8.0, 12.0), (16.0, 20.0)])
 For Python network models, use PricingResource(time_windows=...) with oneentry per vertex: from pybaldes import PricingResource

time = PricingResource(
    bounds=[(0.0, 30.0)] * 3,
    time_windows=[None, [(8.0, 12.0), (16.0, 20.0)], None],
)
 None entries use ordinary bounds. The field survives network JSON round tripsand is omitted when unset, allowing ordinary models on builds without the feature.Window validation and normalization take place in Rust when solving the model. Network JSON, built with clp,multi-time-windows, accepts time_windows on aresource: one entry per vertex, each either null (ordinary bounds) or a nonemptylist of [lower, upper] pairs. For a three-vertex network: {
  "kind": "disposable",
  "time_windows": [null, [[8, 12], [16, 20]], null],
  "bounds": [[0, 30], [0, 18], [0, 30]]
}
 When both fields are supplied, bounds intersects the union; the second intervalin this example is effectively [16, 18]. Without the build feature the JSON fieldis rejected as unknown, rather than silently ignored. Solomon and CVRPLIB fileformats retain their existing input semantics; use the graph API or network JSONfor disjoint windows.
