title: Multiple time windows
heading: Implementation and validation
text:
Implementation and validation Forward transitions choose the first admissible value at or after arrival;backward transitions search from the last interval and clip at the head beforesubtracting consumption and projecting onto the tail domain. Both intersectvertex and arc restrictions. These transitions are shared by pricing, replay,canonical path collection and elementary enumeration. Exact incumbent validationalso applies union membership using its exact arithmetic. Bucket propagation projects across gaps, and component/reachability constructionincludes the image of a whole bucket cell. A discontinuous waiting jump can thusreach a later interval without being pruned by an adjacency built for the hull.If a far cell endpoint is infeasible, the image uses a conservative hull bound.Backward bucket arcs retain both phase flags, since a gap can cross thehalfway boundary inside one input cell. Actual label resources select the phase.This can create extra dependencies and increase preparation work; no performanceimprovement is claimed. Consumption-symmetric prefix reuse is disabled on graphswith configured unions, because hull symmetry alone does not justify timereversal. Ordinary forward/backward labeling remains available. Tests compare bucket pricing with independent exhaustive integer path scheduleson randomized DAGs and elementary cyclic graphs. Regressions cover earliest andlatest projection, gap rejection, arc intersections, terminal domains, effectivesink bounds, zero-width windows, nonindexed resource coordinates, normalization,topology invalidation, halfway continuation, enumeration, JSON loading, and exactincumbent witnesses. Validation commands: cargo test -p baldes --features clp,multi-time-windows,simd --lib --test multi_time_windows --test main_pricing --test fixing_enumeration --test accumulated_resource --test porting_regressions
cargo test -p baldes --lib --test main_pricing --test fixing_enumeration --test accumulated_resource --test porting_regressions
cargo clippy -p baldes --lib --test multi_time_windows --features clp,multi-time-windows,simd
 The Python regression in python/tests/test_multi_time_windows.py passes againstthe feature-enabled extension and skips on wheels without it. Test builds usedCARGO_PROFILE_DEV_OPT_LEVEL=0, CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0, andCARGO_INCREMENTAL=0. Modified Rust files pass rustfmt. The broader Clippy runincluding all unit tests hits existing denied approx_constant andabsurd_extreme_comparisons lints in unrelated tests; targeted Clippy completeswith repository warnings.

title: P-step CVRP and VRPTW extension
heading: P-step CVRP and VRPTW extension
text:
P-step CVRP and VRPTW extension Documentation index baldes::extensions::pstep implements the compact continuous relaxation inProposition 1 of A p-step Formulation for the Capacitated Vehicle RoutingProblem, Dollevoet, Munari and Spliet. The extension is available without Cargo features. Solving requires animplementation of Baldes's LpMaster, such as Clp (--features clp). cargo build --release --features clp --bin baldes
./target/release/baldes pstep instances/cvrplib/P-n16-k8.vrp --p 2 --threads 4
./target/release/baldes pstep instances/cvrplib/P-n16-k8.vrp --p 3 --threads 4 --enumerate --json pstep.json
 Use baldes pstep --help for time, iteration and label limits. --enumeratechecks the bound against the complete column pool; use it on small cases.The JSON separates a converged full-model lp_bound from a potentiallynonconverged restricted_objective. A work-limit error cannot certify a bound.Neither output is an integer routing solution. The fleet is unlimited even ifthe CVRPLIB instance name or header specifies a conventional truck count. Rust callers can use Problem::from_instance on a parsed inputs::Instance.It preserves the input's distance rounding. Then callProblem::solve_column_generation with an empty LpMaster andColumnGenerationOptions; pricing.p and pricing.threads control the stepsize and CPU parallelism; pricing.method selects Auto (default),Enumeration, or Bucket. The older examples/pstep.rs illustrates full-poolconstruction, and examples/pstep_cvrp.rs produces CSV benchmark records. Create a Problem with customer demands, vehicle capacity and a directed costmatrix. Matrix indices are start depot 0, customers 1..=n, end depot n+1.For a conventional single-depot instance, copy depot-to-customer costs intorow 0 and customer-to-depot costs into column n+1. None means no arc.Customer demands must be strictly positive; capacity and supplied costs mustbe finite, with nonnegative costs. The model has an unlimited homogeneous fleet. Problem::enumerate builds the complete column pool for a supplied positivep. Every partial path is elementary and capacity feasible. Paths have exactlyp arcs, except those starting at the depot, which may be shorter. Empty depotroutes are omitted. At large p, the pool contains full routes and depotprefixes; flow conservation forces incomplete prefixes to zero. The compact prior-demand choices are zero for depot starts, maximum feasibleprior demand for depot ends, and both extremes for internal paths. Coincidentextremes are stored once. A junction customer's demand belongs to both adjacentpaths; the load coefficients account for this overlap. Formulation::entries exposes sparse columns in this row order: Rows Coefficient Sense / RHS 0..n Customer degree (1 at endpoints, 2 internally) = 2 n..2n Start +1, end -1 = 0 2n..3n Start d + q_i, end -(d + q(path)) >= 0 Formulation::into_master populates an empty LP backend with nonnegativecontinuous columns. Solve through the backend's status and time-limit API.An optimal solve gives the full p-step LP bound to solver tolerance. At p=1this has the single-commodity flow bound; at p>=n+1 it has the set-partitioningbound. Bounds need not increase at every successive p; the paper guaranteesnondecrease when p is replaced by an integer multiple. The reference enumerate implementation has combinatorial cost. Both columncount and search work are bounded by EnumerationOptions. Hitting a limitreturns an error instead of returning a restricted pool as a complete model.It is intended as an exact column-pool reference for small instances and small p. price_steps solves independent jobs for each start, end and prior-demandextreme. The default Auto method uses streaming elementary enumeration whenp<=6 and the dense prefix estimate 1+n+...+n^(p-1) is at most 100,000;otherwise it uses the core bucket-graph labeling engine. This is a boundedsize heuristic, not a prediction that one backend always wins. Capacity andmissing arcs prune enumeration further. Enumeration retains just the bestpath per job, so it does not build the full column pool. Both methods solvethe same exact pricing problem and enforce work/time limits. Use --pricing enumeration or --pricing bucket to compare a specific case;--enumerate remains the independent full-pool LP cross-check. --labelslimits generated labels for bucket pricing and attempted extensions forstreaming enumeration. JSON reports these separately as generated_labelsand enumerated_extensions, and records the requested and selected methods.Exceeding either budget aborts pricing without certifying convergence. For bucket pricing, hop count is an equalityresource, preventing artificial waiting from creating extra arcs. Capacity isdisposable: every load window has lower bound zero, so waiting never helps anda cheaper label using less capacity safely dominates. Reduced costs use actualcustomer demands, not any resource waiting. Customer startsrequire exactly p arcs; depot starts allow 1..p. The fixed endpoints and extrememake the reduced cost additive along arcs, including degree, endpoint and loadduals. Each returned path is replayed against the master coefficients. Workers share immutable instance costs and duals. Each owns its searchstorage and results. Results are merged in fixed job order and all threadsjoin before the main thread updates the LP. threads=1 runs the same pricingalgorithm, making serial/parallel results reproducible. Parallel overhead mayoutweigh the benefit on very small cases. The solver starts with degree artificials, uses exact pricing to complete phaseI, and then switches to travel costs. Convergence requires every pricing jobto finish without a negative reduced-cost step at the requested tolerance.Steps are deduplicated by node order and prior demand. LP columns are added inbatches. Restricted-master objectives are not full-model lower bounds untilpricing converges. Reported bounds are numerical, not independently certified. For p<=3 the path topology itself enforces elementarity. For p=4, a relaxedbucket solve is sufficient when its minimum is elementary. Otherwise, pricingpartitions by the first arc and forbids later returns to its head. Each resultingfour-arc path is elementary; every feasible elementary step belongs to onepartition. The relaxed minimum also bounds these partitions. Longer steps useexact cycle exclusion around bucket solves: a cyclic relaxed minimum branches onforbidding each arc of a detected cycle. Every elementary path lies in at leastone child; relaxed costs bound each child. This avoids the core's 15-elementlocal NG mask limit. It can still require exponential work for larger p.PricingOptions bounds total labels and bucket subproblems per endpoint job,as well as worker count and time. Exceeding a pricing limit returns an error. Time windows, cuts, integer solving and integration with Baldes'sbranch-and-price tree are not implemented here. For integeroptimization of this compact model, impose binary aggregate arc flows, asin equations (7)–(9); making extreme p-step columns binary is not equivalent.The exposed paths and coefficients provide the data needed for a separatearc-flow integrality implementation. Run node scripts/benchmarks/benchmark_pstep.mjs ./target/release/baldes from the repositoryroot to repeat the known-instance validation and serial/parallel timing checks.It writes raw JSON and CSV records under results/pstep/ (override withPSTEP_OUT) and comparesevery bound with full column enumeration. Add --grid to run p=2,3,4 on all three bundled CVRPLIB instances, with fourworkers, 120 seconds per solve and five million labels per endpoint job. Gridrecords go under results/pstep-20261020/p234/. Reference enumeration is omittedfor the larger p=4 pools and A-n32-k5 at p=3, whose pool exceeds the CLI's columnlimit. Pricing stops are recorded explicitly, without a claimed LP bound. The validation runs gave these numerical bounds (four workers, developmentprofile). The normal CVRP column uses default root NG-route pricing; the integervalues were obtained separately with the normal tree solver. Instance p=2 LP p=3 LP p=4 LP Normal CVRP root LP Integer optimum P-n16-k8 408.968169 434.947541 441.000000 441.000000 450 E-n22-k4 336.229510 344.079301 351.662163 373.500000 375 A-n32-k5 672.464631 678.388776 Time limit 757.983333 784 The A-n32-k5 p=4 run stopped at 120 seconds without a full LP bound. The othereight cases converged; six also matched complete-column enumeration within1e-5. The A-n32-k5 integer solve used capacity cuts, rank-one cuts and aone-second HGS warm start before closing the gap at 784. Compare backends with node scripts/benchmarks/benchmark_pstep_pricing.mjs. It alternatesbackend order over three repetitions, checks converged bounds agree, and writesraw JSON and CSV to results/pstep-pricing/ (or the second positional argument). Set PSTEP_RUNS,PSTEP_SECONDS, or PSTEP_THREADS to change repetitions, per-solve limits,or worker count. An optional binary path and output directory are accepted. The 2026-10-21 release comparison used an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X, four workers,three repetitions with alternating backend order, no warmup runs, and fivemillion labels/extensions per job. The binary was built withcargo build --release --features clp --bin baldes (opt-level 3, thin LTO).These are end-to-end solve medians, including the LP; they are local timings,not a guarantee for larger or different instances. Instance p Bucket seconds Streaming enumeration seconds P-n16-k8 2 0.0262 0.0033 P-n16-k8 3 0.1658 0.0044 P-n16-k8 4 0.5595 0.0089 E-n22-k4 2 0.1812 0.0372 E-n22-k4 3 1.7307 0.0658 E-n22-k4 4 18.36 0.32 A-n32-k5 2 0.6490 0.1771 A-n32-k5 3 10.7781 0.3635 A-n32-k5 4 Time limit 2.47 The initial run used a 15-second limit; the extended run allowed 20 seconds.E-n22 p=4 needed the extended limit. Converged backend bounds agreed within1e-5. Enumeration also converged for A-n32 p=4 at 691.463021739; this is anumerical p-step LP bound. The larger p=4 full-pool model was not independentlysolved for that instance. Raw records, binary/input hashes, and compilermetadata are under results/pstep-pricing-20261021/final/ and verified/.

title: P-step CVRP and VRPTW extension
heading: Experimental CUDA pricing
text:
Experimental CUDA pricing Build with an NVIDIA CUDA toolkit (nvcc on PATH) and a working CUDA driver: cargo build --release --features clp,cuda --bin baldes
./target/release/baldes pstep instances/cvrplib/P-n16-k8.vrp --p 3 --gpu --rounding none
cargo test --release --features cuda --lib extensions::pstep
cargo run --release --features cuda --example pstep_gpu_bench
python3 scripts/benchmarks/benchmark_pstep_cuda.py
 --gpu is the CLI shorthand for --pricing cuda. PricingMethod::Cuda runs exact elementary enumeration for each endpoint/loadextreme on an NVIDIA GPU. It supports effective p <= 6, uses double precision,and preserves CPU enumeration traversal and tie order. It is opt-in; Autokeeps selecting CPU methods. The LP and reduced-cost replay remain on CPU.threads applies to CPU methods; CUDA reports zero CPU pricing workers. The prototype allocates and transfers data each round. Timing includes thesecosts, synchronization, and result replay. Runtime errors and extension limitsabort the entire round. The deadline is checked after synchronization: an activekernel is not preempted, and an over-budget result is discarded. Large p orlarge dense instances can therefore overrun a requested wall-clock limit. The synthetic benchmark warms every configuration once, then alternates fivemeasured rounds on identical problems and duals, comparing every returned path.The CVRPLIB script uses three fresh-process runs per configuration, alternatesCPU/CUDA order, fixes rounding to none, and checks converged LP bounds.

title: P-step CVRP and VRPTW extension
heading: Time windows
text:
Time windows The CLI automatically enforces finite service-start windows in Solomon inputs: cargo build --release --features clp,cuda --bin baldes
./target/release/baldes pstep instances/Solomon/C201.txt --p 3 --gpu --rounding none --json c201-gpu.json
./target/release/baldes pstep instances/Solomon/C201.txt --p 3 --pricing enumeration --threads 16 --rounding none --json c201-cpu.json
cargo test --features cuda,clp --test pstep_vrptw
cargo run --release --features cuda --example pstep_vrptw_bench -- instances/Solomon/C201.txt instances/Solomon/C202.txt
 Rust callers use TimeWindowProblem::from_instance. TimeWindowProblem wrapsthe existing CVRP data and adds windows and service durations for both depotcopies and every customer. Travel duration equals travel cost, in the same unitsas the windows. Finite ordered windows and nonnegative service times are required.Auto uses CPU enumeration; Cuda uses the GPU; bucket pricing is currentlyunsupported for this model. CUDA still requires effective p <= 6. The master has four blocks of n rows: degree, endpoint flow, cumulative load,and service-start flow. A timed step contributes its start time positively atits first customer and its end time negatively at its last customer. Servicestarts of outgoing steps must therefore cover incoming end times. This followsthe endpoint-time extension in Vaes (2022), sections 3.2–3.3. For a fixed path, propagation represents its earliest end service time asmax(start + transit, barrier). transit includes service on each arc's tail;barrier accounts for waiting. Latest feasible starts are bounded by everyvisited due time. Pricing considers the nondominated earliest schedulingbreakpoint and the latest feasible start, together with the existing loadextremes. This retains compatible time assignments in the master instead ofonly filtering individually feasible segments. The result remains an unlimited-fleet LP relaxation, with no integer routecertificate. The JSON identifies problem: VRPTW and time_windows_enforced.A converged LP bound is distinct from a restricted-master objective. GPU/CPUcomparisons must use identical rounding; the examples explicitly use none.

title: P-step CVRP and VRPTW extension
heading: Measured Solomon comparison
text: Measured Solomon comparison On a Ryzen 9 9950X and RTX 5090, three fresh-process runs with all 100customers and --rounding none gave these median LP solve times. P-step CPUpricing used 16 workers; the normal solver used its default settings. Instance Default solver P-step CPU p=2 P-step GPU p=2 P-step CPU p=3 P-step GPU p=3 C201 0.127 s 1.031 s 1.187 s 2.612 s 2.053 s C202 8.449 s 2.489 s 2.719 s 7.523 s 5.677 s All CPU/GPU p-step pairs converged to matching bounds. The default solverobtained 591.55655667 for both cases. C201 p-step obtained the same bound;C202 p-step obtained 590.78102398 at p=2 and 591.54926228 at p=3, so itsfaster times do not represent equally strong bounds. GPU startup outweighedpricing savings at p=2. At p=3, warmed, matched-dual pricing rounds were6.96x (C201) and 7.25x (C202) faster on GPU; whole-solve improvements were1.27x and 1.33x because LP solving remained on CPU. Machine details, input/binary hashes, timing ranges and LP boundsrecord the measurements. These timings precede the --gpu alias and integrationof the unrelated imported-pricing update; the measured CUDA and VRPTW algorithmsare identical. The normal solver comparison uses its stronger route LP.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: EVRP implementation status
text: EVRP implementation status Documentation index baldes::extensions::evrp is the initial model and independent schedule replay layer.It supports deterministic directed travel with separate time, energy and cost,delivery capacity, customer service-start windows, repeat charging-stationvisits, and explicit partial charging with station-specific piecewise-linearcurves. Fixed-sequence charging optimization and reference bidirectional directpricing and a two-phase subpath prototype are available. Both feed the sameroute-based LP master and column-generation adapter. Charging curves map energy to cumulative time from empty. Charging from ato b takes T(b) - T(a); charge_for applies the inverse curve and caps atfull charge. Knots must start at zero and increase strictly in both coordinates.Non-concave charging profiles are accepted. Energy and time units are suppliedconsistently by callers. Problem::replay takes an explicit closed route with an amount charged pervisit and an initial departure time. The vehicle starts full. It reports everyarrival, service start, departure and arrival/departure energy, plus totaltravel cost and delivered load. Charging follows station service and mustfinish by closing; customers only require service start within their window.Waiting is allowed and consumes no energy. A route can cover a customer subset,but cannot repeat customers or contain intermediate depots. Comparisons usestrict floating-point bounds with no implicit tolerance. Travel costs must benonnegative; pricing reduced costs are not inputs to this validator. Replay checks feasibility of a supplied charging schedule, not optimalityof its charging decisions. Tariffs, charger congestion, regeneration, mixedvehicle compatibility and station insertion are not implemented.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Fixed stop sequence optimizer
text: Fixed stop sequence optimizer Problem::optimize_fixed_order(order, departure, ChargingOptions::default())chooses continuous partial charging amounts on a supplied sequence of customersand stations. It minimizes completion time. Travel cost is fixed by thatsequence, and charging has no separate monetary cost in the current model.Station visits may repeat; customer visits must be elementary. The algorithm propagates piecewise-affine earliest departure time as a functionof exact remaining energy. At a station, for cumulative charging time T andincoming time function F, it evaluatesT(x) + min { F(q) - T(q) : q <= x }. On each affine interval the minimum isattained at an endpoint or at q = x. All these candidates are generated;their lower envelope is split at domain endpoints and function intersections.The construction permits non-concave charging curves without an energy grid.Time-window waiting is another piecewise-affine operation. Every retained piecekeeps its predecessor and energy mapping for schedule reconstruction. The result distinguishes Optimal, Infeasible, WorkLimit, andNumericalFailure. Optimal is the optimizer's result in floating-pointarithmetic, not an interval-arithmetic certificate. Every returned schedulepasses independent strict replay. Reconstruction that fails replay reportsNumericalFailure, never Infeasible. The work budget counts generated piecesand envelope comparisons; reaching it yields no feasibility or optimality claim.The envelope implementation prioritizes a transparent reference algorithm overlarge-instance speed. Tests compare charging allocations against independent quarter-energy gridenumeration on tiny heterogeneous/non-concave instances whose optimum lies onthat grid, and check waiting, repeated stations, exact windows and work limits.These tests do not establish performance on published benchmarks.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Direct bidirectional pricing
text: Direct bidirectional pricing Problem::price_direct(duals, fleet_dual, departure, DirectOptions::default())prices elementary customer routes with repeatable station visits. The dualvector has one entry per location and must be zero at stations and depots.Reduced cost is travel cost minus customer duals minus one fleet dual. The bestreplay-validated route is returned even when its reduced cost is nonnegative.No subset-row cuts, ng relaxation or branching restrictions are accepted yet. The implementation uses forward earliest-departure functions F(e) andbackward latest-departure functions B(e) at exact departure energy e. Backwardfunctions exclude processing at the meeting node, already processed by theforward label. Internally backward times are negated to share lower-envelopecode. Backward extension undoes charging, station closing, service, customerwindows and travel in the appropriate order. At a station the core operationis max { B(y) - T(y) : y >= q } + T(q) - service, with station closing appliedto departure before charging is undone. Dominance conservatively requires equal visited-customer sets, no greaterreduced cost, no more used arcs and pointwise time dominance over the entireother function's domain. The function comparison covers domain gaps andinterior crossings; endpoint-only scalar tests are insufficient. Joins requirecompatible customer sets, capacity, total arc count and some common energywith F(e) <= B(e). Both directions retain energy mappings for reconstruction;every returned complete route passes strict schedule replay. This is an E1-inspired reference implementation of the coherent functionextension/dominance/join approach described byNafstad, Desaulniers and Stålhane (2025), Sections 3–4.The prefix/suffix affine-envelope construction is specific to Baldes's model;the paper's faster PWL algorithm, midpoint-by-time stopping, unreachable-customersets and acceleration techniques are not reproduced here. The current objectiveis travel cost, not the paper's separate route-duration extension. Pricing statuses are explicit: Bounded: all customer-serving routes with at most max_arcs travel arcswere covered. This does not certify that longer routes have no negative cost. Complete: that bound covers every relevant route, using customerelementarity when there are no stations, or a conservative depot-horizonbound when all available non-self travel times are strictly positive. WorkLimit / NumericalFailure: no pricing completeness claim. Any returnedincumbent remains independently replay-validated. Complete describes exhaustive model coverage in f64 arithmetic, not a rigorousreal-number reduced-cost certificate. No station-repeat bound is inferred fromzero-time travel. Nonnegative-cost self loops are omitted because they cannotimprove a schedule or customer coverage. Work/label limits and arc limits areconfigurable. Both directions currently grow to half the arc bound and comparecompatible label pairs; this prioritizes correctness evidence on tiny casesover large-instance speed. Tests compare minimum reduced costs to exhaustive stop-order enumeration withthe fixed-order optimizer, with dominance enabled and disabled. They also checkcapacity, customer elementarity, zero-time travel, work limits, bounded versusglobal coverage, and domain-interior dominance failures.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Two-phase subpath prototype
text: Two-phase subpath prototype Problem::price_subpaths(duals, fleet_dual, departure, SubpathOptions::default())uses the same objective, dual convention, route arc limit and completenessstatuses as direct pricing. Phase one generates elementary customer ordersbetween depot/station endpoints with no interior charging. It retains all suchorders fitting a full battery and load capacity, including direct charger-to-charger moves with no customers. max_subpaths caps this phase explicitly. Phase two composes these subpaths into complete routes. It propagates theentire continuous time/energy function through every constituent customer andendpoint, optimizes charging, and checks customer elementarity and capacity.It may prune a prefix only with equal customer history, no greater reduced cost,no more arcs and full function-domain dominance. Subpaths are never suppliedas master columns. Both backends return the same complete-route representationwith a replay-validated charging schedule. The decomposition is inspired byJacquillat and Lo, v3 (2026).The prototype deliberately retains distinct phase-one orders and carries fullcharging functions in phase two. It does not implement the paper's compressedresource vectors, two-sided subpath domination, adaptive ng relaxation or cuts.Thus it does not assume that scalar forward domination can replace the paper'sdomination requirements. Keeping the full prefix state makes composition anexplicit dynamic program under this static model; the paper's speedups havenot been reproduced. Tests compare both backends with exhaustive route-order evaluation, under thesame data, duals and arc bounds, with dominance enabled and disabled. Fixturesinclude heterogeneous/non-concave charging, repeated stations, and a route withtwo consecutive charging stops in both directions. Global versus boundedcoverage and phase-one/phase-two work limits have separate checks.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Physical-graph backend
text: Physical-graph backend Problem::price_physical_graph(duals, fleet_dual, departure, PhysicalGraphOptions::default())uses the ordinary Baldes labeling engine. SelectEvPricingBackend::PhysicalGraph(PhysicalGraphOptions::default()) in the shared EV master touse it in both feasibility and travel-cost phases. The reference direct andsubpath backends remain available; the default backend is unchanged. Problem::pricing_graph(...) also exposes the compiled Graph<3> for apricing::Solver<3>. The graph preserves location IDs and duplicates the depotat vertex locations.len() as the sink. Its active scalar resources track arccount and delivered load. Only customers receive elementarity sets, so stationvisits may repeat. A PWL boolean state records whether a customer hasbeen served; the sink requires that state to be one. Customer duals are chargedon incoming arcs and the fleet dual is charged once on source departure.The delivery-only native simultaneous-load resource additionally guards loadfeasibility and dominance without scalar epsilon comparisons. The native CoupledResource::Charging retains earliest departure time as acontinuous function of exact remaining energy. Travel consumes energy; servicestarts inside its window. Stations apply the full partial-charging envelopeT(x) + min_{q<=x}(F(q)-T(q)) and require service/charging to finish by closing.Heterogeneous and non-concave strictly increasing curves are supported withoutan energy grid. Forward labels retain owned front pieces. Backward labels retainthe physical suffix; joins replay that suffix on the actual forward front.Dominance conservatively requires equal charging fronts, and reversal reuse isdisabled. This resource adds no objective and cannot be a numeric parent. After native pricing chooses a stop order, the existing fixed-order optimizerreconstructs its charging amounts and independently replays the schedule. Afailed reconstruction reports numerical failure, never infeasibility or completepricing. max_front_work bounds each individual frontier extension, includingsuffix replay; it is not a total pricing-work budget. max_reconstruction_workseparately bounds witness reconstruction. Label limits and max_arcs bound thenative search. Resource arithmetic/state failures remain unknown; the nativeengine may aggregate a nonzero frontier-budget exhaustion into numerical failure.The work statistic counts witness reconstruction work, not native front work. This adapter supports at most fifteen customers by default, reflecting nativeexact NG local memory (31 or 63 with the ng-memory-31 or ng-memory-63build feature), and at most 1023 input locations because it adds a sink.It uses native numerical resource/cost comparisons. Complete and Boundedretain their numerical coverage meanings; no directed-rounding certificate isprovided for charging. The largest absolute reduced arc cost times max_arcsmust be below 1e12 - 1, because the native engine reserves 1e12 as a sentinel;unsupported scales are rejected explicitly and require rescaling cost units.Cuts and restrictions can be attached to theexposed graph/solver; the shared EV master does not add cut separation or treesearch. The tiny regression comparisons establish agreement on the testedfixtures, with no performance or large-instance scaling claim.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Reproducible tiny comparisons
text: Reproducible tiny comparisons Run cargo run --features clp --example evrp_compare for a CSV comparison ofall three backends with identical data and tolerances (1e-7 for LP and reducedcost). On the checked fixtures: Case Direct LP Subpath LP Full route-pool LP Meaning Three customers, route capacity two, fleet limit two 4.5 4.5 4.5 Fractional weights of 0.5 demonstrate LP rather than integer optimality. Two customers, nonlinear charging required, fleet limit one 5.0 5.0 5.0 Returned routes require partial charging and pass replay. The test reference pool enumerates every tiny stop order and constructs chargingschedules independently on an integer-energy grid. For these integral fixtures,every order with no grid witness is also checked for continuous infeasibilityby the fixed-order optimizer. The full pool LP is built separately from columngeneration, and the fractional case also has an analytic objective of 4.5.Additional tests cover fleet/reachability infeasibility, an empty customer set,seed validation and deduplication, phase-I initialization without seeds,resuming after limits, and bounded/work-limited pricing without convergence. The CSV reports columns, pricing calls, labels, retained subpaths and algebrawork. These tiny reference counts do not establish a runtime advantage orscalability on published instances. Run cargo test --lib evrp:: for model/algebra/pricing tests andcargo test --features clp --lib evrp:: to include shared-master comparisons.

title: EVRP implementation status
heading: Supported scope and remaining extensions
text: Supported scope and remaining extensions The raw ElectricRouting.jl multi-depot data is downloaded underinstances/evrp/electricrouting-jl/:161 instances and 312 upstream reference solutions, pinned to commit102c9c90f6021d2dea664f0d8ad6990661c7668a with per-file hashes. These filesneed a format reader and multi-depot integration before equivalent Baldes runs;they are not inputs to evrp_compare. Their nonlinear charging curves must bespecified separately to match an upstream nonlinear experiment. This implements the initial static, single-vehicle-type travel-cost EV LPworkflow. It is not an integer branch-and-price solver. Cuts, branching/ngstate, mixed fleets, tariffs, congestion, time-dependent travel, externalbenchmark parsers and large-instance performance engineering remain extensions.The E1 reference backend and E2-inspired prototype do not reproduce everyacceleration from either paper. The native backend uses the explicit charging-front resource; scalar resourcepricing alone does not establish nonlinear charging feasibility.

title: Robust vehicle routing
heading: Robust vehicle routing
text: Robust vehicle routing The production robust VRPTW implementation uses the ordinary bucket graphlabeling engine and standard root/tree solvers. Labels carry budgeted demandand travel-time states in addition to their nominal bucket resources. Forwardand backward extension, dominance, and concatenation use those robust states.

title: Robust vehicle routing
heading: CLI
text:
CLI cargo build --release --features clp
target/release/baldes solve instances/Solomon/R112.txt \
  --customers 25 --tree --cuts --robust 1,2,0.5,0.5
 The format is --robust GAMMA_DEMAND,GAMMA_TIME,ALPHA_DEMAND,ALPHA_TIME: GAMMA_DEMAND bounds how many demands can deviate per route. GAMMA_TIME bounds how many travel times can deviate per route. Demand deviations are trunc(ALPHA_DEMAND * demand). Travel-time deviations are 0.1 * trunc(10 * ALPHA_TIME * travel_time)in instance units. For both budgets equal to one, use --robust 1,1,0.5,0.5; for both equal totwo, use --robust 2,2,0.5,0.5. A zero budget disables that uncertainty.Robust Solomon input requires time windows and --rounding tenth, the default.Remove --tree for a root relaxation solve.

title: Robust vehicle routing
heading: Rust and the example
text:
Rust and the example Build robust data with extensions::robust::Problem::from_instance andUncertainty, or supply Node and Travel data directly. Then callProblem::pricing_graph (or pricing_graph_with_memory), construct amaster::routing::RoutingContext, and use master::routing::solve ormaster::tree::solve. The graph retains the budgeted resources throughoutpricing; no separate robust master is needed. The example uses this production path and prints a 36-row root LP sweep: cargo run --release --features clp --example robust_c201 -- \
  instances/Solomon/C201.txt 15 0.5
 Arguments are the instance, customer prefix, and relative deviation for bothuncertainties. Each budget ranges over 0,1,2,3,5,10. The example uses fullcustomer NG memories to price elementary routes, with cuts and enumerationdisabled. It shares the CLI's Solomon conversion, including integer-scaledtime resources. CSV status names come from the standard CG solver; Optimaldenotes completion of the root LP, not an integer optimality claim. lp_boundis NaN when artificial activity remains positive or the solve is incomplete.

title: Robust vehicle routing
heading: Independent validation reference
text: Independent validation reference extensions::robust::reference retains the independent forward-only elementarylabeler and minimal LP master for small-instance checks: reference::price compares pricing minima with the bucket graph engine. reference::RobustMaster compares elementary LP objectives. Problem::replay checks individual routes against the uncertainty recurrences. Production code should use the bucket graph path above. The former root-levelRobustMaster, pricing types, and Problem::price remain as deprecatedcompatibility entry points. New validation code should import referenceexplicitly. Removing compatibility entry points is deferred until the fullbenchmark sweep and migration checks are complete. Regression tests compare forward-only and bidirectional bucket pricing againstboth brute-force enumeration and the independent reference, including sparseasymmetric arcs and nonzero depot indices. Separate tests check every routesplit for robust concatenation and compare bucket-root LPs with the referencemaster.

title: Robust vehicle routing
heading: Table 7 solver sweep
text:
Table 7 solver sweep cargo build --release --features clp --bin baldes
python3 scripts/benchmarks/benchmark_robust.py \
  --output results/robust-table7 --jobs 4 --time 60
 The default grid uses the first 25 customers of C1/R1/RC1 Solomon instances,excluding R101–R104 and RC105 as specified in the local paperpapers/munari_robust.pdf, pages 24–25. Each of the 24 remaining instancesgets one nominal solve and 54 uncertainty settings: demand-only, time-only,and joint uncertainty, each with Γ = 1…6 and α = 0.10, 0.25, 0.50. This is a solver screening pass with a 60-second limit per case. The paper'slimit was 3,600 seconds; use --time 3600 to match it. --instances R112selects a smaller smoke sweep. The output directory must be new so earlierresults are preserved. The runner copies the tested binary and records its hash, source/input hashes,settings and commands. It writes per-case logs, solver JSON, independent replayresults, results.csv, and summary.json. Replay checks exact customer cover,fleet size, route costs, worst-case demand, and worst-case service-start timesin integer tenth units. The summary also detects contradictions between lowerbounds and feasible incumbents as uncertainty increases. all_optimal requiresall cases to finish Optimal with valid incumbents, closed gaps, and no suchcontradictions. Time limits and incomplete solves remain unresolved. This sweep does not perform the paper's 10,000-realization Monte Carlo risksimulation and is not a reproduction of its risk estimates.

title: Robust pickup and delivery with time windows
heading: Robust pickup and delivery with time windows
text:
Robust pickup and delivery with time windows baldes::extensions::robust_pd models the one-to-one RPDPTW inAbreu, Battarra, Costa and Munari, The robust pickup and delivery problemwith time windows, EJOR 335 (2026), 812–828(paper). The 60 original benchmark files in instances/RobustPDPTW/ contain5–75 requests, in classes AA, BB, CC and DD. Their pinned source and hashesare recorded in scripts/data/robust_pd_manifest.json.Instance files follow the repository's existing policy for local downloaded data.Download or verify them with: python3 scripts/download_robust_pd.py --download
 Run native branch-and-price with Clp: # FILE Γq Γt σq σt SECONDS
cargo run --release --features clp,multi-time-windows --example robust_pdptw -- \
  instances/RobustPDPTW/AA05.txt 1 1 0.1 0.1 60

# Deterministic baseline, retaining the paper's nominal-demand adjustment.
cargo run --release --features clp,multi-time-windows --example robust_pdptw -- \
  instances/RobustPDPTW/AA05.txt 0 0 0 0 60

# NG-route relaxation with 8 requests per neighbourhood.
cargo run --release --features clp,multi-time-windows --example robust_pdptw -- \
  instances/RobustPDPTW/AA05.txt 1 1 0.1 0.1 60 --ng 8
 Pricing is elementary unless --ng N (Parameters::ng_size = Some(N)) isgiven. On 40 benchmark cases with 10–30 requests and 30 s limits,elementary pricing proved 32 optimal and NG 8 proved 31, so NG is opt-in. The example prints termination status, numerical lower bound, incumbent,routes, worst load, and worst return time. It independently replays everyincumbent route and verifies request coverage and total objective.An incomplete or time-limited result is not an optimality claim. The maintained interface is the Rust model and runnable example above. LocalPython/Gurobi formulation experiments may live under ignored working/; theyare not part of a fresh checkout or the public Python solve interface.

title: Robust pickup and delivery with time windows
heading: Model
text:
Model Each request i has pickup i and delivery i+n on the same route, in thatorder. Vehicles start at depot 0 and finish at the distinct depot 2n+1.Every request is served exactly once. The fleet is homogeneous and hasup to n vehicles; departures cost 10,000 by default, as in paper §6.1. At each route position, let O be the set of requests currently on board.Robust capacity is checked using Proposition 1 (paper p. 815): load(O) = sum(q[i] for i in O)
        + sum(the Γq largest demand deviations among requests in O)
 A delivery removes its entire request, including its uncertainty. Alreadydelivered requests do not consume load or demand-uncertainty budget at alater position. This preserves the common demand realization of eachpickup/delivery pair. Travel-time robustness uses the existing BudgetedTime resource and thepaper's equation (6). For each γ from zero through Γt, it retains theworst service start, including waiting and the preceding node's service.Every customer window and the return-depot window must hold. Waiting canabsorb delays, so summing the largest travel deviations alone is insufficient. The physical graph has one vertex per original node. A coupled plugintracks a request memory and the open (on-board) requests, enforcesprecedence and pairing, and checks capacity in both directions. Joinsreplay the suffix against the forward state. A label dominates anotherwith equal open requests and a memory subset; no delivery is skipped, sono triangle inequality is assumed. The weaker subset test on open requestsis unsound here: under budgeted travel times, a shortcut that skips adelivery can be later than the detour. Requests that can no longer bepicked up and delivered in time join the memory, using shortest nominaldurations as lower bounds. The shared master has one set-partitioning rowper request; the pickup contributes its coefficient exactly once. With --ng N, memories are NG neighbourhoods: the request and the N−1requests with the nearest pickups. A route may then pick up a request againafter delivering and forgetting it; such a column covers that request twiceand cannot be integral. The graph declares bounded walks of at most2(2n+1) arcs and the plugin certificate applies the same memory, sowindow-fallback branching keeps NG columns instead of stalling.

title: Robust pickup and delivery with time windows
heading: Heuristic
text: Heuristic Problem::heuristic (example flag --heuristic, using SECONDS as its timelimit) returns robust-feasible routes without branch-and-price. It buildsroutes by cheapest pair insertion, then applies pair relocation, routeelimination, and ruin-and-recreate. Each route caches forward worst-casestarts, the backward thresholds used by pricing joins, and per-positionon-board load summaries, so a placement check costs O(Γt) time work perposition and O(1) capacity work. Problem::replay verifies every acceptedroute. A unit test compares the cached check with full replay on everyplacement of random instances. HeuristicMethod::Genetic (example: --heuristic hgs) is a hybrid. It runsthe same trajectory for 40% of the time, which reduces the fleet mostreliably, then seeds an HGS-style population with its best. Offspring comefrom route-based crossover: some routes of one parent, the other parent'sroutes without already covered requests, and cheapest reinsertion of therest. Children are mutated with probability 0.3, half of the time bydissolving a whole route, and parents are chosen by binary tournament onHGS biased fitness with a broken-pairs distance. On five seeds at 30 s, itreduced travel by about 0.1% on 75-request cases with the same fleet, butfound the smallest fleet less often than the default iterated local searchon two 40-request cases. --seed N sets the heuristic seed.

title: Robust pickup and delivery with time windows
heading: Optional ILS operations
text:
Optional ILS operations HeuristicMethod::ExtendedIteratedLocalSearch(IlsExtensions) selects optionaloperations without changing the default ILS. IlsExtensions::all() enablesregret-2 repair across distinct target routes (including a singleton), removalat a tight load cut or an attaining worst-time segment, transactional pairexchange, non-reversing tail exchange at empty-on-board cuts, and a depth-oneejection chain. Every replacement route passes robust replay. Critical removalis mixed equally with uniform ruin; within critical removal the load and timevariants are equally likely. Pair exchanges sample at most 64 request pairs,tail exchanges at most 128 cut pairs, and ejection scans at most eight shuffledrequests against each other. These are bounded neighbourhood scans rather thanclaims of exhaustive local optimality. Ejection requires a feasible sourceremoval; pair exchange directly checks final routes without this restriction. The example accepts --heuristic extended or one of regret, critical,exchange, tails, and ejection to enable one extension at a time. Theexisting --heuristic ils remains the baseline. For example: cargo run --release --features clp,multi-time-windows --example robust_pdptw -- \
  instances/RobustPDPTW/AA40.txt 5 5 0.3 0.3 10 hundredth --heuristic extended --seed 1
python3 scripts/benchmarks/benchmark_robust_ils.py \
  --output internal/robust-pd/ils-extensions --seconds 2
 The benchmark interleaves methods in reproducibly shuffled order for pairedseeds, records input and executable hashes, and stores every run's output,objective, fleet, nominal travel, and elapsed time. The example verifies requestcoverage and route feasibility. Short runs are exploratory; compare multipleseeds and longer budgets before selecting a default. The requested limit ischecked at search boundaries, and construction or a move scan can overrun it.

title: Robust pickup and delivery with time windows
heading: Input conventions
text: Input conventions Instance::read validates consecutive node ids, signed demand pairs,finite data, time windows, and zero depot demand/service.Problem::new(instance, Parameters) preserves original file data andderives effective demands and deviations separately. Defaults apply the §6.1 adjustment before generating demand deviations:for original request demand q and a=ceil(0.3*q), if q+a > Q, replacethe nominal demand by Q-a. This adjustment also applies in deterministicruns so comparisons share the same nominal demands. SetParameters::adjust_demands=false to use the raw demands.Deviations are ceil(σq*q) and ceil(σt*t). Budgets are nonnegative integers. The coordinate-only files do not explicitly supply a travel matrix. Thedefault uses Euclidean distance rounded to the nearest 0.01 for nominalcost and travel time. This convention matches the upstream workbook'snominal objectives for all four five-request instances; the PDF itselfdoes not specify a coordinate rounding rule. Parameters::distance_roundingcan select DistanceRounding::FullPrecision. The example accepts a finalnone argument for that convention (default: hundredth).

title: Robust pickup and delivery with time windows
heading: Validation and boundaries
text:
Validation and boundaries Regression tests compare replay against exhaustive demand and arc-delayscenarios, compare every forward/backward join split, compare nativepricing against exhaustive routes, and compare the integer master againstan independently enumerated set partition on two requests. All 60 filesare parsed by an opt-in test after downloading: cargo test -p baldes --lib extensions::robust_pd
cargo test -p baldes --lib all_downloaded_instances_parse -- --ignored
cargo test -p baldes --features clp,multi-time-windows --lib extensions::robust_pd
 All 76 five-request configurations listed in the upstream workbook werealso solved to optimality and matched an independent exhaustive route andset-partitioning reference. Of those, 73 match the published objectives.Three differ under the paper's stated ceiling rule for travel deviations:AA05_5_30_5_30, BB05_0_0_1_10, and BB05_1_10_1_10.Those differences disappear in the reference when replacing ceiling byunrounded or nearest-rounded travel deviations. The implementation retainsthe paper's ceiling rule. Details are in the internal evidence directory. This is native robust pricing with a general branch-and-price master.It does not implement the paper's compact MIP, RRCI/RIPEI separators,or its complete experimental benchmark campaign. Exact request historiescan produce exponentially many labels; large-instance scalability isnot established. The pairing/load plugin supplies an independent bounded-work certificateusing outward-rounded load sums. The example uses the master's numericalbound mode; no large-instance bound-certification campaign has been run.The initial twelve-case ten-request smoke test returned five Optimal and sevenIncomplete results. A subsequent shared-master fix closes stalled nodes whentheir selected lower bound rules out improving an existing validated incumbent.It does not treat finite artificial penalties as an infeasibility proof.Repeating all 24 five-/ten-request settings three times now returns Optimal inall 72 runs, with unchanged objectives and independently replayed incumbents.The 21 formerly incomplete ten-request repetitions all close. Evidence andremaining work are tracked inlocal ignored internal/robust-pd/; these are investigation artifacts, not shipped documentation.

title: BALDES IPM in Rust
heading: BALDES IPM in Rust
text:
BALDES IPM in Rust Documentation index · Backend configuration baldes::extensions::ipm implements an interior-point LP solver in Rust. It ispart of the main baldes crate under src/extensions/ipm, requires Rust 1.70+,and has no C++ bindings, BLAS requirement, or unsafe code.Use its direct model API below, or select master_solver="ipm" in apyBaldes routing root solve. From the BALDES repository root: cargo run -p baldes --example ipm --offline
cargo test -p baldes --test ipm --offline
cargo test -p baldes --lib ipm:: --offline
cargo fmt -p baldes --check
 The example minimizes -x - 2y, with x + y <= 3 and x >= 1, andreturns objective -5 at approximately [1, 2].

title: BALDES IPM in Rust
heading: API

title: BALDES IPM in Rust
heading: Source mapping and implementation
text: Source mapping and implementation C++ source Rust module Behavior ip_solver.h, src/ipm/ip_solver.cpp model.rs, solver/ Standard form, homogeneous self-dual Mehrotra loop, upper-bound elimination, adaptive regularization, predictor/corrector and centrality corrections, recovery hipo_ldlt.h factor/mod.rs, sparse_solver.rs::HiPOLDLT Block ordering, symbolic fill, fundamental supernodes, elimination forest, frontal assembly, child Schur updates, restricted 1x1/2x2 Bunch–Kaufman pivots, sign-preserving small-pivot regularization, refinement normal_eq_ldlt.h sparse_solver.rs::NormalEqLDLT SPD normal equations A D⁻¹ Aᵀ + Rd, followed by primal recovery sparse_solver.h sparse_solver.rs::SparseSolver Backend dispatch and structural fill estimate Eigen sparse/dense plumbing matrix.rs, factor/mod.rs Owned sparse CSC input and factors stored as sparse columns; dense arrays only for individual fronts and Schur updates The augmented matrix is [-(theta + Rp), Aᵀ; A, Rd]. The ordering preservesthe primal/dual boundary, and fundamental supernodes cannot cross it. Frontsare processed in increasing elimination order, a valid child-before-parentorder, and child Schur buffers are released after parent assembly. Child updatesstore only the lower triangle, packed by row; parents assemble that trianglewithout copying an unused upper half.Sparse augmented factors may use an up-looking row-update path when theprimal block has at least twice as many variables as rows and symbolic L hasat most 32 off-diagonal entries per system variable on average. This pathexpects negative primal and positive dual pivots; small, non-finite or wronglysigned pivots retry the existing pivoted multifrontal factorization. OriginalKKT refinement remains enabled. Sparse factor columns use contiguous CSC valuesand share an immutable pattern across numerical refactors and clones. Numeric pivot swaps are composed with the symbolic permutation and applied torows of previously assembled factor columns. Iterative refinement uses|b - Kx| / (|b| + |K||x|) with at most two correction solves. Deliberate differences from C++: Ordering keeps the independent diagonal primal block in natural order.Eliminating these vertices cannot connect other primal vertices, so buildinga primal column-intersection graph cannot reduce fill. The dual Schur graphuses deterministic exact minimum degree with explicit graph updates,rather than the shared C++ approximate minimum degree quotient graph.Complete remaining graphs are emitted directly; dense intersection graphsuse packed adjacency (at most 32 MiB), while sparse or larger graphs retaintree sets. Those graph representations produce the same ordering. Primalreordering preserves structural fill but can change floating-point sums. The normal-equations path uses this crate's multifrontal factorization,rather than the external C++ supernodal implementation. Its fixed CSC patternand row-to-column source positions are cached; refactors accumulate valuesdirectly without duplicate triplets or repeated sorting. The comparison backends LDLT, SUPERNOODAL, and FRONTAL from the siblinglinear_system directory are not separately ported or aliased to HiPO. Fixed variables are eliminated. Free variables, upper-only bounds, shiftedbounds, zero columns, mixed senses, objective offsets and row dual signsare tracked explicitly through recovery. Complementarity includes the upper-bound slack/multiplier product. Successchecks primal feasibility as well as dual feasibility and gap. Centrality corrections are added to the current Newton direction insteadof overwriting it. Each correction targets products at the full step and isweighted by the best of nine points in [alpha², 1], following HiGHS HiPO.The homogeneous Schur denominator uses its equivalentpositive quadratic form to avoid subtractive cancellation. Primal and dual regularization start at sqrt(eps) rather than 1, closerto HiPO's small static values. A failed Newton step retries with ten timesthe regularization, as before. A singular 2x2 pivot returns a numerical error instead of replacing onlyits determinant, which would be inconsistent with the stored D block. Ruiz equilibration is implemented and enabled by default (five passes).Each pass rounds its factors to powers of two, so scaling is exact.The C++ header declares scaling routines, but its optimization loop doesnot invoke them. Set scaling_iterations: 0 to disable scaling. The internal objective is normalized after equilibration. Dual recovery anddual/gap checks undo objective scaling, retaining tolerances in originalunits. Wide upper bounds start with feasible slacks and unit complementarityproducts, avoiding a large artificial residual from bounds such as 1e12. A regularized least-squares starting estimate reduces initial row and dualresiduals before positive shifts for the HSD variables. Finite upper boundsretain unit complementarity. Unsafe estimates, empty systems and very tightbounds retain the unit initializer. This adds one factorization and two solvesper eligible LP; it is not a warm start from the previous CG solve. The restricted master selects this solver with --master ipm; the API is alsousable independently. Performance parity with the C++ solver and large-instancerobustness have not been established. Nested dissection is not implemented.

title: IPM factorization: cached assembly and lower-triangle updates
heading: IPM factorization: cached assembly and lower-triangle updates
text: IPM factorization: cached assembly and lower-triangle updates This comparison measures the native Rust IPM before and after the assembly-map,workspace, and dense-kernel changes. The baseline already includes the tree/nodeparallel controls. These are BALDES-to-BALDES measurements, not a comparisonagainst HiGHS timings.

title: IPM factorization: cached assembly and lower-triangle updates
heading: Changes
text: Changes Compute CSC-to-front scatter positions and child-to-parent row maps duringsymbolic analysis. Share immutable maps across solver clones. Retain dense scratch, pivot permutations, multiplier vectors, and outputcolumn capacity across Newton steps. Reset scratch when the symbolic planchanges; solver clones start with independent empty scratch. Update the contiguous lower triangle and read symmetric pivot candidates fromthat triangle. Avoid mirroring the trailing matrix after every pivot. Theprevious full-matrix kernel remains an independent test oracle. Batch tree work over retained scratch buffers. Nested node work uses the samebounded Rayon pool; no workspace lock is held during nested execution. Recycle consumed Schur buffers through a size-binned pool, capped at 8 MiB persolver. The limit covers spare buffers, not live contributions or factors.Releasing consumed contributions avoids retaining every clique on deep trees. Preserve the serial up-looking fast path and release its old compressedfactor before allocating the next output. The dense update is still a rank-1/rank-2 kernel. Blocked panel factorization,relaxed supernodes, and dependency-driven subtree scheduling remain future work.

title: Python wheels and releases
heading: Python wheels and releases
text: Python wheels and releases The Python distributions workflow builds pybaldes wheels for Linux x86-64and ARM64 (manylinux2014), and macOS Intel and Apple Silicon. Wheels use theCPython stable ABI, starting at Python 3.9. Each wheel is installed and testedoutside the checkout on Python 3.9 and 3.14 before it can be released. The standard wheel includes bundled Clp, multi-time-window resources and thedefault master branching policies. It uses portable CPU settings. HiGHS,Gurobi and CUDA require separate source builds; Windows wheels are not currentlybuilt because the bundled native backend configuration targets Unix systems.

title: Python wheels and releases
heading: Create a release
text:
Create a release Set the same version in the root Cargo.toml andpython/rust/Cargo.toml, then refresh Cargo.lock with cargo check -p pybaldes.Python package metadata derives its version from the bindings crate. Commit the release changes and push the commit. Create and push a matching version tag, for example: python .github/scripts/check_release.py --tag v2.0.2
git tag -a v2.0.2 -m 'BALDES 2.0.2'
git push origin v2.0.2
 A pushed v* tag triggers validation, builds all four wheels and a sourcearchive, publishes them to PyPI, and creates a GitHub release with generated notes andSHA256SUMS after PyPI publication succeeds.A failed build or installed-wheel test prevents release publication. The sourcearchive includes the vendored Clp/CoinUtils files, and wheel builds start fromthat archive to check source completeness. Tags must match the Cargo version exactly. Prerelease versions use Cargo syntax,for example 2.1.0-rc.1 and tag v2.1.0-rc.1; maturin normalizes Python packagemetadata. Prereleases are marked as such and do not replace the latest release.Existing releases are not overwritten automatically. Pull requests affecting packaging or solver sources also run the distributionbuilds. A manual workflow run builds and tests artifacts without publishing.The isolated PyPI job uses the repository secret PYPI_API_TOKEN with tokenauthentication. It receives tested artifacts and does not execute repositorybuild scripts. Existing PyPI files are skipped to allow retries after a partialupload. Token authentication does not enable trusted-publishing attestations.Only the GitHub release job has repository write permission; it uses the standardGitHub token.

title: Python wheels and releases
