text:
Install or build Install from PyPI in a virtual environment: python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install pybaldes
 For a local source build, initialize native dependencies first: git submodule update --init --recursive
python -m pip install 'maturin[patchelf]>=1.9.4,<2'
maturin build --release --locked --sdist --out dist
 Local Linux builds use the host's system ABI. Official Linux wheels use themanylinux build container and its portability checks. SeePython bindings for editable builds and optional backends.

title: Stochastic branch-and-cut versus branch-and-price
heading: Stochastic branch-and-cut versus branch-and-price
text: Stochastic branch-and-cut versus branch-and-price scripts/benchmarks/stochastic_branch_cut.py is a directed Pythonreimplementation of Approach 4 (BC-Theta) from Tomazella, Munari and Morabito(2026), not the authors' implementation:https://optimization-online.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Tomazella_Munari_Morabito_2026_Formulations-1.pdf It uses gurobipy and supports P1 (classical) and P3 (optimal restocking). Itreads the same generated JSON consumed by the Rust stochastic extension. Aworking Gurobi license is required. No extra failure penalty is added.

title: Stochastic branch-and-cut versus branch-and-price
heading: Implemented mathematical components
text: Implemented mathematical components Directed binary routing arcs, exact customer degrees and upper fleet count,corresponding to equations (2)-(4),(6). The depot has source and sink copies. Expected-capacity inequalities (5). Every integer candidate is decomposedinto depot routes and disconnected cycles. Violated capacity/subtour rowsare added with cbLazy; this separation is complete on integer candidates.Zero-demand cycles also receive a subtour inequality. Nonnegative route-recourse variables and route Theta cuts, equation (31),generated at integer candidates. Each route is anchored at its minimumcustomer ID. Route recourse is computed by a separate Python Bellman evaluatorusing equations (9) or (11). Returned incumbents are independently replayed. Fractional capacity cuts through cbCut. Up to 12 customers all subsets arechecked. Larger cases use threshold components and pairs. This separator isnot CVRPSEP, and may miss fractional cuts; integer separation stillestablishes the intended integer model to Gurobi's tolerances. The paper specializes BC-Theta to an undirected formulation for symmetric costs.This implementation retains directed arcs, including both orientations and theirpotentially distinct recourse costs. It has a different relaxation/model size;it is not a reproduction of the reported C++/Gurobi 11.0.3/CVRPSEP run times.Approaches 1-3 (full EECR MIP and EECR separation) are not implemented here. Rounded Euclidean costs can violate triangle inequalities. For such inputs, asafe nonnegative per-route shift B = -n * min(0, min(c_i0+c_0j-c_ij)) (with asmall numerical margin) makes route recourse charges nonnegative for Theta cuts;B is subtracted on every depot departure. This preserves the originalobjective. The shift is zero for metric matrices. recourse_shift_per_routerecords it; no metric closure silently changes either solver's costs.

title: Stochastic branch-and-cut versus branch-and-price
heading: Running a baseline
text:
Running a baseline .venv/bin/python scripts/benchmarks/stochastic_branch_cut.py \
  instances/stochastic/generated_salavati_style/synthetic-n20-m2-r01-fr0.90.json \
  --policy p3 --seconds 30 --threads 1
 The output is JSON with status, incumbent, lower bound, gap, replayed objective,node/cut counts, Gurobi version and build/solve times. --log enables Gurobiconsole logging. The default clean JSON mode is used by the comparison runner.--no-fractional-cuts retains complete integer separation with a weaker search.Callback errors terminate the solve and are raised, never reported as optima.

title: Stochastic branch-and-cut versus branch-and-price
heading: Paired timing runs
text:
Paired timing runs Build before timing. The full generated grid needs 63-entry NG memory: cargo build --release --features clp,ng-memory-63 --example stochastic_instance
.venv/bin/python scripts/benchmarks/compare_stochastic.py \
  instances/stochastic/generated_salavati_style/synthetic-n20-m2-r01-fr0.90.json \
  --baldes-bin target/release/examples/stochastic_instance \
  --output results/stochastic-comparison-new \
  --policy p3 --seconds 30 --threads 1 --repetitions 3
 The destination must be new/empty. Each solver runs as a separate process onidentical input bytes. Run order alternates. Gurobi threads and Rayon/OMP/BLASthread environment variables share the requested count. Reports contain inputand binary/source hashes, solver versions, commands, build description, bounds,gaps, statuses and both process wall time and internal solve time. Gurobi's TimeLimit covers optimization after model construction; BALDES's limitalso includes node master construction. Read build/process times alongsideinternal solve times. Neither algorithm receives an external warm start; BALDESinternally seeds singleton columns and a greedy feasible route packing. BALDES's default runner work budgetis 1,000,000 labels per pricing call (--max-labels changes it). Work limits andincomplete pricing remain visible and do not certify optimality. Completedpricing columns/statistics, incumbents and relaxation bounds are retained.Column generation defaults to NG prepricing with eight-customer memories;--ng-size 0 on the runner disables this stage. Every emitted column is replayedwith true stochastic recourse; cyclic walks are excluded from incumbents.The reverse Bellman-vector fallback can be compared with the originaladapter using stochastic_instance ... --bidirectional.Pass --hgs-seconds 3 --hgs-seed 0 to the paired runner to enable themean-demand HGS warm start for BALDES. Its budget is included in BALDES'ssolve limit and the report records the option and route-validation counts. The runner marks comparable completed solves only if BOTH statuses are Optimal,and then checks objective agreement. An Error, timeout, work limit or absenceof an incumbent is not a speedup. results.json retains full records;summary.csv is the flat timing table. Synthetic instances cannot be comparedto original published best-known costs. Shared-host smoke timings are not ascalability study.

title: Stochastic branch-and-cut versus branch-and-price
heading: Verification
text:
Verification .venv/bin/python -m pytest scripts/tests/test_stochastic_branch_cut.py -q
 Tests compare against independent scenario-tree evaluation and exhaustive routepartitions, including both policies, asymmetric costs, negative recourse fromnonmetric distances, zero-demand subtours, fleet infeasibility and zero time.

title: Customer decomposition for HGS
heading: Customer decomposition for HGS
text:
Customer decomposition for HGS baldes hgs INSTANCE --dri enables a customer-based decomposition inspired byKerscher and Minner, Decompose-route-improve framework for solving large-scalevehicle routing problems with time windows (2025), papers/decomposition.pdf. cargo build --release --features clp --bin baldes
target/release/baldes hgs instances/Solomon/C101.txt --get-bks --dri --time 60 \
  --workers 4 --subproblem-customers 200 --dri-vicinity 3 --dri-neighbors 20 \
  --dri-fuzzy 0.8 \
  --solution-output /tmp/C101-dri.sol
 --get-bks or --initial-solution FILE supplies an incumbent. The incumbent isvalidated and saved first; it is returned if the cluster solution is infeasible,exceeds the fleet, or fails to improve it. Without an incumbent, failure of acluster or of the fleet check is reported as an error. --dri and --intensifyselect separate workflows. Only the distance objective is currently supported.For downloaded Solomon/Homberger BKSs, --get-bks selects truncated tenths;for a local BKS, select its metric explicitly with --rounding. The symmetric dissimilarity takes the minimum of the two directed values fromequations (11)–(14). Each directed value multiplies spatial distance by a factorfor time-window flexibility, waiting, and combined demand. It uses the instancetravel distance as its spatial measure; the paper's optional polar-angle term isnot included. When time windows or the depot horizon are infinite, the temporalfactor is set to one, an extension for CVRP. The implementation computes fuzzy memberships using equation (18) with κ = 2by default (--dri-kappa changes it),and updates medoids using the weighted dissimilarity objective (19). Customersare assigned to the highest-membership available cluster for routing. A sizecap bounds HGS subproblem memory without storing a full customer-pair matrix.The fuzzy membership matrix is capped at 50 million entries; increase thecluster-size limit if a finer partition would exceed that cap.Customers whose maximum membership exceeds --dri-fuzzy (default 0.8) areexcluded as source vertices in the cross-cluster search. Set it to 1 to considerevery customer. For bounded work, the implementation uses deterministic farthest-first medoidinitialization, samples at most 16 candidate medoids per cluster, and caps thenumber of clustering iterations (--dri-iterations, default 5). Capacity-bounded hard assignment can differfrom the largest-membership assignment in the paper. It does not implement thepaper's silhouette-based selection of cluster count. Negative dissimilarities,which can arise for windows extending beyond the depot horizon, are clamped tozero for membership calculations. Subproblems use the same depot, customer attributes, distance matrix and metricas the original instance. They are dispatched through a bounded CPU worker pool;when an incumbent is supplied, each cluster is seeded with its projected routesif that projection passes independent feasibility checks.the routing phase receives 80% of the time remaining after clustering by default(--dri-routing-fraction changes this share), and theremainder is used for improvement. The available per-cluster time is proportionalto its size and clipped by the shared routing deadline. Each cluster may use upto one vehicle per customer as in the paper, but the merged plan must respectthe original instance fleet. If the combined clusters exceed the fleet, theimprovement pass first favors moves that reduce the excess; only a completeplan that passes the original fleet bound can replace the incumbent. Failed orinfeasible subproblems never enter the merged plan. The improvement pass explores first-improving cross-cluster relocate, swap, androute-tail crossover moves, as well as single-route 2-opt. Candidate customers and clusters are restricted tonearest neighborhoods using the same similarity score. Every proposed completeplan is replayed against the original instance before acceptance; during fleetrepair only, the fleet limit is temporarily relaxed.Clustering, HGS setup, and individual local-search operations check deadlinescooperatively, so a single operation may overrun a time limit.

title: BKS-seeded HGS intensification
heading: BKS-seeded HGS intensification
text:
BKS-seeded HGS intensification The hgs command has optional BKS seeding and route-decomposition search.Ordinary baldes hgs INSTANCE retains its existing behavior. Build the CLI withcargo build --release --features clp --bin baldes. # Fetch the published BKS, populate HGS with it, then run ordinary HGS.
target/release/baldes hgs instances/cvrplib/A-n32-k5.vrp --get-bks --time 30

# Download the BKS and repeatedly intensify bounded subsets of its routes.
target/release/baldes hgs instances/cvrplib/A-n32-k5.vrp \
  --get-bks --intensify --time 300 \
  --workers 4 \
  --subproblem-routes 8 --subproblem-customers 300 --subproblem-time 2 \
  --threshold 0.001 --elite-size 8 --restart-after 30 \
  --solution-output /tmp/A-n32-k5-best.sol

# Reuse a local VRPTW seed, without accessing the network.
target/release/baldes hgs instances/Solomon/C101.txt \
  --initial-solution /tmp/C101.sol --intensify --time 60 \
  --rounding tenth \
  --solution-output /tmp/C101-best.sol --seed 7
 --get-bks uses the bundled standard-library Python downloader and requiresPython 3 plus internet access. It finds the instance name in the current CVRPLibCVRP/VRPTW catalogs and downloads its public route file. Lookup and downloaderrors stop the command. --initial-solution FILE supplies the same route formatlocally and conflicts with --get-bks. Seeds must cover every customer exactlyonce and be feasible for the selected metric, capacity, windows, and fleet.Consequently, a full-instance BKS cannot seed a --customers truncated instance.Route indices are BALDES customer indices, starting at 1, with depot 0 omitted. --intensify enables the outer search. Without an explicit seed, it first runsordinary HGS for up to 10% of the search time (at most five seconds); providinga BKS avoids full-instance HGS setup on large instances. Its steps are: --std-similarity optionally ranks route neighbors using the spatial–temporal–demand formula in equations 11–14 of Kerscher and Minner, using the instance'stravel distance as spatial cost. Infinite time windows use a neutral temporalfactor. This changes route selection; it does not implement the paper's customerclustering or its cross-cluster improvement phase.The separate --dri customer-clustering mode provides those phases. --barycenter instead ranks neighbors by Euclidean distance between the meancustomer coordinates of each route. It cannot be combined with--std-similarity. It uses coordinates even for explicit distance matrices, soit is useful only when those coordinates carry meaningful spatial information.Every fifth round still selects random neighbors, as in the default selector. Choose a random anchor route and nearby routes, measured by minimum distancefrom up to four anchor customers. Every fifth round chooses random neighbors.Neighborhoods expand from two routes during stagnation, bounded by--subproblem-routes and --subproblem-customers. Oversized routes are skipped. Build a sub-instance with the same depot, capacity, windows, service times,rounding, and explicit matrix entries. Seed its HGS population with theselected routes before generating other individuals. On alternating rounds,try a feasible random customer swap before seeding to escape the current plan. Solve with HGS, map customer indices back, and splice the new routes into theuntouched routes. Independently replay the entire proposal before using it. Accept proposals within --threshold times the current distance, coolinglinearly to zero over --restart-after stalled rounds. Save strict improvementsseparately, so a temporary deterioration never replaces the best solution. Maintain a bounded elite pool using differing directed arcs for diversity,ignoring route order. Restart from a randomly selected elite after stagnation. --workers N enables CPU parallelism with one HGS population and random generatorper worker. Each batch selects disjoint groups of complete routes from thesame solution snapshot. Results are collected in job order, mapped back andmerged once, then the combined proposal is replayed against the full originalinstance. A failed/infeasible subproblem leaves its original routes intact.Arbitrary fragments of one route are not optimized independently: their boundaryloads and arrival times would couple the subproblems. By default --batch-size 0 selects up to workers jobs per snapshot. Set a fixedpositive batch size to keep decomposition and search decisions identical acrossworker counts. For example, --batch-size 4 --workers 1 solves those four jobsserially, while --batch-size 4 --workers 4 solves them concurrently. Fewer jobsare dispatched when there are insufficient unassigned routes. --intensify-roundscounts subproblem jobs; acceptance and best-plan updates happen once per batch.Fixed seeds, batch size, and iteration budgets give reproducible results withoutper-job wall-time limits. Changing automatic batch width changes the searchtrajectory as well as throughput. Memory grows with simultaneous subproblems,approximately workers × subproblem_customers² for their distance structures. --objective auto uses distance for the current CVRPLib CVRP and VRPTW sets,matching their published conventions. --objective distance and--objective vehicles-distance select the objective explicitly.The latter rejects increases in vehicle count regardless of threshold and triesa reduced-fleet subproblem every fourth round. Inner HGS minimizes distance underthe selected fleet cap; it is not itself a lexicographic solver. Search is bounded by --time (default 60 seconds) and --intensify-rounds(default 1000). Each subproblem uses --subproblem-time and the ordinary HGS--nb-iter, --population-size, and --seed controls. Time limits are cooperative:a local-search operation or HGS setup can overrun a deadline. BKS downloadingprecedes the search budget. The initial plan and each strict improvement areatomically checkpointed when --solution-output FILE is supplied; this explicitlyreplaces that file. Parent directories must already exist. --json retains theexisting HGS result schema; generations counts inner genetic generations, andthe intensification summary (including batch and worker counts) is written to stderr.--subproblem-time 0 uses the iteration budget within each job. The outer deadlineis checked before dispatch and before a queued job begins; an executing fixed-workjob can overrun it. Positive per-job limits are reduced to the remaining budget. Control Default Meaning --threshold 0.001 Initial allowed relative distance deterioration --workers 1 Independent CPU HGS workers --batch-size 0 Jobs selected per snapshot; 0 uses worker count --elite-size 8 Maximum elite plans --elite-diversity 0.05 Minimum directed-arc Jaccard distance --restart-after 30 Stalled rounds before restart --subproblem-routes 8 Maximum routes per subproblem --subproblem-customers 300 Maximum customers per subproblem --subproblem-time 2 Seconds per HGS solve Decomposition controls require --intensify; seeding and extension flags requirethe hgs command. Seeded and intensified runs default to the instance's distanceconvention (CVRPLib integers for EUC_2D; unrounded for local Solomon files).With --get-bks, VRPTW instead uses truncated tenths, as specified by the currentCVRPLib Solomon/Homberger catalogs. --rounding is an explicit override. FileCost metadata is ignored and totals are recomputed.Current HGS capacity/demand storage requires integral demands and capacity fitting32-bit integers; the intensifier rejects incompatible inputs. The Rust APIs are run_hgs_seeded, intensify, and intensify_with_callback underbaldes::extensions::hgs; network access belongs to the CLI only. The callbackreceives the initial plan and each strict improvement, and may fail to stop searchwhen a checkpoint cannot be saved. A zero API time limit selects fixed-work search. The design is inspired by the route-subset HGS, threshold acceptance, elite-pool,and decompose-and-intensify descriptions in theCVRPLib updates.Those short reports do not specify complete algorithms or parameter values;this implementation makes its own choices as documented above. It includes noMIP subsolver, so it does not claim to reproduce the reported matheuristic or itsBKS improvements. Benchmark evidence is needed before making performance claims.

title: BKS-seeded HGS intensification
heading: Parallel benchmarks and GPU boundary
text:
Parallel benchmarks and GPU boundary Use fixed batches and fixed-work inner solves to compare the same computation: python3 scripts/benchmarks/benchmark_hgs_intensify.py \
  target/release/baldes instances/XL/XL-n2121-k186.vrp /tmp/XL-n2121-k186.sol \
  --workers 1 2 4 --batch-size 4 --rounds 24 --repeats 3 \
  --output results/hgs-workers.json
 The runner alternates worker-count order and checks that costs, routes, andgeneration counts match before reporting speedup. It records binary and seedhashes and refuses comparisons that did not complete the round budget. It usesan existing local seed, keeping downloading outside the measured runs. On October 28, 2026, the command above with 300 non-improving HGS iterations,population 12 and seed 7 completed 24 subproblem solves on XL-n2121-k186 usingan AMD Ryzen 9 9950X (16 cores, 32 logical CPUs). Three repetitions per workercount, using the release CLI, gave these median wall times: Workers Seconds Speedup over one worker 1 1.2601 1.00× 2 0.7202 1.75× 4 0.3838 3.28× All runs produced identical routes, cost (283,097), and generation counts. Thismeasures execution speed on a fixed search workload, not an improvement to thepublished BKS or a claim about time-to-improvement. Local raw measurements andbinary/seed hashes are in results/hgs-intensify-workers-20261028.json. No HGS GPU option is exposed. BALDES's existing cuda feature acceleratesp-step pricing, whose short-path enumeration is a different algorithm from HGSlocal search and genetic population management. Enabling it does not acceleratethis extension. A useful HGS GPU backend would need batched candidate-moveevaluation, CPU/GPU agreement on capacity/time-window feasibility and rounding,and a measured improvement in total solve time including transfers. No GPUspeedup is claimed. Independent CPU subproblems are the implemented parallelbackend; a GPU backend remains a separate, evidence-dependent extension.

title: BKS-seeded HGS intensification
heading: Validation
text:
Validation cargo fmt -p baldes --check
cargo clippy -p baldes --features clp --bin baldes --offline
cargo test -p baldes --features clp --offline --lib extensions::hgs::intensify
cargo test -p baldes --features clp --offline --test hgs_driver --test hgs_e2e --test cli hgs
python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p test_get_bks.py
 These checks passed: 12 algorithm unit tests, 12 focused CLI/HGS integrationtests and three downloader tests. Clippy reports existing repository warnings.Live --get-bks --intensify smoke runs preserved feasible BKSs for bothXL-n2121-k186 and C101. The default-feature library test build was alsoattempted; unrelated coupled-kernel/robust-PD tests require unavailablefeature-gated APIs and serde_json, so the successful library validation usedclp as shown above.

title: Stochastic demands and replenishment recourse
heading: Stochastic demands and replenishment recourse
text: Stochastic demands and replenishment recourse baldes::extensions::stochastic implements a CVRPSD extension based onTomazella, Munari and Morabito (2026), Pseudo-Compact Formulations andBranch-and-Cut Approaches for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem withStochastic Demands:https://optimization-online.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Tomazella_Munari_Morabito_2026_Formulations-1.pdf The model assumes independent finite discrete customer demands, integer vehiclecapacity, and demand realizations no larger than capacity. The depot is vertex0, and demand entry i belongs to customer i + 1. Costs may be asymmetric;callers should supply a matrix satisfying the triangle inequality. Constructionchecks matrix dimensions, nonnegative finite costs and zero diagonal, but doesnot check every triangle. A priori routes visit each assigned customer once,and their total expected demand cannot exceed capacity.

title: Stochastic demands and replenishment recourse
heading: Supported policies
text: Supported policies Policy::Classical implements P1, equation (9): replenish at the customer onfailure. If a customer empties the vehicle exactly, replenish before visitingthe next customer. No replenishment is charged after the last customer. Policy::OptimalRestocking implements P3, equation (11): at each remaining-loadstate choose whether to replenish before continuing or risk a customer failure. Problem::evaluate_route returns planned travel cost, expected recourse cost,their sum, and expected demand. It uses a backward dynamic program with Q + 1states and two vectors, taking O(route length * (Q+1) * support size) time.Probability sums within 1e-12 of one are normalized during Demand::new.Computation uses f64; no Monte Carlo sampling is involved.

title: Stochastic demands and replenishment recourse
heading: BALDES pricing and branch-and-price
text:
BALDES pricing and branch-and-price Problem::pricing_graph compiles to the ordinary BALDES physical graph, usingCoupledPlugin objective costs for expected recourse. Problem::price runspricing::Solver::price_phase_partial, including bucket labeling and optionalbidirectional joins. This prices the stochastic objective directly. The compiled graph also workswith RoutingContext::set_partitioning and the shared routing root master innumerical bound mode; regression tests cover its phase-I cost suppression andrestoration. The default search traverses the physical graph in reverse and carries aQ + 1 Bellman continuation vector. Each extension prepends one Bellmanoperator in O((Q+1) * support size), avoiding repeated prefix evaluation.For visited-customer subsets, componentwise continuation-vector dominanceis safe because Bellman expectation and minimum operators are monotone.Expected capacity is summed in customer-ID order, independently of route order. PricingOptions::bidirectional = true retains the original bidirectionaladapter: forward states retain their complete customer sequence and joinsreplay suffixes. Problem::pricing_graph also retains that original physicalorientation for shared-master integration. Generic completion bounds andreversal reuse remain disabled for cost plugins. Other cost plugins retainequality dominance unless they explicitly supply a cost-preserving dominancecontract. Large instances can still exhaust their label or time budget. The adapter supplies full elementarity through NG memory and supports at mostNG_MEMORY_CAPACITY customers: 15 by default, or 31/63 with ng-memory-31 /ng-memory-63. The route domain has at most n+1 arcs, including departure andreturn. A loose scalar mean-load window is only a necessary filter; canonicalforward resource replay enforces the expected-demand capacity condition.Cost magnitudes are checked against BALDES's route-pool sentinel; unusuallylarge units must be rescaled. Column generation starts with scalar NG-route prepricing when the customercount exceeds ColumnGenerationOptions::ng_size (default 8; zero disables it).For configured sizes above four, it first tries a four-customer neighborhood.If that stage neither finds a new improving route nor proves convergence, ittries the configured size, then falls back to stochastic Bellman pricing.Completed lower bounds are retained across stages; interrupted stages cannotcertify convergence by themselves.Problem::price_ng builds nearest-customer memories in the ordinary BALDESengine. Its first sweep retains 16 labels per bucket to find columns quickly;these heuristic sweeps supply no lower bound. A complete scalar sweep cansupply a bound. The master allocates at most 100,000 labels and two seconds perNG neighborhood, subject to the remaining pricing and solve time budgets.During the expected-cost phase, every eighth master iteration also starts eachNG neighborhood with a complete scalar sweep, bypassing the bounded heuristicsweeps. This gives bound-producing pricing a chance even when earlieriterations keep finding improving columns. The same label and time limitsapply; an interrupted sweep cannot certify convergence. The scalar objective charges travel plus each visited customer's minimumnonpositive preventive detour. Bellman recourse is bounded below by the sum ofthese customer charges, including on nonmetric matrices. Hence the minimum ofa completely priced NG relaxation is a global lower bound on true elementarystochastic reduced costs. It proves convergence only if it excludes improvingcolumns within tolerance. It does not generally equal true stochastic pricing. Cyclic walks never enter the master or an incumbent. Candidate elementary routesare evaluated with the full P1/P3 Bellman program, including all branch duals.When cycles obscure useful candidates, decremental state-space refinement addsthe repeated customer to memories along its cycle and reprices; every elementaryroute remains in the relaxation. Label/time exhaustion retains earlier validbounds but cannot turn an observed minimum into a bound. Primal pool/complementsearch runs during column generation, and feasible integer restricted-mastersnapshots can become incumbents even before pricing converges. Use stochastic_instance ... --ng-size 8 for this pipeline and --ng-size 0for the Bellman-only adapter. Problem::price itself retains its original exactstochastic pricing contract. The benchmark runner also accepts --ng-size. Master<M: LpMaster> builds exact customer-cover rows and an upper fleet row.Phase I uses artificial variables and zero physical/recourse costs; phase IIrestores total expected costs. Every seed/generated route is independentlyre-evaluated. Complete pricing is required before reporting LP convergence orphase-I infeasibility. Restricted-pool objectives are never reported as globalbounds. Problem::solve_with accepts a factory for fresh LP backends. Its arcbranch-and-price driver branches on fractional directed arc flows: zero removesthe arc from subsequent pricing; one adds a required-arc equality row whosedual enters pricing. Each child performs two-phase column generation. Solvingonly an integer restricted route pool is not used to establish optimality.Problem::solve is the Clp convenience wrapper, available with features=clp: use baldes::extensions::stochastic::{Policy, SolveOptions};
let answer = problem.solve(Policy::OptimalRestocking, 3, SolveOptions::default())?;
 An optional HGS warm start searches a deterministic CVRP with the same costmatrix and mean customer demands. HGS uses integer loads, so means are scaledand rounded down for the heuristic. Every candidate route is independentlychecked for elementarity and the original expected-capacity constraint, thenevaluated with the selected stochastic recourse policy before entering thecolumn pool. A complete HGS plan becomes an incumbent only if it covers eachcustomer once, respects the fleet limit, and all its routes pass validation.HGS candidates do not establish bounds or optimality. Its time budget is partof the overall solve time; initialization can overrun the requested limit. Set SolveOptions::hgs_warm_start to Some(HgsWarmStart { time_limit, seed }).The result's hgs_warm_start summary reports accepted and rejected candidatecounts and whether the HGS plan passed validation. For generated instances: cargo run --release --features clp,ng-memory-63 --example stochastic_instance -- \
  instances/stochastic/generated_salavati_style/synthetic-n20-m2-r01-fr0.90.json \
  --solve --seconds 30 --hgs-seconds 3 --hgs-seed 0 --json
 Run the complete example: cargo run -p baldes --features clp --example stochastic
 SolveStatus::Optimal means the branch-and-price tree is exhausted under theconfigured floating-point tolerances. It is not an outward-rounded arithmeticcertificate. Node, iteration, pricing-work, and time limits retain an incompletestatus. Completed routes and labeling statistics survive pricing interruptions;partial routes can improve the restricted master but never establish convergence.Best-fit starts with several nearest-neighbor/shuffled orders, travel 2-opt,and a bounded exact-cover/complement search over known columns provide feasible incumbents without waiting for complete pricing.Heuristic packing failure does not prove infeasibility. Stopped solves return the best incumbent found and a numerical lower bound.The initial degree relaxation accounts for negative recourse on nonmetricmatrices. A hop-bounded shortest-walk relaxation supplies a global reduced-costlower bound even after incomplete pricing; shifting the fleet dual by itsnegative part gives a valid full-master bound. Open nodes retain the best suchbound or their inherited bound. PricingResult::minimum_reduced_cost is absentafter incomplete pricing; lower_bound is the separate relaxation bound.Generic directedplugin certification returns unknown for cost-bearing plugins, preventing afeasibility-only proof from silently assigning zero recourse cost.

title: Stochastic demands and replenishment recourse
heading: Exact tiny-instance baseline
text: Exact tiny-instance baseline Problem::solve_tiny enumerates elementary route orders, retains the cheapestorder for each customer subset, and solves the resulting set-partitioning problemby subset dynamic programming. max_vehicles is an upper limit, not an equality.All customers, including zero-demand customers, must be assigned. This deliberately supports at most nine customers. route_budget bounds thenumber of evaluated routes; exceeding it returns an error, not a feasible answeror an optimality certificate. Ok(None) means that exhaustive search proved fleetinfeasibility. An empty customer set has a zero-cost solution. Optimality is withrespect to the supplied distributions and ordinary floating-point comparisons.

title: Stochastic demands and replenishment recourse
heading: Remaining boundaries
text:
Remaining boundaries The paper's arc-based MIP, rule-based and penalty recourse policies, Pythonbindings, stronger stochastic dominance, specialized fast joins, and stochasticcut separation are not implemented. The branch-and-price driver currently addsarc branch rows and uses no additional cutting planes. Verification: cargo test -p baldes --features clp --test stochastic --test stochastic_pricing
 Tests cover hand-calculated costs, comparison against a separate scenario tree,BALDES pricing against exhaustive route orders in both directions, phase-I costsuppression, forbidden/required arc handling, full-route LP comparisons, integeroptima against the tiny oracle, a fractional root requiring branching, andincomplete-work statuses.
